💡 Key Takeaways
  • Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment Darragh O’Brien has last week revealed that more than 300,000 home energy upgrades have been completed with government support since 2019.
  • Since 2019, SEAI (Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland) schemes have provided over €2 billion for communities and households – including the aforementioned home energy improvements.
  • It has been revealed that momentum is growing, following the introduction of fresh measures, higher grants, and enhanced eligibility declared in January and again in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment Darragh O’Brien has last week revealed that more than 300,000 home energy upgrades have been completed with government support since 2019. The more than 300,000 energy upgrades have benefitted well over a quarter of a million individual houses (271,000). Over 42,000 of these were vulnerable, energy-poor households that benefitted from fully-funded (free) energy upgrades. All of these homes are now warmer and healthier, with lower energy bills. On this journey, more than 115,000 of these homes achieved a B2 energy rating or better. Over 22,000 heat pumps were installed.

Since 2019, SEAI (Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland) schemes have provided over €2 billion for communities and households – including the aforementioned home energy improvements. Looking across all schemes (if expenditure on Local Authority upgrades by the Department of Housing is included) the spend (in monetary terms) on vulnerable households and those at risk of energy poverty each year now accounts for more than 60% of the overall spend.

It has been revealed that momentum is growing, following the introduction of fresh measures, higher grants, and enhanced eligibility declared in January and again in October. The changes included the introduction of grants for windows and doors, increased grant for heat pumps, higher grants for certain Department of Social Protection payment recipients, as well as new supports for certain landlords.

So far this year, SEAI has received more than 120,000 applications, more than double the volume at the same point last year.

Commenting on this milestone, Minister O’Brien said:.

Sources indicate that “I am delighted that we have achieved this really significant milestone, whereby we have now completed more than 300,000 home energy upgrades. The recently enhanced measures to the home energy upgrade schemes are helping to deliver meaningful and long-lasting reductions in energy costs for households and businesses right across the country. Depending on the measure installed and the characteristics of the property, households could benefit from savings of up to nearly €900 per year. These grants are on top of the existing supports for energy upgrades, including insulation, window and door replacements and heat pumps. When installed as part of whole home upgrade, homeowners can save over €1,100 per year on their energy bills.

“Importantly, more than 42,000 households have benefited from fully funded upgrades through the warmer homes scheme, ensuring that those most in need of energy supports are not left behind in the transition to a cleaner more sustainable energy future. There are a number of recently enhanced measures to support households at risk of energy poverty, medically vulnerable customers, lower-income homeowners and renters. These will help to ensure that those who need support most can access the benefits of lower energy bills and warmer healthier homes.

“These enhanced measures, developed through the work of the National Energy Affordability Taskforce which I chair, form part of the Government’s broader efforts to improve energy affordability, strengthen energy security and support the transition to a cleaner energy future. Budget 2027 allocated a record capital allocation of over €650 million for SEAI home and community energy upgrades, including more solar PV, new battery grants and a boiler scrappage scheme. The forthcoming Energy Affordability Action Strategy, which I will bring to Government in the coming weeks, will set out a roadmap for improving energy affordability for households and businesses.”.

CEO of the SEAI (Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland), William Walsh, said:.

According to recent reports, “Behind these figures are people and families, in warmer, more comfortable homes, with more security over their energy bills. There is real momentum behind this work now. Every year we help more and more people, and with energy costs on the minds of many, especially at this time of year, I’d really encourage anyone thinking of upgrading to get in touch with us at SEAI, or check out our website www.seai.ie to see how to get started.

“Thanks to record Government support, the grants available have never been more generous – there really is an option for everyone now, regardless of where you’re starting out from or what your budget is.”.

The recently enhanced measures include: solar PV and battery are now offered as standard under fully-funded Warmer Homes Scheme; more generous grants for solar, attic and cavity insulation for certain Department of Social Protection recipients and homes in HAP, RAS, and RASP tenancies; more favourable eligibility criteria for solar PV and solar thermal; a fossil fuel boiler scrappage support scheme; a home battery energy storage grant; and enhanced supports for businesses that will save thousands in energy costs.

For more information on home and business energy supports see the SEAI website: https://www.seai.ie.

News release from the Government of Ireland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that NAED Energy Holding Inc. (NAED) just published the rating of PV-1, its production line for T2X perovskite/silicon heterojunction tandem solar cells. Each PV-1 line is rated at 16,000 G12 half-cut wafers per hour: 400 wafers every 90-second index, a rate set by the line’s inline PVD tool (ITO-1). The line’s four PECVD modules are built for a faster 76-second index, about 18,950 wafers per hour.

At NAED’s planning basis—85% availability, 97.5% yield, and the T2X programme target of 30% cell efficiency—one PV-1 line produces about 116 million cells and 0.77 GW of tandem cells a year. NAED’s six-line site, at 96,000 wafers per hour, has a rated capacity of about 4.6 GW a year.

Throughput and capacity in this release are rated values, and cell efficiency is modelled. NAED will publish measured throughput, yield, and efficiency, with their test basis, as results are logged. For all technical information on PV-1 and the T2X cell, contact cto.fusion@naedcorp.com.

According to recent reports, the 34.4% figure is NAED’s modelled T2X cell (Voc 1.969 V, Jsc 20.18 mA/cm², fill factor 0.867, 217.2 cm² half-cell). For context, the highest published efficiencies for perovskite/silicon tandem cells of this size are in the 32–33% range, including Maxwell’s certified 32.38% on a G12 half-cell reported in January 2026. NAED’s planning figures use the 30% programme target.

According to recent reports, the comparisons below are rate-to-rate. A PV-1 figure describes a complete integrated line, while some benchmarks describe a single tool; supplier figures are the suppliers’ own published ratings.

According to recent reports, A single PV-1 line runs at or above the rate of leading single deposition tools while carrying the full tandem process — wet clean, PECVD, PVD, top-cell deposition, printing and test — in one line. Six lines carry the output of about three large HJT lines or seven to eight commercial tandem lines.

According to recent reports, one year of output from the six-line site is enough cells for about 7.7 million 600-watt panels, which would generate roughly enough electricity for about 650,000 U.S. homes for a year (17% capacity factor, 10,500 kWh per home; typical U.S. values, not site data). Panels keep generating for 25–30 years, so each year of production adds to that total.

News from NAED Energy Holding Inc.

SolarEdge unveils U.S.-made optimizer for C&I solar

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SolarEdge’s newly introduced Duo Power Optimizer promises to simplify commercial and industrial solar installations with 50% fewer optimizer units, independent module-level power tracking, and enhanced safety features.
  • It has been revealed that the commercial and industrial (C&I) solar market is getting a latest hardware option aimed at making installations simpler without sacrificing system performance.
  • In a recent development, confirmed November 16 ahead of RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, the new product introduces a 2:1 architecture that allows one optimizer to connect two solar modules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SolarEdge’s newly introduced Duo Power Optimizer promises to simplify commercial and industrial solar installations with 50% fewer optimizer units, independent module-level power tracking, and enhanced safety features.

It has been revealed that the commercial and industrial (C&I) solar market is getting a latest hardware option aimed at making installations simpler without sacrificing system performance. SolarEdge Technologies has unveiled its new Duo Power Optimizer, a U.S.-manufactured solution designed to deliver module-level energy harvesting and monitoring while cutting the number of power optimizers in half.

In a recent development, confirmed November 16 ahead of RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, the new product introduces a 2:1 architecture that allows one optimizer to connect two solar modules. Notably, each module retains its own independent maximum power point tracker (MPPT), which preserves the module-level performance benefits associated with the traditional one-to-one optimizer configurations.

For developers, EPCs and installers managing large-scale rooftop and distributed generation projects, the value here lies in fewer components to purchase, wire and install, with no trade-off in module-level optimization.

Simplifying installation without sacrificing performance.

SolarEdge’s optimization tech addresses the challenge of conventional string inverter systems, which is that an underperforming module can affect the output of an entire string. But by allowing each module to operate independently, the system limits the impact of shading, degradation or performance differences between panels.

The Duo brings demonstrates that capability in a two-module configuration. By reducing the number of optimizers by 50% compared with one-to-one designs, SolarEdge is targeting an opportunity to streamline balance-of-system requirements and reduce the installation labor.

It has been revealed that solarEdge’s U.S.-made Duo Power Optimizer connects two solar modules while maintaining independent module-level power tracking for commercial and industrial solar installations. Credit: SolarEdge.

The hardware also incorporates design changes intended to improve jobsite efficiency. Each optimizer features two input pairs: a shorter connection for the nearest module and a pre-extended connection for the adjacent module. The arrangement reduces excess wiring and eliminates the need for field-made jumpers.

The configuration also accommodates modules with different orientations, making it particularly relevant for east-west and dual-tilt racking applications.

Safety moves closer to the module.

Beyond installation efficiency, SolarEdge is emphasizing electrical safety as a central feature of the fresh product.

The Duo extends the tech giant’s Sense Connect technology to its input and output connectors, monitoring connector temperatures to identify developing issues before they potentially escalate into overheating or electrical arcs.

It has been revealed that also, the optimizer introduces what SolarEdge describes as an industry-first approach to arc fault detection: every optimizer acts as an individual arc sensor. Rather than relying exclusively on detection at the inverter, the system distributes monitoring throughout the array, allowing potential arc faults to be identified closer to their source.

Industry observers note that solarEdge claims the technology provides coverage across strings with up to 3,280 feet of total cable length between the inverter and optimizer. It can also help pinpoint problems to the optimizer area, potentially making troubleshooting and maintenance more efficient.

Manufactured at SolarEdge’s Florida facility, the Duo is designed to meet U.S. Domestic Content and Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) requirements, according to the company. SolarEdge states its domestic-content eligibility levels are consistent with those of its previous U.S.-manufactured power optimizers, subject to applicable tax guidance and project-specific requirements.

A practical play for the C&I market.

For SolarEdge, the Duo represents an effort to combine three priorities that are becoming more and more notable in commercial solar: installation efficiency, system-level safety, and domestic manufacturing.

Industry observers note that the technology does not fundamentally change the value proposition of module-level optimization. Instead, it looks to make that architecture more economical and easier to deploy at scale.

SolarEdge will showcase the Duo Power Optimizer at RE+ 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Washington, DC — Today and tomorrow, environmental and public health experts, alongside community advocates, will testify during a virtual public hearing to the dangers and risks posed by the Trump administration’s proposed rollback of long-awaited methane pollution standards finalized in 2024.
  • Soon after taking office in 2025, the Trump EPA suspended the implementation of key provisions from the Biden-era standards, delaying their enforcement by up to 18 months despite no widespread evidence of compliance difficulties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sierra Club staff & members highlight dangers of rolling back methane pollution standards.

Washington, DC — Today and tomorrow, environmental and public health experts, alongside community advocates, will testify during a virtual public hearing to the dangers and risks posed by the Trump administration’s proposed rollback of long-awaited methane pollution standards finalized in 2024. The hearing is part of a broader public comment period in reaction to the Environmental Protection Agency’s blueprint to reverse key components of the landmark safeguards aimed at reducing methane, and associated pollution, from both fresh and existing oil and gas equipment.

Soon after taking office in 2025, the Trump EPA suspended the implementation of key provisions from the Biden-era standards, delaying their enforcement by up to 18 months despite no widespread evidence of compliance difficulties. Now, this rollback would permanently eliminate some of the rule’s most notable safeguards, including its ban on routine flaring at oil wells and its program to leverage third-party monitoring data to identify and stop particularly large methane releases known as super-emitter events.

The proposal would also shield low-producing wells from leak monitoring requirements and other key safeguards, despite consistent evidence showing that such wells do not pollute less than higher-producing wells. Nearly one in ten people in the U.S. live in a county with over a thousand low-producing wells. These sources represent nearly half of the sector’s methane emissions and are primarily owned by large, well-resourced and highly profitable corporations.

Sierra Club experts and members will be among many testifying against the rollback.

In reaction, Sierra Club staff providing testimony released the following statements:.

Andres Restrepo, Sierra Club Senior Attorney noted: “EPA’s authority and obligation under the Clean Air Act to control methane emissions from the oil and gas sector has long been settled law, and the safeguards that the Biden Administration put into place in 2024 rely on cost-effective, widely available technologies and practices that the industry itself has used for years. The Trump Administration’s current proposal to strip the 2024 rule for parts and leave a rump regulation in place has support in neither the law nor the facts. The agency is attempting to manufacture sham justifications to mask what is nothing more than the giveaway that Donald Trump openly promised to oil and gas executives in exchange for supporting his campaign. Sierra Club will use every resource at its disposal to fight back against this betrayal of our families and communities.”.

Industry observers note that cyrus Reed, Legislative and Conservation Director of Sierra Club’s Lone Star Chapter, stated: “No state produces more oil and gas than Texas, and no state has more to gain from strong methane regulations than our state. We already have poor air quality from ozone pollution, particulate matter and other pollutants like hydrogen sulfide, and rolling back the methane standards will only make matters worse. Texas voters went to the polls in record numbers for a non-presidential election, and for the most part, voted for change, in largely because of anger over rising prices, but also due to a politics that often favor entrenched wealthy interests. This rollback proposal does not respond to this call for change, but instead proposes to let bad corporate actors off the hook and increase pollution that leads to higher energy prices, harms our health, and supercharges climate disruption.”.

Antoinette Reyes, Permian Basin Organizer, Sierra Club Rio Grande Chapter, said: “As the federal government moves to weaken methane protections, Upcoming Mexico is working to strengthen its own. But pollution doesn’t stop at state lines, and neither should our commitment to protecting communities. Families in the Permian Basin already face industrial air pollution, from odors and poor visibility to respiratory health concerns. Every preventable methane leak wastes a valuable energy resource, potential tax revenue, and affects the quality of the air we breathe. Proven technology exists to reduce these emissions. State action alone cannot fill the gap left by federal rollbacks. We need strong protections at every level to safeguard our health, climate, and communities.”.

Sources indicate that sarah Corcoran, Deputy Director of the Sierra Club Pennsylvania Chapter, mentioned: “Pennsylvania is one of the leading states in the nation for fracked gas infrastructure. We are also one of the states with the highest pediatric asthma and cancer rates — but those numbers are increasing across the nation. The Trump Administration is not doing anyone any favors by reducing these regulations, not the industry, not the environment and not the American people who will feel the health impacts of these decisions for years to come. Policies that reduce methane waste, such as controls on flaring, quicker response times, transparent communications with impacted residents and more frequent testing are commonsense and cost effective. We need stronger protections in place for methane, not looser.”.

Recent findings suggest that methane is a potent greenhouse gas that has more than 80 times the power of carbon dioxide over a 20-year period, driving approximately one-third of the warming our planet has experienced to date. Each year, the U.S. oil and gas sector emits large amounts of methane into our atmosphere. Methane is emitted from oil and gas sources alongside other damaging pollutants, such as smog- and soot-forming volatile organic compounds and air toxins like benzene and formaldehyde, human carcinogens.

According to EPA’s analysis, the 2024 standards are projected to avoid 58 million tons of methane through 2038, as well as 16 million tons of volatile organic compounds and 590,000 tons of air toxins.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • today rolled out upcoming generative artificial intelligence models and updates to Foundry, the company’s unified enterprise platform that helps developers and organizations ground, test and deploy AI applications and autonomous agents.
  • Updates to Foundry IQ, part of Microsoft IQ, now provide an enterprise knowledge graph out of the box, delivering a full estate of unstructured and application data to provide rich context for building applications and delivering on essential use cases.
  • Microsoft also said Foundry now uses existing transparency and observability capabilities to help customers create learning loops.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:05 EST / NOVEMBER 17 2026.

Microsoft Corp. today rolled out upcoming generative artificial intelligence models and updates to Foundry, the company’s unified enterprise platform that helps developers and organizations ground, test and deploy AI applications and autonomous agents.

Updates to Foundry IQ, part of Microsoft IQ, now provide an enterprise knowledge graph out of the box, delivering a full estate of unstructured and application data to provide rich context for building applications and delivering on essential use cases.

Microsoft also said Foundry now uses existing transparency and observability capabilities to help customers create learning loops. Internal evaluations allow autonomous agents to establish baselines for quality, safety, latency and cost, enabling continuous behavioral improvements.

Sources indicate that this includes human annotations, now in preview, that allow experts to rate and comment on agent traces based on business judgment. It feeds back into an improvement loop. It’s combined with optimization tests against evaluations and comparisons against real-world results. Foundry now also has upcoming capabilities to adapt to supported models with organizational data to apply reinforcement learning while Foundry runs compute.

Each improvement becomes the next baseline and teams can continue measuring results and test changes, allowing them to improve quality.

In a recent development, microsoft today revealed Decision-1.1 is generally available. It’s a fast, cost-effective model designed to make reliable decisions in software at scale.

The generative AI model can make decisions dynamically at low cost, rather than relying on hard-coded rules, while offering superior decision-making capabilities compared with large language models. LLMs spend a lot of time making decisions in routing, classification, prioritization, verification and workflow control by “thinking it through,” which is unnecessary. Decision models are designed to reach answers quickly within constrained definitions and provide calibrated confidence scores, allowing applications to defer when uncertainty is high.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced model builds on the previous generation, Microsoft-Decision-1, released in October. The new model delivers a significant improvement in intelligence and speed at a competitive price.

The Efficacy of Broad Match + Audiences Strategy in Real Estate

📅 06 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtybiznews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When considering digital marketing strategies, the realm of real estate is no different from any other industry.
  • Industry observers note that the real estate sector thrives on the availability of a vast array of properties, each with a unique combination of attributes that appeal to different prospective buyers.
  • Industry observers note that the broad match feature in Google AdWords is a type of keyword match that allows your ads to show whenever someone searches for that keyword or a related phrase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When considering digital marketing strategies, the realm of real estate is no different from any other industry. The key objective remains the same - reaching the target audience with an impactful, compelling message that can inspire action. An increasingly popular approach adopted by real estate agents is the broad match + audiences strategy. This approach leverages the power of Google AdWords' broad match feature and combines it with audience targeting to attain superior marketing results.

Industry observers note that the real estate sector thrives on the availability of a vast array of properties, each with a unique combination of attributes that appeal to different prospective buyers. Recognizing this immense diversity and matching it with the correct buyer is a daunting challenge that real estate agents constantly grapple with. This is where the broad match + audiences strategy steps in, optimizing the process by expanding reach while ensuring relevance.

Industry observers note that the broad match feature in Google AdWords is a type of keyword match that allows your ads to show whenever someone searches for that keyword or a related phrase. It can include searches that are misspellings, synonyms, related searches, and other relevant variations.

With the broad match feature, you're casting a wide net over an extensive range of search queries. It brings with it the advantage of gaining visibility across a wider spectrum of potential buyers who might not use the exact keywords that you've selected for your campaign.

Sources indicate that in the real estate industry, property attributes can be incredibly diverse, ranging from "3-bedroom apartments in New York City" to "colonial-style houses with large gardens in Austin". By leveraging the broad match feature, agents can reach potential clients who use various search terms that directly or indirectly relate to their listing.

Audience targeting is a method used in digital marketing to segment audiences based on specific criteria like demographics, interests, buying behavior, etc. Google AdWords allows you to target your ads to specific audiences, ensuring they are seen by those who are most likely to be interested in your offerings.

According to recent reports, in the context of real estate, audience targeting can be a game-changer. For instance, if an agent specializes in selling luxury homes, they can target audiences with high-income levels and a demonstrated interest in luxury living. Alternatively, if an agent focuses on properties suitable for first-time buyers, they can target younger audiences who have recently started searching for homes.

It has been revealed that the marriage of broad match keywords with audience targeting may seem counter-intuitive at first, considering one aims at breadth and the other at specificity. However, the combination forms a robust strategy that takes the best of both worlds - wide reach and precise targeting.

The broad match feature ensures a wide reach, allowing real estate agents to surface their listings to a large number of prospective clients. But, broad match alone can lead to high impression counts with low conversion rates as the ads may be presented to irrelevant audiences. This is where audience targeting steps in to bring precision.

When used in conjunction, the broad match feature ensures that your ads reach a wide array of searchers, while audience targeting ensures these ads are shown to a specific subset of this wide audience who are most likely to be interested in your property listings.

This synergistic approach allows real estate agents to achieve two key objectives:.

It has been revealed that in the dynamic and competitive world of real estate, digital marketing strategies need to be both comprehensive and precise. The broad match + audiences strategy does precisely that - it maximizes the reach of property listings while maintaining relevance to the audience. As such, it is not surprising that this strategy is being widely adopted by savvy real estate agents seeking to gain a competitive edge in the digital realm. The power of a wide-reaching yet finely tuned marketing strategy should not be underestimated in a market as diverse and competitive as real estate.

  • In a recent development, dominion and NextEra have failed to show that customer benefits, not shareholders profits, were a motivating factor for the merger.
  • If approved, the new utility would service 10 million customers across the Southeastern United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Richmond, Virginia — Tomorrow, November 17, the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) will begin the evidentiary hearing for NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy’s merger proposal, which would create the nation’s largest ever utility. Sierra Club filed expert testimony last month urging the SCC to reject the merger given the way it threatens the Virginia’s Clean Economy Act (VCEA) and violates the Utility Transfers Act, posing a significant risk to energy affordability for Virginia families.

In a recent development, dominion and NextEra have failed to show that customer benefits, not shareholders profits, were a motivating factor for the merger. The utilities have offered a temporary $10 per month bill credit to Virginia customers for four years to help cover any additional costs. However, the credit does not so much as cover the $30 per month Virginia families expect to pay in anticipated bill increases to maintain fossil fuel plants and meet AI data centers demand in 2027 alone.

If approved, the new utility would service 10 million customers across the Southeastern United States. Allied groups will rally outside the SCC tomorrow for the Stop the NextEra Takeover: Final Rally at the SCC.

Ahead of tomorrow’s hearing, Connor Kish, Director of the Sierra Club Virginia Chapter, issued the following statement:.

“Throughout November, Virginians have shown up in droves at public hearings to oppose Dominion and NextEra’s proposed merger. Utility customers, independent policy experts, and local leaders have cited sky-high energy bills, AI data center demand, and abandoned climate goals as reasons to be wary of Dominion and NextEra’s bid to become the country’s largest ever utility.

“Meanwhile, the utilities have yet to prove the merger will result in any tangible benefits for customers. Their offer of a temporary $10 monthly bill credit for customers is nothing in comparison to the $10 billion in profits shareholders are anticipated to receive should the SCC approve the merger. Virginia deserves utilities that prioritize families, not shareholders out for bonuses. To keep the lights on and make bills affordable, it’s critical that SCC fulfill its duty to the public and reject the merger.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs.
  • It has been revealed that heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes.
  • “Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

It has been revealed that heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

“Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

Sources indicate that traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the problem by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

HYDAC’s newly introduced “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

Sources indicate that the importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

In a recent development, field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

Industry observers note that after initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later indicated turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another important advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

“What operators are increasingly recognizing is that small improvements in thermal management can create meaningful gains in turbine reliability, maintenance efficiency, and long-term asset performance,” said Erickson. “The field data we’re seeing continues to validate the value of designing cooling systems specifically for real-world wind operating environments.”.

It has been revealed that more recently, long-term SCADA data from Mitsubishi platforms further validated the technology’s performance. After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

Sources indicate that for wind asset owners and service providers, the implications are substantial: Improved thermal management supports healthier oil viscosity, more stable gearbox operation, and potentially longer component life. At the same time, reduced cleaning frequency and fewer cooling-related service events translate directly into lower operational expenditures and increased turbine availability.

Recent findings suggest that as the industry continues to prioritize lifecycle optimization and energy production efficiency, innovative subsystem upgrades such as advanced heat exchanger technology are becoming increasingly valuable. Rather than waiting for costly failures or performance degradation, operators are seeking practical retrofit solutions that improve reliability without requiring major system redesigns.

It has been revealed that “Effective thermal management is critical to protecting gearbox health and maintaining oil performance over time. By addressing one of the most common causes of cooling degradation — debris accumulation — operators can improve uptime while reducing unnecessary maintenance interventions,” said HYDAC’s Erickson.

It has been revealed that for wind stakeholders evaluating ways to improve gearbox reliability, reduce maintenance exposure, and enhance turbine performance, cooling system optimization deserves greater attention. Proven retrofit technologies like advanced heat exchanger designs can offer a practical path toward improved uptime and operational efficiency without requiring major system overhauls.

Industry observers note that as fleets age and performance expectations continue to rise, collaboration between operators, service providers, and technology partners will be essential to building more resilient wind assets for the future. Now is the time to evaluate whether existing cooling systems are supporting — or limiting — long-term turbine reliability goals.

“HYDAC’s goal is to help wind owners and service providers solve practical operational challenges in ways that create long-term value across the entire asset lifecycle. Innovations like the Square Wave heat exchanger are designed to improve reliability, simplify maintenance, and support greater energy production over time.”.

Don’t let cooling system limitations impact turbine performance.

Proactive cooling optimization can help operators reduce maintenance exposure, protect critical drivetrain components, and maximize energy production across the asset lifecycle.   • For some reason, Trump is obsessed with trying to bring the United States backward by several decades.
  • According to recent reports, the Sierra Club updates us on this latest absurdity: “On Friday, November 13, the Trump Department of Energy issued yet another illegal ’emergency’ order, forcing the J.H.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when a power plant gets old enough and is inefficient and expensive, it should be shut down. When it’s time to close, it’s time to close. As we’ve learned about the severe health costs and climate costs of old coal power plants, that’s even more obviously the case with them. But not for Donald Trump.

For some reason, Trump is obsessed with trying to bring the United States backward by several decades. That means, among other things, that he hates solar and wind power and he wants coal to rule again. Since coal power has become uncompetitive, he’s been using wacky logic to force old coal power plants to stay open while also paying off wind power companies to the tune of billions of dollars to not turn on power plants they’ve built. Trump’s logic with the coal plants is that we are in an energy emergency and urgently need the power — but aside from that being ridiculous, how can he then justify going and blocking wind and solar power plants from being finished and connected to the grid?

According to recent reports, the Sierra Club updates us on this latest absurdity: “On Friday, November 13, the Trump Department of Energy issued yet another illegal ’emergency’ order, forcing the J.H. Campbell power plant to remain online. The Department issued that order despite the D.C. Circuit court ‘s decision in September rejecting the Department’s claim to ‘vast, top-down emergency power to pick its favorite generators to run at all costs.’.

Industry observers note that “This would be the power plant’s seventh order from the administration, despite no evidence that the plant has ever been needed to avoid a grid emergency or has ever prevented power outages. The extension order continues to cost families in the midwest region more than $600,000 per day to keep the old and toxic coal plant online.

“According to the Sierra Club’s Burning Money tracker, the Trump administration’s unlawful extensions have cost Americans well over half a billion dollars. Of that, over $326 million comes from J.H. Campbell based on reported utility cost recovery filings for portions of the facility’s extension orders.”.

Half a billion dollars! At a time when Americans are struggling with high costs, Trump has forced expensive old coal power plants to keep running and has thus cost us half a billion dollars. And one wonders how a gigantic llue tsunami took over the country. Here’s more:.

“At a time when prices are soaring and Americans are struggling to make ends meet, the Trump administration’s decision to problem yet another illegal and expensive extension is punishing,” said Sierra Club Senior Advisor Jessi Eidbo. “Families cannot afford to pay even more for electricity, especially when what they are paying for is a dated, defunct, deadly fossil fuel plant. The courts have already made it clear that these orders are illegal—ruling specifically that this very facility’s first order was not justified—but instead of listening to the courts and reason, Trump’s DOE marches ahead driving up costs to feed the coal industry. We will continue to challenge the administration until they stop.”.

“Michiganders are growing tired of Trump’s attempts to keep them reliant on the dirty, expensive fossil fuel industry,” added Elayne Coleman, Sierra Club Michigan Chapter Director. “Michiganders showed up in droves on Election Day to reject this administration and seek something better. We look forward to working with our upcoming leaders in Lansing and Washington DC, to expand clean, renewable energy in Michigan.” We’ll see. It’ll be hard to get any support for renewable energy through the White House as long as Trump lives there. We’ll see.

#30138. Nvidia at SC26: Agents are the fresh scientists, and they need a lab

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2003 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Siliconangle ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia at SC26: Agents are the fresh scientists, and they need a lab

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2003 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GUEST COLUMN by Zeus Kerravala.
  • Industry observers note that for most of its history, the high-performance computing market measured progress the same way: how fast a machine could solve a fixed problem.
  • But this week, Nvidia argued that speed at solving a single problem is no longer the right way to measure leadership.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:27 EST / NOVEMBER 17 2026.

GUEST COLUMN by Zeus Kerravala.

Industry observers note that for most of its history, the high-performance computing market measured progress the same way: how fast a machine could solve a fixed problem. Rankings rose, a new system took the top spot, and the cycle started over. Raw performance remains the foundation of scientific computing, and Nvidia Corp. brought plenty of it to SC26.

But this week, Nvidia argued that speed at solving a single problem is no longer the right way to measure leadership. An equally important question now is how many times a researcher can go from hypothesis to result in a day, and what happens when the “researcher” is an artificial intelligence agent that never sleeps.

Sources indicate that that idea ties together Nvidia’s bevy of announcements at the show. The manufacturer introduced open science models, a CPU-only supercomputing rack, a latest HPC-specific GPU, a batch of CUDA-X libraries, quantum integration for the Slurm workload manager, a quantum co-design platform with IBM and Fermilab, and a co-packaged optics deployment at Lambda. It also marked CUDA’s 20th birthday.

Taken individually, these announcements look like a typical supercomputing show news payload. Taken together, they describe a stack built for a different user, namely the AI agent that reasons through a scientific problem, calls a simulation, reads the result and decides what to try next.

Here’s a summary of what Nvidia announced:.

Industry observers note that while each announcement is interesting, the more compelling story is what they reveal about where scientific computing is headed. I see five themes.

Industry observers note that ian Buck (pictured), Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, summed up this thesis when introducing Rubin HPC: “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery.” This marks an crucial industry shift. Simulation used to be the end product. In an agentic workflow, it’s a tool call within a much larger loop of hypothesis, simulation, and refinement.

It has been revealed that when an agent can generate thousands of candidate molecules or material designs, the bottleneck shifts from ideas to the time required to test them. That’s why so much of the SC26 news focuses on loop speed alongside peak flops. Nvidia claims cuPhoton cut the time to correlate Event Horizon Telescope black-hole data from more than a month to eight minutes.

Industry observers note that at Pacific Fusion, a Nemotron-powered agent running on the same system can analyze plasma simulations as they run, allowing researchers to steer the simulation in real time rather than waiting for it to finish. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is using Nvidia’s DAQIRI networking library to move electron-microscopy analysis into the experiment itself, so researchers can decide what to measure next while measurements are being taken.

According to recent reports, all of these share the same idea: Shrink the gap between asking a question and getting enough of an answer to ask a better one. For researchers, this should change how they evaluate infrastructure. Single-job time-to-solution is an vital metric, but time-to-insight per iteration is equally important and should be tracked.

According to recent reports, the most key data point at SC26 may have come from a startup, not a supercomputer. Lila Sciences post-trained Nemotron with lab feedback, nearly doubling its accuracy on quantum-dot synthesis protocols to 61%, beating GPT-6 Astra’s 54% at what Nvidia states is 10 to 20 times lower inference cost. Therna nearly doubled accuracy over frontier models in predicting mRNA protein-expression ranges. Terray Therapeutics trained the model to extract reactants, products, and conditions from chemistry diagrams.

According to recent reports, that’s consistent with what I’ve been hearing across my enterprise clients: frontier models are a great starting point, but domain-tuned open models often win on accuracy and economics in specialized fields. Science pushes this further than most industries for three reasons. Research data is often proprietary or regulated. Experimental feedback serves as a training signal that general-purpose models lack. Labs want models running on infrastructure they control.

That last point is why Nvidia optimized Nemotron 3.5 Super VL to run on a 128GB DGX Spark. KTH Royal Institute of Technology reports that an agent built on it fixed 81% of broken GROMACS molecular-dynamics setups in a single overnight run on a single Spark.

Nvidia releasing the dataset and the recipes, not just the weights, is notable here because the model is a commodity, but the know-how to adapt it is what research teams have lacked.

Industry observers note that nvidia is well-known as the industry’s top GPU provider, but it also offers a CPU rack with Vera. Nvidia is now targeting the part of HPC that has never been accelerated, a market x86 has owned for decades. In Nvidia’s own testing, Vera delivered 1.9 times the performance and 2.4 times the performance per watt of x86 on an OpenFOAM airflow simulation.

DKRZ, the German Climate Computing Center, has selected Vera for its HLRE-5 system. The fresh Fortran compiler beta isn’t all that sexy, but it’s an crucial piece. Huge amounts of scientific code are written in Fortran, and nobody wants to rewrite it. Removing that friction is how a CPU challenger takes share.

Across the portfolio, Vera handles CPU-bound simulation. Rubin HPC is built for sparse, memory-bound science rather than AI training. DGX systems sit alongside IBM quantum computers. Nvidia is extending Slurm, the open-source scheduler most supercomputing centers already use, to schedule QPUs alongside CPUs and GPUs using familiar commands. Nearly 30 data centers are now deploying more than 50 quantum processors, and Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal and Quantinuum have adopted the expanded Slurm.

Nvidia wants to be the company that coordinates whichever processor the agent needs next. An agent doing drug discovery might call a CPU-bound molecular dynamics job, a GPU-accelerated docking run, and eventually a quantum chemistry routine. The vendor that owns the orchestration owns the workflow. Owning the hardware still matters, but less so than before.

The quantum news deserves its own mention because the tone has shifted. Two or three years ago, vendors mostly talked about qubit counts. At SC26, the focus was on error correction, decoding, and integration, which are classical computing problems. Nvidia’s latest TCBP-JOBS decoder, available in CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0, delivers up to 13,000 times faster decoding for error-correction research and reduces some design studies from 12 weeks to 45 minutes. IBM and RIKEN’s hybrid quantum-classical chemistry work, which modeled protein-ligand complexes with up to 12,635 atoms, is a Gordon Bell Prize finalist.

According to recent reports, IBM’s Jerry Chow discussed the opportunity: “Scaling quantum and classical together will open new frontiers in high-energy and nuclear physics and beyond.” Nvidia has long embraced a systems approach spanning a broad ecosystem of partners, and IBM adds to that. IBM doesn’t need Nvidia to build qubits; it needs accelerated classical computing to make those qubits useful. That’s a typical position for Nvidia, which becomes essential to quantum, regardless of which qubit approach wins.

Energy used to be a facilities problem in HPC. Now it’s a research constraint because every watt spent on overhead is a watt not available for simulation. Nvidia’s Vera delivers twice the energy efficiency of x86 on the Weather Research and Forecasting model.

Lambda’s deployment demonstrates the same idea at the network layer. Across more than 10,000 GPUs, Lambda used co-packaged optics switches and observed network latency drop by about 4% at rack scale and up to about 10% at pod scale, with a median optics temperature of 36 degrees Celsius versus 51 degrees for pluggable optics. This approach is up to five times more power-efficient and up to 15 times more reliable than pluggables, and engineers can swap the light sources in the field.

As Nvidia’s blog notes, with agentic inference, a single network disruption can cause cascading latency across many agents. When the workload is a continuous loop rather than a batch job, uptime becomes a research metric. Lambda is also the first large-scale neocloud proof point for co-packaged optics, which I expect other GPU clouds will need to address.

It’s fitting that Nvidia marked its CUDA software’s 20th anniversary at the same show. CUDA was introduced at SC06, and Nvidia reports that more than 11 million developers now build on it, with more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries. From AlexNet to AlphaFold, the pattern has been the same: hardware draws attention, while libraries create lock-in.

In a recent development, the agentic era raises the stakes for that library catalog. A human scientist might know a handful of tools well. An agent can call any of them, so the size and quality of the toolbox matter even more. Every new CUDA-X library is effectively a new skill for every science agent built on the Nvidia stack. That’s the competitive moat that AMD, Intel, and the custom-silicon players have to cross, and it deepened this week.

In a recent development, most of the performance numbers at SC26 are Nvidia’s own or those of its partners. Historically, I have found Nvidia’s numbers to be accurate, but buyers should validate them against their own workloads. Several key products, including Rubin HPC and HLRE-5, won’t arrive until 2028.

Recent findings suggest that every additional layer Nvidia owns, from CPU to scheduler integration to quantum decoding, raises the familiar question of how open an end-to-end stack can be. Nvidia’s response this week was a strong emphasis on open source: open models, open datasets, open libraries, and contributions to Slurm.

According to recent reports, the bigger takeaway is the shift in what Nvidia is selling. For 20 years, it accelerated the computations scientists ran. Now it’s building the stack for an agent to run the scientific method itself: reason, simulate, measure, refine and repeat. If that model takes hold, the winners in scientific computing won’t be the companies with the fastest single chip. They’ll be the ones that make the whole discovery loop spin fastest. Right now, no one is better positioned than Nvidia for that.

Sources indicate that zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, XPENG just reported 3rd quarter financial details today, while also forecasting what will happen in the 4th quarter. Everything is looking quite rosy at the moment.

As far as 3rd quarter financials go, on the back of strong sales, the tech giant logged 24.28 billion yuan ($3.643 billion) of revenue. That’s a new quarterly record for the company. It’s 19% more than in Q3 2025 and 23% more than Q2 2026.

That said, despite strong revenue, the manufacturer still scored a net loss. It had a significant 870 million yuan ($130.5 million) net loss, in fact, which was up 128% from 380 million yuan in Q3 2025 and down 35% from 1.34 billion from Q2 2026. XPENG made a small profit in Q4 2025, and since then has again been trying to get its finances into the green again instead of in the red.

Recent findings suggest that good news going into the 4th quarter is the organization expects even better. XPENG is forecasting 169,000 to 174,000 vehicle deliveries, which would mean year-over-year growth of 45% to 50%. Expected revenue is 30.4 billion yuan to 31.8 billion yuan, which would mean growth of 37% to 43%.

We’ll see. The tech giant is still not expected to get another net profit quarter, but perhaps the quarter could surprise and XPENG could log its second quarterly profit. One thing making that unlikely, though, is that XPENG’s R&D costs were up significantly, 17.5%. Also, general and administrative expenses were up 11.4% year over year. We’ll see what the 4th quarter brings.

HLTH 2026: Calibrate, Withings study finds wraparound care boosts GLP-1 weight loss by more than 60%

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As health looks and employers continue to evaluate the costs and outcomes associated with GLP-1 weight loss drugs, a latest study found that wraparound clinical care and behavior change support can make expensive GLP-1 treatments more effective and durable.
  • A two-year real-world study from Withings Health Solutions and Calibrate Health suggests that pairing GLP-1 medications with Calibrate’s integrated obesity care program produced substantially greater weight loss than GLP-1 treatment alone, and Calibrate members sustained more of their weight loss.
  • Recent findings suggest that the study followed 4,961 U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
HLTH 2026: Calibrate, Withings study finds wraparound care boosts GLP-1 weight loss by more than 60%" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

As health looks and employers continue to evaluate the costs and outcomes associated with GLP-1 weight loss drugs, a latest study found that wraparound clinical care and behavior change support can make expensive GLP-1 treatments more effective and durable.

A two-year real-world study from Withings Health Solutions and Calibrate Health suggests that pairing GLP-1 medications with Calibrate’s integrated obesity care program produced substantially greater weight loss than GLP-1 treatment alone, and Calibrate members sustained more of their weight loss.

Recent findings suggest that the study followed 4,961 U.S. adults who began GLP-1s between 2022 and 2024, comparing 3,422 Calibrate members with 1,539 Withings customers taking GLP-1s without the program. After adjustment for differences between the groups, Calibrate members lost 17.3% of their starting weight at two years versus 10.7% for the GLP-1-only group, a more than 60% relative difference.

Sources indicate that the study was a real-world observational analysis, not a randomized controlled trial. Because Calibrate members chose to join the program, the two groups differed at the start. Before comparing, a statistical adjustment made them comparable on age, sex, race, BMI, health conditions and GLP-1 treatment, according to the study. Weight was followed for over 24 months.

The study findings, shared first with Fierce Healthcare, underscore that GLP-1 treatment may work better when medication is paired with personalized clinical management, behavioral coaching and continuous monitoring, rather than being treated primarily as a prescription benefit, according to Calibrate, a digitally integrated obesity management solution.

The study results also reinforce that obesity should be treated as a disease, another chronic metabolic condition requiring intensive, ongoing support, rather than a medication-only problem, Linda Anegawa, M.D., Calibrate Health’s chief medical advisor, told Fierce Healthcare.

“With any chronic disease, like hypertension for example, you won’t get as good outcomes if you just hand someone a medication and don’t support them across other pillars of health, like self-monitoring blood pressure, physical activity and stress reduction. Type 2 diabetes is another good example; you can give high doses of insulin, but medication can’t do the job alone without nutrition education and support,” she noted.

In a recent development, “[The study results] make it very clear that treatment [for obesity] shouldn’t stop at just drug coverage,” she added. “As we envision the future, I’d like to see obesity care looking very similar to diabetes care, with insurance covering the full range of necessary services from medication treatment to nutrition education and overall lifestyle support. Obesity is a complex, chronic disease deserving of the same coverage parity as any other.".

Treating obesity as such not only prevents health complications and improves quality of life, but it will also lower overall long-term health systems’ costs of care, Anegawa asserted.

The advantage of the integrated care program persisted despite weight regain, the study found. While both study groups regained some weight after reaching their lowest point, the Calibrate members remained about 16.6% below their starting weight, according to the study results. The GLP-1-only group reached a best point of 12.6% weight loss and was about 9.2% below baseline at the peak of its rebound.

According to recent reports, there was a body-composition benefit as well. In a subgroup of 974 participants followed for body composition, the muscle-to-fat ratio improved 49.3% for Calibrate members versus 39.9% for GLP-1-only users at 18 months, roughly a 9-point difference.

The study data is based on two years of daily weigh-ins from Withings-connected scales, analyzed with causal-inference methods. Body composition was followed over 18 months in 520 Calibrate members and 454 Withings customers.

The study reinforces the importance of evaluating body composition, rather than weight alone, in obesity treatment, Anegawa noted.

“We know that abnormal visceral fat accumulation and dysfunction is what drives most of the metabolic conditions we treat, so if we aren’t equipping members to maximize visceral fat loss and preserve muscle, we can actually end up making people sicker. Losing muscle has severe consequences—it isn’t just scaffolding. Muscle is a critical metabolic organ that regulates energy balance, hormonal signaling and insulin sensitivity,” she noted.

Adding the insights of body composition to Calibrate's clinical and metabolic data allows the company to better monitor trends and adapt care based on quality evidence, she noted.

There are several key factors that make an integrated obesity care program more effective than a medication-only program, Anegawa stated.

"Physician-led personalized care that includes medication optimization for each member’s needs, tailored wraparound support, and features that drive continuous engagement—all of which are designed to maximize clinical outcomes," she said.

"Breaking this down, we start with a comprehensive clinical evaluation for each member, vs. other programs, which only require a questionnaire for a prescription. This helps us get to know each member’s medical and weight histories in detail. We analyze comprehensive lab data to understand their baseline metabolic profile. This information is then used by our expert clinicians to personalize clinical care from day one," Anegawa stated.

According to recent reports, live one-to-one coaching support focuses on four pillars of healthy weight maintenance: nutrition, activity, sleep and mindset shift. Tailored education and anticipatory guidance help members manage side effects and stay on treatment, while connecting members to their personal motivations helps sustain engagement through challenges and supports lasting improvements in metabolic health, according to Calibrate.

According to recent reports, calibrate Health has been working with connected health device maker Withings for over five years. The tech giant's members use Withings devices regularly as a required part of the program, according to Anegawa.

"We were already getting body composition data that gave us additional insights into individual members’ health. That data led to additional questions, such as are there significant differences that we can see in aggregate? If so, how large are the differences, and are they changing clinical outcomes? Can we use these data to inform and improve the evolution of our protocols and clinical care? So in asking these types of questions, it became clear to both the Calibrate and Withings teams that we should formalize this into a collaborative study," she noted.

The use of smart devices, specifically Wi-Fi or Bluetooth-connected scales, provides continuous data to help identify weight loss patterns that might not have been apparent through traditional clinical measures, noted Antoine Pivron, vice president of Withings Health Solutions.

"Today, most people on a GLP-1 are monitored through a keyhole. A patient whose primary care doctor prescribes the drug might be weighed a few times a year, and each reading reflects one day: what they ate, the time, the clothes they wore. Between visits, nobody knows whether they plateaued in month three, started regaining in month five, or stopped the drug altogether," he remarked.

According to recent reports, "Specialty programs do better, but many rely on self-reported weights from whatever scale the patient owns. And people tend to stop reporting exactly when things go wrong, which is the moment the care team most needs to know," he added.

According to recent reports, body composition is the biggest blind spot, Pivron asserted. Withings' smart scales track weight and detailed body composition metrics to help identify whether the weight coming off during treatment is fat or muscle.

"In the study we did with Calibrate, two years of data let us see the full shape of the journey: the drop, the low point, and the partial regain that follows. We could also see the quality of the weight loss, not just the quantity. Program members improved their muscle-to-fat balance more, but part of their extra weight loss was muscle. That tells a program exactly where to focus next: protein and strength training," Pivron said.

Withings, a French consumer electronics tech giant, debuted its B2B health solutions division in 2019 to meet the growing market around virtual care and remote management in the U.S.

Pivron expects connected health devices like smart scales to play a growing role in GLP-1 treatment programs and broader chronic disease management.

It has been revealed that "A GLP-1 prescription isn’t a care strategy. The programs that work combine three things: the drug, the clinical and coaching support around it, and the data that demonstrates whether it’s working. Miss one, and real-world results rarely match what we see in trials," he remarked.

Body composition will become standard in GLP-1 care, Pivron asserted: "That’s where the clinical definition of obesity is already heading.".

Connected devices provide the data layer—continuously tracking weight and body composition, predicting when patients may be veering off course and identifying additional risks such as hypertension.

In a recent development, "But a risk score is not a diagnosis. A notification with no next step just creates anxiety. These signals belong inside a care program with a protocol: confirm with a cuff, see a clinician, treat if needed," he stated. "Employers and payers are moving toward paying for outcomes. Connected devices are how a program proves it delivered them.".

Employers face rising healthcare costs—projected to climb 9.5% next year—and GLP-1 treatments are a major contributor to that cost growth.

The study provides evidence of better outcomes with wraparound care, but it did not evaluate the impact on healthcare spending.

Anegawa contends that improvements in markers associated with high metabolic risk, like Hemoglobin A1c, the liver enzyme ALT and lipids, would point to meaningful cost savings.

Calibrate data from separate evaluations show substantial improvements in these markers among Calibrate members.

“Among Calibrate members who started the program with diabetes or prediabetes, 80% reached normoglycemic status at one year. Among those with abnormal ALT, 79% shifted to the normal range, and 68% of those with abnormal triglycerides were normal at year one," she remarked.

Withings' body composition data builds on Calibrate's prior data and gives the firm another lens on the whole picture, "suggesting that lower healthcare spend is likely,” Anegawa said.

It has been revealed that greater treatment persistence could also ultimately reduce costs. An integrated approach helps keep members engaged so they stick with treatment and get the full benefit of therapy, she noted.

Along with weight loss and metabolic improvements, Calibrate members also report compelling health and productivity outcomes, Anegawa said. Among members with a high work-related burden at intake, 82% no longer reported it at one year.

“My favorite evidence of all is that 90% report that Calibrate improved their overall quality of life, and 94% say that their health is better than a year ago - the most clinically meaningful to me overall,” she said.
