HLTH 2026: CVS Health, Cigna and Abridge collaborating with OpenAI to test computer-use agents" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

OpenAI is expanding computer-use agents for healthcare, enabling AI to navigate electronic health record systems, payer portals and other software to tackle repetitive and manual tasks.

Computer-use agents, also called computer-using agents, are AI systems designed to interact with software interfaces the same way a human does—by viewing a screen, moving a cursor, clicking buttons and typing text.

Research teams at OpenAI have been exploring how computer-use agents can assist healthcare teams with fragmented clinical and administrative workflows while keeping people in control, Karan Singhal, head of Health AI and Artificial General Intelligence at OpenAI, told Fierce Healthcare.

"Around six months ago we set a research bet that we thought that the abilities for agents to use computers would end up being helpful and reliable enough in healthcare to help people with clinical and administrative workflows," Singhal said in an exclusive interview sharing evaluation results on OpenAI's early work with computer-use agents in healthcare.

In an interview with Fierce Healthcare, Singhal also shed light on how OpenAI is working with CVS Health, Cigna Healthcare, Abridge and Ambience to apply computer-use agents to specific workflows, including referrals, prior authorizations, discharge planning, specialist consults and care manager preparation.

Sources indicate that healthcare systems are often disconnected, forcing administrative staff and care teams to manually move information from one system to another before a patient can get care. If a clinician orders an MRI, for example, the insurer may need information from the patient’s medical record, but a staff member still has to pull that information and enter it into a separate portal to request authorization, Singhal noted.

OpenAI executives and researchers framed computer use as the next step in healthcare AI, moving beyond copilots that draft or summarize information to agents that can actually work across EHRs, payer portals and other applications on a user's behalf.

Computer-use agents can bridge healthcare's fragmented software environment, especially where application programming interfaces (APIs) and other integrations don't exist or don't connect an entire workflow, Singhal noted.

"We have been working with health systems on things like ChatGPT for Healthcare and our integration with Epic, but there are still limitations in how useful AI agents can be today. Computer use is really a way of resolving a lot of these barriers that exist between AI capabilities and healthcare software so that care teams can deliver better care, more effectively and more efficiently," he said.

OpenAI continues to invest in APIs, plugins and MCP connectors to integrate AI with healthcare software, but the industry’s fragmented and legacy technology can make those integrations slow and incomplete, Singhal noted. Computer use can help bridge those gaps.

"What we hope to do with this release is move us closer to a world where, because AI is connected to more services, AI can help more with a lot of these workflows," he noted.

Care teams, developers and individual clinicians can access computer use for healthcare through ChatGPT for Healthcare, ChatGPT for Clinicians and the OpenAI API.

In a research demonstration using synthetic patient data, OpenAI highlighted how a computer-use agent could support a clinician and an authorization specialist working on the same MRI request. In the demonstration video, a patient messages their clinician about lower back pain. The clinician then instructs the computer-use agent to review the patient’s visit notes, physical therapy records and prior imaging in the EHR. The computer-use agent drafts an MRI order, an encounter note and a reply to the patient for the clinician to review.

In the same demo video, the agent then uses the same records to prepare a prior authorization request in the insurer’s portal for an authorization specialist to review.

"The clinician and authorization specialist were both completely in control of their workflow, but the computer-use agent was able to help across different parts of the workflow and translate that into action," Singhal noted about the demo video.

Sources indicate that openAI evaluated GPT‑6 Astra on tasks clinicians handle in their EHR inboxes. These tasks, shaped by physician input, require Astra to carry out multi-step workflows designed to test both clinical reasoning over longitudinal patient context and navigation of complex interfaces. Reviewers examined the model’s actions alongside the notes, orders and patient messages it produced, assessing whether the work would be helpful and clinically safe in the context of the task, according to an OpenAI blog post.

OpenAI states its GPT-6 Astra model can perform multi-step EHR tasks such as reviewing patient records, drafting messages and notes, preparing medication refills and proposing orders, while leaving key actions for clinician review. In OpenAI's evaluation, 99% of 325 reviewed tasks were rated clinically safe, while physicians rated the model "very helpful" or "extremely helpful" in 93% of 646 assessments.

Clinical safety was assessed by evaluating whether inaccuracies, omissions or actions in the model’s work could plausibly lead to patient harm, OpenAI said.

Regarding the 1% of tasks rated not clinically safe, Singal noted researchers did not identify any cases where the model created a specific, plausible risk of patient harm. "In some cases, the model might overreach and might take an action without getting the proper sign-off or authorization," he said.

"The models are not perfect today, and what we're sharing is an upgrade on research results where we're seeing this critical point where the models seem to be useful in practice," he added.

OpenAI researchers also evaluated computer-use agents for administrative tasks, such as prior authorizations, appeals and medical equipment orders.

Recent findings suggest that openAI notes it designed its computer-use agents with robust safeguards and data security in place, according to the company. The agents can be configured with limits on system access and actions, and audit logs provide a clear record of agent actions and approvals, giving healthcare teams visibility into how each workflow was completed.

Organizations are testing out and deploying computer-use applications across different workflows and administrative tasks.

CVS Health is using OpenAI’s computer-use capabilities to automate repetitive work across clinical systems, including sending documents, processing referrals and supporting specialist consults. In one production workflow, an agent cleared a months-long document-sending backlog over a weekend, OpenAI detailed in the blog post. Another agent handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consults each day.

Generative AI manufacturer Abridge is building computer-use agents to help clinicians carry out care plans across use cases and applications they use every day, including those without APIs. The company also plans to develop an inpatient use case, adding EHR information and nurse and clinician context to identify what needs attention and to coordinate next steps, the company said. As an example, agents can work concurrently on medication access and home health coordination, using computer interaction alongside calls and messages.

Recent findings suggest that cigna Healthcare is using OpenAI’s models to pull together member information from more than 10 clinical and administrative systems, including benefits, providers, appointments and previous interactions. The goal is to reduce the time case managers spend searching across systems and give them more time to support members, OpenAI wrote in the blog post.

Companies including Assort, Bunkerhill, Forus, Gravity and Tennr are testing agents that interact directly with EHRs and payer portals for referral management, authorization checks, medication approvals and other operational tasks.

Industry observers note that “We're continuing to invest in the models, making the models better at computer use. An vital way that we think that they could continue to improve is around improved latency and costs,” Singhal noted.

OpenAI sees its role in healthcare as building foundational AI capabilities and letting healthcare companies handle the “last mile” of implementation, Singhal noted. Computer use is one example: OpenAI provides the technology and safeguards, while partners apply it to specialized workflows and deploy it within healthcare organizations.

The company also confirmed today improvements to trusted clinical search in ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians, including how ChatGPT finds, evaluates and cites medical evidence. Most crucially, though, it's weird and impractical and fun — characteristics I hope befit Pattinson's Bond, who I hope will follow more in Pierce Brosnan's quippy brogue-prints than Daniel Craig's tactical bootsteps.

China’s Electric Heavy Trucks Are Taking Sales from Diesel and LNG

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (997 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In September 2026, battery-electric trucks captured 49.8% of China’s fresh domestic heavy-truck registrations.
  • Battery electric accounted for about 13% of domestic heavy-truck registrations in 2024, 28% in 2025 and nearly 38% in the first nine months of 2026.
  • From May through September, new-energy heavy trucks exceeded 40% of new registrations for five straight months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In September 2026, battery-electric trucks captured 49.8% of China’s fresh domestic heavy-truck registrations. Of 65,800 trucks registered, 32,800 ran on batteries. Another 36 used hydrogen fuel cells. Battery electric accounted for more than 99% of the broader new-energy category. China’s freight operators are buying batteries at a scale that puts diesel and LNG suppliers under pressure.

The shift has gathered speed. Battery electric accounted for about 13% of domestic heavy-truck registrations in 2024, 28% in 2025 and nearly 38% in the first nine months of 2026. The figures come from compulsory-insurance registrations for trucks sold into the domestic market, excluding exports. China’s total domestic truck market remains below its pre-pandemic levels. Battery trucks are gaining share while the market for new heavy trucks remains constrained.

From May through September, new-energy heavy trucks exceeded 40% of new registrations for five straight months. The category reached approximately 226,400 vehicles in the first nine months, up 64% from the same period in 2025, and nearly 99% were battery electric. Tractor units that pull semi-trailers are leading the change. In September, 64.48% of new domestic tractor registrations belonged to the new-energy category. Electric trucks are moving freight on ordinary commercial routes, including work beyond ports and industrial yards.

My full TFIE Strategy Briefing traces China’s heavy-truck sales from 2015 through 2026, examines real freight costs and charging choices, and assesses the consequences for manufacturers, logistics companies and fuel demand.

According to recent reports, the operating economics explain much of the appeal. Trucks earn money by carrying cargo, so annual kilometres, payload, electricity prices, charging stops and vehicle availability matter as much as the price on the invoice. High-mileage routes make electricity and maintenance savings more valuable. A costly grid connection or charging queue can eat into those savings. Fleet operators need to evaluate the truck and its route together.

Industry observers note that recent ICCT case studies document how those economics play out. A Guangdong warehouse fleet of 28 electric trucks had estimated five-year ownership costs 16% below comparable diesel trucks. In Yangtze River Delta express delivery, 50 electric tractor-trailers working routes of 300–500 km achieved a narrower 3% advantage over six years without purchase incentives. Another operation covering 900 km a day with strategically placed high-power charging showed estimated ownership costs 19% below diesel. The differences reflect route, utilization and charging arrangements.

Those three operations offer a more useful procurement lesson than a single quoted range figure. The operator starts with cargo, schedules and energy access, then selects equipment. The narrow 3% margin in express delivery also reveals why financing and charging costs can determine whether a viable electric route makes money.

Recent findings suggest that battery swapping has carved out a sizable part of this market. In September, 20.09% of newly registered battery-electric heavy trucks were classified as swap-capable. That compares with 22.92% across January–September 2026 and 30.39% for all of 2025. The number of swap-classified trucks continued to rise, while conventional charging gained a larger share of the expanding electric market. China’s registration classification also includes some trucks with leased batteries that are recharged rather than exchanged.

Sources indicate that swapping fits dense, repeatable freight operations such as steelworks, ports and bulk-material haulage. Fleet operators and station owners can standardize vehicles and use stations often enough to pay for batteries held in inventory. Conventional charging serves a wider range of routes and can fit scheduled stops, overnight parking and depot operations. Both approaches depend on predictable truck traffic and reliable electricity connections.

According to recent reports, china is building infrastructure around those freight patterns. Yunnan commissioned 3,350 km of heavy-truck charging corridors in 2025, with 113 stations and 869 connectors. Fujian opened a 649 km coastal corridor in October 2026, including 15 charging stations and eight swapping stations. The IEA’s 2026 charging review describes the concentration of heavy-vehicle charging around freight corridors and industrial centres. Long-haul coverage still has gaps, but the network is expanding where trucks already have work to do.

Hydrogen has found little traction alongside this expansion. China registered 689 fuel-cell heavy trucks in the first nine months of 2026, compared with more than 223,000 battery-electric trucks. LNG has a much larger installed customer base, although its advantage over diesel has narrowed as gas prices change. Battery trucks offer a different cost structure built around drivetrain efficiency and lower maintenance needs. That makes the competition increasingly difficult for equipment and fuel suppliers dependent on combustion engines.

Sources indicate that sales changes take years to work through the operating fleet. Kpler projects that latest-energy trucks, predominantly battery electric, will account for about 8% of Chinese heavy trucks in service at the end of 2026. It also estimates they will displace about 230,000 barrels of diesel per day compared with moving the same freight using diesel trucks. Freight vehicles with high daily utilization can have a large effect on fuel demand before they become a majority of vehicles on the road.

China’s June 2026 heavy-truck programme joins purchasing incentives, grid access, charging corridors, financing and logistics planning. Its 2030 targets include a 40% share of newly introduced-energy heavy-truck sales, a 20% share of the operating fleet and 30,000 km of zero-carbon freight corridors. Monthly new sales have already surpassed the sales-share target. Building and replacing enough vehicles to reach the fleet target will take longer.

Recent findings suggest that other countries have different electricity tariffs, road networks and freight routes, but the procurement method travels. Start with the actual jobs trucks perform. Identify routes with strong electric economics, plan the charging and grid connections those routes require, and finance vehicles and infrastructure as one programme. Other drivetrains can compete where their operating costs or performance are better. The evidence from China’s largest commercial freight applications increasingly favours batteries.

The complete TFIE Strategy Briefing includes the historical registration series, the ICCT ownership-cost cases, charging and swapping corridors, and fleet-turnover analysis. TFIE Strategy works with fleets, utilities and policymakers on freight-electrification scenarios and investment decisions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
The Permanente Medical Group launches tech incubation company" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

The Permanente Medical Group revealed on Monday the launch of a physician-led innovation company it mentioned will strike technology partnerships to co-develop, incubate and launch upcoming enterprise healthcare delivery technologies.

Permanentech—a wholly owned subsidiary of the 10,000-physician medical group, which is itself part of the massive integrated nonprofit Kaiser Permanente—looks to rapidly advance potential new healthcare offerings informed by its frontline physicians and the broader organization’s focus on value-based care.

It marked the launch by announcing its first portfolio company: Wrapt Health, which offers an automated tool that predicts likely missed medical appointments for early outreach and rescheduling. In line with Permanentech’s broader thesis, it was born from a TPMG physician’s experiences, validated within the medical group and so far scaled to 22 sites in Kaiser Permanente’s Northern California region.

“Our clinicians are continuously innovating and refining how we deliver care,” Kenneth Trauner, M.D., CEO of Permanentech and chief innovation officer at TPMG, said in a release. “Permanentech gives them a dedicated resource to rapidly turn their insights and creativity into scalable solutions that benefit both our patients and the wider health care community.”.

Permanentech will be focused on technologies and AI-enabled tools addressing patient service, access and quality, TPMG mentioned, with successful products also having the potential to improve “the economics of care delivery.” The business is structured “to move at the pace of the technology industry,” but has “a clear advantage” via its access to TPMG and Kaiser Permanente’s substantial footprint for deployment and validation, it said.

Those efforts will involve both home-grown tools and those developed by established or early-stage partners.

According to recent reports, the former will champion physician-developed tools created inside TPMG’s ecosystem as an independent company rolls out. Starting from the concept phase, that support would include financing as well as clinical and operational validation, as was the case with Wrapt Health.

“Our physicians and care teams see every day where technology can make care better,” Kristine Lee, M.D., an associate executive director and chief transformation officer at TPMG, stated. “Permanentech gives them a real hand in building tools that lift administrative burden and give time back to patients. When clinicians help build the tools, those tools fit the way they actually work.”.

Strategic partnerships and joint ventures, meanwhile, will focus on co-development, clinical valuation and scaled deployment. Permanentech noted the latter will begin with local deployments that are expanded to other TPMG sites when solutions “prove their value,” and could include additional strategic support as a partner tech giant looks to advance their offering beyond TPMG.

Permanentech aims to add more portfolio companies and partnerships “in the coming months,” according to its announcement.

According to recent reports, “For decades, our physicians have delivered high-quality, preventive care inside an integrated system where clinical expertise, data and incentives all point toward keeping people healthy,” Maria Ansari, M.D., CEO and executive director of TPMG, said. “Permanentech is our commitment to putting that ecosystem to work alongside the best technology from inside and outside our walls.”.

Pleasanton, California-based TPMG is the country’s largest medical group, caring for 4.7 million Northern California members with about 10,000 physicians and nearly 47,000 nurses and support staff. It operates at 203 medical offices and facilities, as well as 21 hospitals.

Its parent organization, Kaiser Permanente, is the country’s largest nonprofit health system by operating revenue ($127.7 billion in 2025). Topline financial results shared earlier this month outlined a 9% year-over-year increase in Q3 operating revenue, while the system’s Risant Health value-based care platform subsidiary in October announced intends to acquire Integris Health, Oklahoma’s largest nonprofit provider.

Bentley Torcal EV Is Already Sold Out Through 2027

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's Tuesday, November 17, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place.
  • In a recent development, in this morning's edition, Bentley's Torcal EV is sold out all the way through 2027, Tesla is going to invest over $3.3 billion in expanding its German factory so it can build Cybercabs, General Motors wants to add a lot more robots and automation into its facilities and BMW wants the U.S.
  • Bentley's first all-electric vehicle might have a bit of a silly name and slightly polarizing styling, but it would seem that's not enough to keep buyers away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Good morning! It's Tuesday, November 17, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most important stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In a recent development, in this morning's edition, Bentley's Torcal EV is sold out all the way through 2027, Tesla is going to invest over $3.3 billion in expanding its German factory so it can build Cybercabs, General Motors wants to add a lot more robots and automation into its facilities and BMW wants the U.S. government to cut it some slack on tariffs.

Bentley's first all-electric vehicle might have a bit of a silly name and slightly polarizing styling, but it would seem that's not enough to keep buyers away. Initial demand for the Torcal is shockingly strong, with the electric crossover already sold out through 2027. Now, if you want one, Bentley is taking orders for 2028. You'll be lucky to get one before you vote for the next President.

One caveat to all of this is that Bentley hasn't said how many Torcal build slots were actually available for 2027, and it hasn't indicated any sales volumes, so theoretically, it could have sold like 5 of the Cayenne-sized EVs, but I sort of doubt that. A spokesperson for the British luxury automaker said it was "very pleased with the response and the position we're in" following the Torcal's reveal in September. From Automotive News:.

It has been revealed that based on orders, the S variant has been the most popular Torcal so far, [Bentley CEO Frank-Steffen] Walliser noted. In general, Bentley has seen the Torcal attract new and younger customers to the brand.

The Torcal, based on Volkswagen Group's Premium Platform Electric, is slotted beneath the Bentayga, Bentley's first crossover.

It will become Bentley's fourth nameplate alongside the Bentayga, Continental GT coupe and convertible, and Flying Spur sedan. The rest of the Bentley lineup is offered with gasoline and plug-in hybrid powertrains.

It has been revealed that the Torcal has a range of up to 375 miles from a 113-kilowatt-hour battery and offers fast charging at 400 kilowatts. Power is rated at 810 hp and 881 pound-feet of torque for the Torcal and 876 hp and 996 pound-feet of torque for the Torcal S, making it the most powerful Bentley to date.

Industry observers note that U.S. pricing starts at $222,495 for the Torcal, $262,695 for the high-performance Torcal S and $300,995 for the Torcal First Edition.

Bentayga pricing starts at $231,150, the Flying Spur starts at $254,850 and the Continental GT starts at $288,750. All prices include shipping.

Recent findings suggest that the EV market is sort of an unknown in the ultra-luxury space. Sure, Rolls-Royce brought out the Spectre in 2023, and that has been a success; the Cadillac Celestiq is doing alright and the Ferrari Luce is selling well, despite its deeply polarizing design. However, Lamborghini killed its Lanzador EV earlier this year.

The Torcal's success is paramount for Bentley in the coming years. It invested $463 million to upgrade its factory in Crewe, England to build the EV, and it has spent even more than that on R&D and supply chain preparations. That's a lot of money to make back for a low-volume automaker like Bentley. It's doubly crucial because the automaker's global sales fell 17% through September, and the brand's profits dropped by over half to $54.1 million through the first nine months of 2026. This thing needs to be a sales success, and luckily for Bentley, it's looking that way.

Tesla is about to drop $3.31 billion to add a latest facility at its Berlin-Brandenburg factory in Germany in an effort to boost production of CEO Elon Musk's latest pet project: the Cybercab. The news comes just days after Tesla opened direct sales to select customers. The blueprint is for production to officially begin in 2029, and it'll eventually ramp up to 1 million vehicles per year, according to factory lead Andrew Tierig. Construction is slated to begin in the first half of next year.

It has been revealed that that's quite an expansion. The German factory, which first opened in March of 2022, makes hundreds of thousands of Model Ys and millions of battery cells, but it doesn't exactly produce a million vehicles per year. From The Wall Street Journal:.

The group remarked on X Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990 and a $299-a-month subscription to Tesla's autonomy software.

Tesla started adding Cybercabs to its Austin fleet of robotaxis in September, and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation to determine whether the steering-wheel-free vehicles comply with safety standards. Tesla told the regulator that the Cybercab meets all applicable standards, the NHTSA said in a filing.

It has been revealed that musk recently said the firm would wind down production of the Cybertruck at its gigafactory in Texas next year to make room for increased production of the self-driving Cybercab. Adding a dedicated facility in Germany would allow Tesla to make the Cybercab on both sides of the Atlantic.

As Tesla's sales in Europe started regaining strength earlier this year after declining in 2025, the company has sought to boost output in Germany. In May, Thierig noted the group would invest $250 million into its German factory to increase production of EV battery cells.

In a recent development, I'm skeptical of the scale of this project, but if it works, it would be good news for Germany's struggling automotive industry. Local automakers are having a tough time right now and cutting tens of thousands of jobs as they look for ways to remain competitive against Chinese rivals. Obviously, building out Tesla's factory and then staffing it would create a lot of theoretical jobs.

Recent findings suggest that general Motors is looking to increase the use of robots and other automation by 20% at its factories in North America by 2028 as it looks for ways to deal with higher labor and onshoring costs. The General is said to be developing its own robots and assembling them at its Kokomo, Indiana, plant, according to unnamed sources who spoke with Reuters. It's focused on using autonomous mobile robots to move parts around its plants. Unsurprisingly, the United Auto Workers union is rightfully worried about this strategy.

At the moment, GM is buying robotics equipment from outside suppliers while developing its own in-house, and it's asking parts suppliers bidding on new contracts to submit automation prepares for their own operations. GM is using a scorecard to rate suppliers' automation efforts and even considering the scores in contract decisions. From Reuters:.

GM remarked it uses automation to improve safety, quality and ​efficiency. "As competition intensifies globally, we continue to put these technologies to work in ways that support our manufacturing teams," its statement said.

US automakers have increased automation ​to contain manufacturing costs since the United Auto Workers won record contract gains in 2023 and President Donald Trump's drive to bring more factory work home put pressure on production costs.

The UAW, as you may have imagined, is not a fan of this.

The UAW won the contract gains from GM and its crosstown competitors Ford Motor and Jeep-parent Stellantis. GM noted the contract would add about $575 ​in labor costs per vehicle; Ford pegged its added cost at $900 per vehicle.

At the time, analysts mentioned the companies likely would increase automation as a ​way to defray the higher labor costs. GM last year said it had about 100 roboticists, AI engineers and hardware specialists working on advanced robotics systems.

US automakers have long ‌mentioned their ⁠labor costs exceed those of foreign rivals and newer competitors such as Tesla, whose US factories are largely nonunion.

Industry observers note that the companies face another round of potentially contentious negotiations in 2028, when the contracts are scheduled to expire. UAW President Shawn Fain already has warned that AI and increased automation pose a threat to workers.

"The fruits of our labor have multiplied like never before, but workers aren't reaping the harvest. That's theft," Fain said at a UAW convention in ​June. "And if AI continues to be used ​as an accessory to that ⁠crime, it has to be stopped.".

Automation is nothing new at vehicle factories, but automakers are exploring more ways to integrate AI and robotics into their plants. At the end of the day, a robot is less expensive and less needy than a person, and if a tech giant can save even a dime by using a robot versus a human, it's going to do it 10 times out of 10.

BMW is sick and tired of being sick and tired over these tariffs, and it wants some relief. It's the latest in a group of foreign automakers that are currently in talks with the Trump administration that are trying to catch a break on import duties by investing billions in new U.S. factories. Last year alone, BMW ate more than $1 billion in U.S. import tariffs, according to Robert Engelhorn, CEO of BMW Manufacturing.

In a recent development, the German automaker is pointing toward the $1.7 billion it spent on expanding its U.S. footprint for EV production at its plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. The tech giant produces more than 400,000 vehicles per year there, and ships about half of them to 120 countries. From Automotive News:.

BMW's status as the largest auto exporter by value in the U.S., as well as its recent investments, are worthy of consideration for tariff relief, as company officials see it.

South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster stated he would like to see lower tariffs for a company bringing outsized economic benefit to the state.

According to recent reports, "Over time, I've had conversations with the people in Washington about that very thing," McMaster told Automotive News at a Nov. 13 event celebrating the opening of BMW's battery pack factory. "Nothing moves real fast sometimes, but it's all going to work out just fine, and this is more proof of it right here.".

Last year, it imported about 215,000 vehicles to the U.S., most of which were sedans like the 3 Series and 4 Series. I'm not sure if it'll be enough to sway the Trump administration, but it's worth a shot. I'm sure having McMaster, a character we saw during Trump's first administration when he served as the National Security Advisor, in its corner is helpful, though.

Allina Health, Sutter Health notch Minn. AG's approval for $26B combination" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Sacramento-based Sutter Health and Minneapolis-based Allina Health's plans to combine have earned the blessing of Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, a key hurdle that paves the path for a Jan. 1, 2027 close.

The nonprofit systems and the attorney general's office declared Monday an oversight agreement replete with service line preservation requirements and $2.15 billion of promised capital investments. Their deal is set to create a 39-hospital cross-regional health system that would be a major player in Minnesota's increasingly concentrated healthcare market.

Industry observers note that "My office has extensive authority to review healthcare transactions in Minnesota: we take it very seriously and with every review, we apply the lens of whether it will help you afford your life and live with dignity, safety and respect," Ellison said in the announcement. "At the end of our thorough review of the transaction between Sutter and Allina, I have determined it passes the public-interest test.”.

It has been revealed that per the attorney general's office, the $2.5 billion be invested over five years to increase healthcare capacity in the state. That includes $150 million toward rural care, $50 million in workforce development and the scaling of virtual addiction therapy programs across the state.

The systems also agreed to maintain core services at rural locations for five years, to maintain reproductive and gender care for five years (as it complies with state and federal statute) and to continue Medicare participation and charity care. For Allina's workforce, they also agreed to retain all employees in good standing, honor all collective bargaining agreements and not enforce some noncompete agreements.

Ellison's office will enforce the five-year commitments via a 10-year period of oversight, which will include annual compliance reports from Sutter and Allina.

"In the context where the provision of healthcare everywhere is under serious financial strain and Allina is facing its own struggles, I appreciate that Sutter is entering Minnesota with a mindset of growth and an understanding that we cannot simply cut our way out of financial challenges and maintain Minnesota’s high standard of healthcare," Ellison remarked. "Sutter’s leadership has a history of delivering on growth and innovation and I look forward to their doing the same here.".

Industry observers note that since the nonprofits announced their deal back in March, Minnesota and the Midwest have been the stage for substantial health system dealmaking. Sanford Health announced and closed its acquisition of North Memorial Health, while Essentia Health and HealthPartners in September shared fresh aims to combine and form an integrated 22-hospital organization.

Industry observers note that sutter and Allina, in a joint statement, thanked Ellison's office for the sign-off and said they proposal to close their transaction on Jan. 1, 2027.

"From the beginning, our vision has been grounded in a simple yet powerful belief: people across Minnesota and western Wisconsin deserve a sustainable health system that provides access to high-quality, affordable health care when and where they need it," the statement reads. "With our combined capabilities and more than $2 billion in investment, we will expand access to care, improve affordability, enhance care team and patient experiences and accelerate high-impact research and innovation.".

Sacramento-based Sutter Health and Minneapolis-based Allina Health's pending combination took a step forward this week with the signing of a definitive agreement, the nonprofit systems revealed Thursday.

The agreement locks in the plans shared earlier this year in a letter of intent—namely, that the cross-market deal would bring more than $2 billion of investment to Allina's markets and that the smaller system would become the "Upper Midwest Division of Sutter Health.".

Now the organizations are left with securing state and federal regulatory approvals before the deal can close, which they expect to happen before the end of this year.

In a recent development, “This important milestone brings us one step closer to our goal of partnering to enhance care, support our teams and expand clinical capabilities and research as a strong, nonprofit health system,” Lisa Shannon, president and CEO of Allina Health, said in Thursday's announcement. “With our combined expertise, complementary strengths and aligned missions and visions, I am confident we will be well-positioned to meet the evolving needs of our patients and communities now and well into the future.

According to recent reports, should the deal close, the resulting organization would span 39 hospitals as well as more than 400 primary and specialty care sites that collectively see over 5 million patients annually. The organization would also employ 88,000 people, with 18,000 aligned physicians.

Sacramento-based Sutter Health and Minneapolis-based Allina Health unveiled looks to join and form a 39-hospital, $26 billion nonprofit health system.

The pair said Tuesday that they have signed a letter of intent for Allina to join Sutter. Allina would maintain its brand and regional headquarters but operate as the Upper Midwest Division of Sutter. Under that arrangement, Sutter is also committing $2 billion to bolster care access and patient experience investments in Allina’s Minnesota and western Wisconsin markets.

“This includes establishing new ambulatory and specialty care sites to fill care gaps and meet growing community needs, as well as recruiting more physicians and enhancing AI and digital health capabilities,” Sutter Health President and CEO Warner Thomas, who would maintain those titles should the deal close, said in the announcement. “Building on our complementary strengths and combined expertise, we will build a healthcare innovation engine that accelerates how ideas move from development and design into improving the health of patients and communities.”.

The systems remarked they proposal to complete due diligence and finalize terms for a definitive agreement “over the coming weeks and months,” targeting a close before the end of 2026 should regulatory reviews run smoothly. A representative for Allina described the structure of the proposed agreement as being similar to a member substitution but noted that the deal's final structure will be outlined in the pending definitive agreement.

Alongside the 39 hospitals, the resulting organization would include more than 400 primary and specialty care sites that collectively see over 5 million patients annually. The combination would also employ 88,000 people, with 18,000 aligned physicians.

Among the benefits of their proposed partnership, the systems led their announcement with the synergistic technical expertise of their organizations and surrounding communities: Sutter’s immersion in Northern California's artificial intelligence and platform development and Allina’s seat in the medtech and engineering hub of Minnesota.

“The proposed combined system will be uniquely positioned to be a national leader in digital and technological advancements that meaningfully improve patients’ and caregivers’ experiences, while continuing to provide the compassionate care their respective communities have relied on for decades,” the announcement reads.

Such efforts, outlined in the announcement, include AI and digital solutions that would reduce administrative burdens for caregivers along with more convenient appointment scheduling for patients via digital consumer tools.

More broadly, the organizations noted they expect the combination will help the organizations bolster physician and clinician recruitment, improve patient affordability and grow their capabilities, “particularly in clinical centers of excellence.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We are incredibly excited for the opportunity to harness the collective strength of our two mission-driven organizations to make a difference in the lives of our patients, communities and care teams,” noted Allina Health President and CEO Lisa Shannon, who would also maintain those titles in regard to the to-be-formed Upper Midwest Division. “As one nationally leading, locally committed nonprofit health system, we will be uniquely positioned to be at the forefront of innovation, building upon the expertise of our physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses and team members to chart a upcoming path for healthcare.”.

Twenty-seven-hospital Sutter is the larger of the two organizations, with $19.8 billion reported total revenue and a $509 million operating income in 2025 (excluding impacts of the to-be-approved 2025 Hospital Fee Program). In the past year, it opened 31 additional care sites, added more than 1,100 physicians and reached 3.6 million patients.

Allina reports $6 billion of revenue with a $95.4 million operating loss and has not had a positive operating margin for the past few years. It operates 12 hospitals and more than 100 other sites.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • General Motors issued another recall intended to address temporary loss of braking in several of its Ultium-platform models late last month, and now we know the problem plagues 2024 Acura ZDXs, too.
  • According to recent reports, the temporary loss of braking only arises under very specific conditions, and it corrects itself after the driver releases the brake pedal and presses it again, but any loss of braking is a scary and dangerous situation.
  • Recent findings suggest that as with the GM recall, the only time the Acura ZDX's temporary loss of braking occurs is under very specific circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

General Motors issued another recall intended to address temporary loss of braking in several of its Ultium-platform models late last month, and now we know the problem plagues 2024 Acura ZDXs, too. You're forgiven if you forgot about the brief existence of the Acura ZDX EV, so allow me to refresh your memory. The ZDX was Acura's first EV, and beneath its sharp and aggressive exterior it was based on the Chevrolet Blazer EV, sharing that crossover's powertrain and technology. According to the NHTSA Recall Report, 14,648 all-wheel-drive 2024 Acura ZDXs need a software upgrade to correct the same temporary loss of braking matter plaguing GM's EVs. Rear-wheel-drive ZDXs are not affected by the recall.

According to recent reports, the temporary loss of braking only arises under very specific conditions, and it corrects itself after the driver releases the brake pedal and presses it again, but any loss of braking is a scary and dangerous situation. In GM's recall of over 67,000 EVs, it was aware of 20 minor accidents due to the fault, two of which resulted in minor injuries; Honda is unaware of any warranty claims or injuries related to the recall.

Recent findings suggest that as with the GM recall, the only time the Acura ZDX's temporary loss of braking occurs is under very specific circumstances. According to the recall report, "the software logic used to calculate vehicle reference speed (Vref) may become unstable when wheel slip associated with turning and light braking occurs together with travel over a road disturbance and release/reapplication of the brake pedal. On a high-friction surface, the unstable calculation may incorrectly determine that the wheels are in deep slip and command an inappropriate reduction in brake pressure.".

To fix the condition, Honda will upgrade the Electronic Brake Control Module software. Owners who have accepted the terms and conditions to accept over-the-air (OTA) software updates can download the updated software remotely, but all owners can take their ZDX to the Acura dealership to have the update installed, too.

I attended the first drive event of the Acura ZDX Type S back in 2024, and I wasn't the biggest fan of the car. It drove fine, but the interior didn't feel any more upscale than the much cheaper Blazer EV, and considering that Acura canceled the model after just one year on sale, I expected sales numbers to be much lower. Check out NHTSA's website for more recall information.

The Rising Tide Of Distributed Energy Resources

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1123 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that centralized power plants can trip widespread brownouts or blackouts when under stress.
  • DERs first surfaced on the CleanTechnica radar in the early 2000’s during the Obama administration, when the US Department of Energy began promoting decentralized, home-and community-based energy resources as the leading characteristic of a modernized and more resilient electricity grid.
  • Nowadays the DERs field embraces practically any non-centralized power generation resource, regardless of size or type.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that centralized power plants can trip widespread brownouts or blackouts when under stress. They make fat targets for enemy weapons, too. In contrast, distributed energy resources (DERs for short) can improve overall resiliency in the face of both natural and human-made disasters, while also enabling ratepayers to take advantage of utility discounts, and even earn revenue from their personal energy assets. The DERs field includes — but is not limited to — rooftop solar, EV charging stations, and home batteries. And, we ain’t seen nothing yet. DERs stakeholders have also begun moving into the distributed computing field as well.

DERs first surfaced on the CleanTechnica radar in the early 2000’s during the Obama administration, when the US Department of Energy began promoting decentralized, home-and community-based energy resources as the leading characteristic of a modernized and more resilient electricity grid. Made possible by the falling cost of solar, wind, and energy storage, the agency’s embrace of small-scale, localized electricity generation was a sharp contrast with the traditional emphasis on large centralized power plants for energy security (see more DERs background here).

Nowadays the DERs field embraces practically any non-centralized power generation resource, regardless of size or type. The DERs field can include, for example, a latest gas power plant commissioned to run an adjacent AI data center.

According to recent reports, to get some perspective on the journey of DERs since the early 2000’s, consider the case of the leading rooftop solar installer Sunrun. After launching in 2007, Sunrun segued into energy storage and virtual power plants, with “virtual” referring to smart grid technology that coordinates thousands of far-flung energy producing (and consuming) devices to balance supply and demand at peak periods of consumption.

For the record, Sunrun now presents itself as a storage-first firm. The company’s focus remains on renewable energy but the storage field is source-agnostic, embracing practically every energy resource on the planet.

Industry observers note that sunrun CEO Mary Powell also prefers to use “distributed” instead of “virtual” in reference to decentralized power systems, to emphasize that hardware is the foundational element. As of this month, Sunrun ranks as the biggest distributed power plant in the US, with solar and storage assets spread among 164,000 enrolled households.

Industry observers note that back in 2021, Sunrun entered into an installation partnership with the home energy management startup SPAN, known for its next-generation home electrical panels among other products, and that layed the ground work for a partnership on distributed computing systems. Earlier this year, SPAN introduced XFRA, a new product consisting of computer nodes to be staged at homes and smaller commercial spaces to form a distributed data center. The model is similar in concept to the familiar Internet-enabled citizen scientist platform, except that XFRA deploys its own nodes instead of using a participant’s personal computer.

This past September, Sunrun announced its selection as an authorized installation partner for XFRA with a focus on new home developments, aiming for gigawatt-scale distributed computing networks beginning in Texas and other selected markets. “Sunrun’s battery-plus-solar systems will maintain reliable electricity for both the homes and the XFRA compute nodes, while preventing the overloading of local distribution infrastructure—allowing SPAN to maximize node deployment.,” Sunrun explains.

“By pairing home energy generation and storage with XFRA compute nodes, we are unlocking fresh economic value for our customers and for Sunrun, while also solving certain speed-to-power constraints that would otherwise limit AI deployment,” Sunrun CEO Mary Powell elaborated in a press statement.

Arch Rao, founder and CEO of SPAN, also chipped in his two cents. “We can now drastically increase our penetration of XFRA compute nodes by pairing them with Sunrun energy systems to deliver cost-effective AI compute capacity at unprecedented speed while also reducing compute cost for certain AI applications,” Rao mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that back when the Energy Department initially began promoting DERs as a function of the energy transition, the agency used the term “prosumer” to describe ratepayers who are empowered to engage with their local power grid as a renewable energy producer, not simply as a passive consumer. The distributed data center adds another layer of engagement to the prosumer mix.

At a personal appearance during Climate Week in New York City in September, Powell referenced distributed computing as the latest demonstration of the company’s ongoing dialog with its customers and other stakeholders, leading to innovative new products that put more power management tools in the hands of ratepayers.

Powell reiterated the point during an appearance at the 2026 “DERVOS” summit at the Brooklyn Navy Yard on November 5, and the DERVOS gathering itself provides further insights into the widening scope of DERs activity.

Sources indicate that “DERVOS” is a play on Davos, which is shorthand for the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum. Like the World Economic Forum, DERs stakeholders have emerged in force upon the global economy as well as here in the US, stretching far from its do-it-yourself roots in the off-gridder movement of the 1970’s.

According to recent reports, the event itself is the brainchild of the collaborative trade organization DER Task Force. The group formally released in 2019 but it claims roots much earlier, in the 1970’s-era Fresh York City activist organization Energy Task Force, whose activities were highlighted by the installation of a wind turbine in the city — illegally, of course.

By the time DERVOS 2026 rolled around, the DER Task Force had become an organization with a reach far beyond Newly introduced York, and it has also embraced the size-doesn’t-matter ethos  under the slogan, “Everything is DER.”.

“That’s what we mean by Everything is DER: not that everything is small, or even literally ‘distributed,’ but that the center of gravity is shifting toward energy resources that are closer to load and controlled by those who need the power,” the Task Force explains (emphasis theirs).

“Sometimes that shift is bottoms-up, sometimes it’s centrally planned, but either way, DERs aren’t the sideshow anymore. They’re the main event,” they add.

Sources indicate that I’ll have much more to report from DERVOS 2026 in the coming days and weeks, but for the time being let’s go back to the foundational idea of improving grid resiliency and security. Climate change aside, in recent years Russia and the US have both provided textbook cases for transitioning out of energy systems that involve building fat, juicy infrastructure targets for attack, alongside precariously long energy transportation systems. If you have any thoughts about that, drop a note in the comment thread.

Image: The renewable energy “prosumer” envisioned by the US Department of Energy in the early 2000’s has become the sophisticated distributed energy resources manager of today (graphic by Sara Harman courtesy of US DOE).

A Smaller Electric Land Rover Defender Is Coming In 2027

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (547 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that rumors of a smaller, electric Land Rover Defender have been swirling for quite some time now — we first reported on it three years ago — and now we're finally getting some concrete information on when we'll be seeing the compact SUV.
  • From the spy shots we've seen, the so-called Defender Sport will be quite a bit smaller than the current five-door Defender.
  • Those who are into the idea of a smaller Defender but who aren't sold on an electric drivetrain needn't worry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rumors of a smaller, electric Land Rover Defender have been swirling for quite some time now — we first reported on it three years ago — and now we're finally getting some concrete information on when we'll be seeing the compact SUV. Jaguar Land Rover CEO PB Balaji says the battery-electric Defender is set to be sold alongside the existing combustion-engine model sometime in 2027, according to Automotive News.

From the spy shots we've seen, the so-called Defender Sport will be quite a bit smaller than the current five-door Defender. We know it'll be the second model underpinned by JLR's brand-upcoming 800-volt Electrified Modular Architecture platform, the first being the Range Rover GT that should be revealed in just a couple months. When production spins up in Halewood, England, it will also mark the end of the Range Rover Evoque and Discovery Sport. The baby Defender will be powered by the same battery pack as the Range Rover GT, which JLR mentioned will have up to 450 miles of range on the European cycle, but the boxier shape of the Defender will certainly cut down on that number.

Those who are into the idea of a smaller Defender but who aren't sold on an electric drivetrain needn't worry. Like the GT, the Defender EV is being developed with hybrid powertrain options as well. However, those buyer is going to have to wait a little while, because the hybrids aren't going to be on sale until 2028 at the earliest. Balaji told AutoNews that they are "fully underway" but "won't catch next year's timelines.".

Recent findings suggest that the Defender EV is set to be JLR's fifth electric vehicle, sitting alongside the aforementioned Range Rover GT, as well as the electric versions of the full-size Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, and the Jaguar Type 01. Yes, there was also the Jaguar I-Pace, but that's long dead. While pricing for the Defender EV hasn't been revealed or hinted at yet, AutoNews expects it to be fairly close to the current Defender 110. That means both will be priced significantly above the Evoque and Discovery Sport, a clear sign that JLR is continuing its move upmarket while leaving entry-level luxury behind.

According to recent reports, the one caveat to all of this is that JLR's EV timelines have been a bit fugazi of late. The Range Rover Electric was only just officially revealed in September, two years after it was initially slated to go on sale. Keep in mind, the fifth-generation Range Rover was first revealed all the way back at the end of 2021.

This new model will be the first in a proposed series of vehicles meant to establish Defender as its own brand within Land Rover, according to Car and Driver. It's part of JLR's "House of Brands" strategy that we first told you about all the way back in 2023. I'm not sure if that's a play that'll work, but who am I to tell a brand how to run. You've got to think the Defender EV will be a solid off-roader. It has the Defender name to uphold after all. It really cannot get away with being mediocre when the going gets rough, can it?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the 2027 Dakar Rally is already set to be an unusual affair with an unexpected return to Africa as the route shifts from Saudi Arabia to Portugal and Morocco. Now, three Aston Martins will be tackling the famed cross-country rally in January. The British manufacturer revealed the Dreadnought on Tuesday, its first rally-raid machine. If that nameplate sounds familiar, the Aston Martin Dreadnought was originally a digital-only vehicle exclusively designed for "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.".

Recent findings suggest that the two-time F1 world champion won't be heading out into the desert alone. He will reunite with his previous Dakar co-driver, Marc Coma. Few competitors are as accomplished and experienced as Coma. The 50-year-old won the Dakar five times with KTM and briefly served as the rally's race director between 2016 and 2018. As a pairing, Alonso and Coma finished 13th in the 2020 Dakar Rally with Toyota. Alonso mentioned his return was driven by a desire to challenge himself. Honestly, F1 isn't much of a challenge at Aston Martin this season. The Spaniard is just trundling around, hoping to finish races. He said in a release:.

According to recent reports, "After deciding to continue racing in Formula One with the Aston Martin Aramco, I thought carefully about Dakar. In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula One and the Dakar Rally in the same year.".

According to recent reports, the version of the Aston Martin Dreadnought won't feature a carbon-fiber chassis, military-grade armor plating or weapons storage like its Call of Duty counterpart. This Dreadnought is based on the Prodrive-designed Dacia Sandrider. The machine is fitted with the same three-liter, twin-turbocharged Nissan engine. The starkest difference is the bodywork, styled after the digital-only combat SUV, most evident in the square headlights and the louvered rear window.

In a recent development, the Prodrive-run effort will also include another usual suspect at the wheel of a Dreadnought: Nine-time World Rally Champion Sébastien Loeb. The living legend has never won the Dakar Rally, but has finished second on three occasions. The third Dreadnought will be driven by Lucas Moraes. The Brazilian joined the Dacia-Prodrive effort after winning the World Rally-Raid Championship with Toyota in 2025. The vehicle's origin may seem ridiculous, but Aston Martin has a legitimate chance of winning the Dakar in January. Prodrive is the returning winner after Nasser Al-Attiyah took the 2026 victory in a Dacia Sandrider.

Breaking: BYD E6Y Odyssey

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A couple of friends embark on a road trip to pick their EV purchase, and it turns into an Odyssey.
  • Globe-trotting friends have ridden in them as taxis in Singapore.
  • According to recent reports, joanne told me that she had been looking for an EV for two years when a search on carsales.com found an ad for an E6Y (the taxi version of the BYD E6).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A couple of friends embark on a road trip to pick their EV purchase, and it turns into an Odyssey.

The BYD E6 is a BEV classic. Globe-trotting friends have ridden in them as taxis in Singapore. Majella and I even took one for a test drive (it reminded me of a ’70s Chrysler Valiant). It was the best selling pure electric car in China in 2016, with about 600,000 sold globally, and it is viewed by many as ahead of its time. So, when one revealed up at our coffee and cake morning tea, I had to interview the owner, Joanne, and her road trip friend, Meredith. What they shared with me was truly an odyssey of determination to get Jo’s car home. Please note: this story took place 6 years ago. Charging availability has improved and so has Joanne’s knowledge of living with an electric vehicle.

According to recent reports, joanne told me that she had been looking for an EV for two years when a search on carsales.com found an ad for an E6Y (the taxi version of the BYD E6). It was a pre-COVID import and had been mothballed at Sydney airport after the company importing the vehicles had decided not to go ahead with taxis. Photos of all the BYDs at the airport were widely circulated as evidence that no one wanted to buy an EV. The cars were being “sold by a mate out of the back of the factory.” At the low cost of AU$32,000, claiming a 400 km range from its 83-kWh battery and only 100 km on the odometer, Joanne saw it as a bargain.

There was some consideration of putting the car on a flatbed and having it shipped, but in the end, the two friends decided on a road trip.

Jo informs me that: “They only brought 120 of the BYD E6Y taxi versions into the country. BYD sold some GLX versions, which had more bells and whistles.”.

In a recent development, she was soon to find out that all is not as it seems. Her lack of knowledge of EVs meant that her trip in the car from Sydney back to Brisbane would be an odyssey of Greek tragedy proportions. Jo reminisces: “Meredith reminded me our original proposal had been to spend just two days driving back to Brisbane with the one overnight stay. I thought I could ‘fast charge’ the car and make it back to Brisvegas on the second day. Hahahaha. Lesson learned the hard way.” They expected it to be just a twelve-hour trip. Meredith adds, “I told her we would laugh about it one day.”.

Industry observers note that joanne contacted the seller and planned her flight to Sydney. Meredith got excited and joined the “road trip” in Newcastle. Jo paid the money and took ownership of the car. “It took two hours to get out of Sydney.” To be fair, that wasn’t the car’s fault — just Sydney’s congested traffic. However, the fact that the previous owner had only charged the car to 50% didn’t help. She was able to charge the car to 80% on the outskirts of Sydney. “But I had no idea that I wouldn’t get the expected range at highway speeds.”.

According to recent reports, another learning curve was the state of charging points — sure, there were plenty listed on PlugShare, but many were unavailable or broken. Again, dear reader, I must emphasize this was 6 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that her next planned stop was accommodation she had booked at Newcastle. She got to within 2 km when the battery readout said “zero.” She was unable to find a place to charge — the car had not come with a granny charger. Jo clarified her Newcastle experience by email: “the Uni in Newcastle was the first I tried to charge. My friend Meredith and I tried three other places to charge all with no luck. I found out later that the Newcastle chargers were notorious for not working.” She confided to me that she now knows that the car can go a little further even when it says zero battery. She also had to learn the difference between AC and DC charging. The BYD she had bought could only handle AC charging.

With the battery reading zero, she felt she had no choice but to leave the car at a nearby garage. The owner of the accommodation she had booked kindly came and picked her and her friend up. The next day, the BNB owner dropped them back to the garage and a tow truck was ordered. The tow truck took them and their car to a local winery where they trickle charged next to the golf carts. The winery also had a Tesla level 2 charger for customer use. It was charging when they arrived. “We left a note on the windscreen of the Tesla that was using the level 2. During breakfast the Tesla owner rang and said the charger was available. We left the winery fully charged and off up the highway.” Not a bad place to get stuck, methinks.

Industry observers note that 280 km up the road to Kempsie, there was access to free charging in the council carpark, but no available accommodation! That’s what happens when you travel on the Queen’s Birthday long weekend. “We were checking out the back seat of the car as a place to sleep when a friend of a friend told them he had a farm in area. ‘Have I got a place for you!’ he told them. After we finished charging, we had to drive down this dark farm track. We couldn’t plug the car in because we still didn’t have a granny charger!” They made themselves comfortable in the available beds in the barn. The next morning in the light of day they found they had driven alongside of a lagoon! “We could have easily driven into that!”.

Meredith adds: “I didn’t think I’d be sleeping in a shed with a tractor and then I couldn’t sleep because of the smell of diesel.” The trip was not just a challenge, but torture.

According to recent reports, their next adventure was just a few kilometers up the road at Gladstone NSW. Low on juice, they contacted people through PlugShare and got a message from a local café owner. You can check out the café here. He already owned a Hyundai Ioniq, and so had a granny charger to lend. The café owner knew a fellow who was visiting his mum in town. This friend had ordered an Atto 3 from BYD and was waiting on this first shipment of BYDs to arrive. Jo took him for a ride around town in her car. “This was his first ride in a BYD.”.

Recent findings suggest that he arranged for them to leave their car at his mother’s home in the next town (Smithtown). Jo and her friend were now in a hurry, as both had to get back to Brisbane to go to work the next day. Leaving the car charging, “We belted back to Brisbane in this horrible little roller skate hire car.” Home in Brisbane, Jo had to strategy how to retrieve her BYD purchase. Meredith did not want another “road trip.”.

This time, Jo travelled south by train. Even this trip was not without drama. She missed her stop. Thankfully, she was able to get off at the next stop and change to the northbound train to make it back to where her car waited faithfully for her. She took a taxi to her car, returned the borrowed granny charger, and began her journey home. She was so keen that she ended up with a speeding ticket.

Industry observers note that joanne arrived at her motel in Balina with 10 km of range showing on the dashboard. But the available ocular charger soon filled up the car. By 9:00 pm, with a full battery, she couldn’t wait to go home. The fireworks display in town was a fitting sendoff for the final leg of her journey.

Jo would like to acknowledge all the good advice and offers of help she received from fellow people of PlugShare, as well as all those referred to above. She is now a confident and competent driver of her BYD E6Y and has made many trips back and forth to Sydney from Brisbane with less drama. The BYD E6Y Facebook group has been a great help. She says she would not part with her green E6Y Singapore taxi — “a comfortable and solid basic car.” Rumour has it that there are about 250 on Australian roads, with the record distance travelled over 1 million km.

Another owner commented: “This unstoppable tank will outlive me I’m sure, best of all its super basic … no internet, no lane assist, no self-driving and plenty of fresh and used cheap parts available. This is why it seems like there are so few … they are so good NO ONE who has one is selling them.”.

It has been revealed that jo has even taken her car camping. “The camping trip was to Yandina up the coast. I did sleep in the back of the car on that trip very comfortably. But that time I had a mattress and bedding. I did take out the bottom half of the back seat from the car so I could get a completely flat rear area for the mattress. When I returned from the camping trip, I popped the rear seat bottom back in the car. It’s just two bolts and a couple of plastic clips that hold it in.”.

And in the future, I asked? “It will be hard to part with my E6. I am waiting on the first solid state 1000km BEVs before I would consider parting with it. I just love the two-tone paint job.”.

In a recent development, jo is another happy battery electric vehicle owner, sharing her learning experience “odyssey” and having fun. “Thanks for the opportunity to immortalise the odyssey,” she told me in her latest email. The future is bright and electric as we learn to live with our new vehicles.

Latest Update: Hammerspace enters the hardware market with newly introduced storage and intelligence capabilities

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hammerspace Inc., which provides high-speed access to distributed data, is expanding beyond its traditional role as a software provider to offer complete, integrated data systems for artificial intelligence workloads, adding its own high-performance flash storage hardware and latest data intelligence capabilities to its existing data orchestration platform.
  • Industry observers note that the tech giant mentioned the Hammerspace Data System combines data discovery, management, orchestration and storage into a single offering designed to simplify the infrastructure needed to support AI training and inference.
  • The announcement marks a significant expansion of Hammerspace’s business model as enterprises increasingly seek turnkey infrastructure for AI applications rather than assembling systems from multiple vendors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:00 EST / NOVEMBER 17 2026.

Hammerspace Inc., which provides high-speed access to distributed data, is expanding beyond its traditional role as a software provider to offer complete, integrated data systems for artificial intelligence workloads, adding its own high-performance flash storage hardware and latest data intelligence capabilities to its existing data orchestration platform.

Industry observers note that the tech giant mentioned the Hammerspace Data System combines data discovery, management, orchestration and storage into a single offering designed to simplify the infrastructure needed to support AI training and inference. Customers can purchase fully configured systems with hardware, software and support or continue deploying Hammerspace software on existing infrastructure.

The announcement marks a significant expansion of Hammerspace’s business model as enterprises increasingly seek turnkey infrastructure for AI applications rather than assembling systems from multiple vendors.

“We also see plenty of opportunities, particularly in the AI space, where they just want one [stock-keeping unit],” noted Floyd Christofferson, vice president of product marketing at Hammerspace. “They want a system, end-to-end, hardware, software, fully integrated and supported.”.

While software companies have historically had limited success expanding into hardware, Hammerspace’s approach is more than just a bundled, remarked Mark Nossokoff, research directory at Hyperior Research Holdings LLC.

“Hammerspace is working with distribution partners to develop and fulfill a branded system optimized for their software stack, maintaining their software business model,” he stated in e-mailed comments. “This can be advantageous when the hardware is based on an emerging standards-based platform, such as the Open Flash Platform, until the hardware platform becomes a standard offering from multiple suppliers.”.

Recent findings suggest that hammerspace has traditionally specialized in providing unified access to data distributed across different storage systems, data centers and clouds. Its software creates a global namespace that allows applications to locate and access files regardless of their physical location, eliminating the need for large-scale data migrations.

It has been revealed that in March, the company introduced an AI-focused data platform that automates the discovery and delivery of enterprise data directly to graphics processing units. The technology builds on Hammerspace’s parallel Network File System, which uses enhancements to Linux to accelerate data access without requiring proprietary client software.

The upcoming offering extends those capabilities with integrated hardware and data intelligence.

A major addition is the Hammerspace Open Flash Platform, a high-density storage system built around data processing units rather than conventional storage servers. The architecture integrates processing, networking and solid-state drives into compact hardware designed to reduce power consumption, cooling requirements and rack space.

Hammerspace remarked the platform achieves throughput of 350 gigabytes per second per rack unit. Broader performance testing is still underway.

In a recent development, the storage complements the firm’s existing Tier 0 technology, which aggregates local Non-Volatile Memory Express storage across GPU servers into a shared resource. That capacity can be used to store key-value caches for AI inference, allowing applications to reuse previously computed context rather than repeatedly processing the same information.

It has been revealed that “The flash subsystem employs a unique design and touts some impressive performance and storage density metrics,” said Hyperion’s Nossokoff. “More compelling will be results based on end user workloads, including relative improvements and comparisons with respect to performance, performance/power, and cost/performance metrics, among others.”.

Sources indicate that the firm remarked customers can combine tier 0 storage, the upcoming flash platform and lower-cost disk or object storage within a single namespace. The new hardware is optional. Customers can continue using third-party storage systems, with Hammerspace handling data access and orchestration across the infrastructure.

Another addition is a data intelligence module that extends Hammerspace’s existing metadata management capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that the software can catalog distributed files, index detailed metadata and scan content to identify sensitive information, including personally identifiable information and regulated data. Consumers can search the catalog using natural language and translate requests into automated data management policies.

For example, an administrator could identify files containing personal information and establish policies preventing that material from entering an AI training pipeline.

Christofferson mentioned the new capabilities extend beyond the file attributes traditionally used to manage storage.

The module also supports integration with existing enterprise catalogs and governance tools through application programming interfaces, avoiding the need to replace established systems.

For current Hammerspace customers, the intelligence capabilities will be added through a software upgrade. The company said existing deployments won’t need to change their underlying architecture.

Hammerspace will assemble, install and support systems using configurable server hardware, metadata nodes and storage components based on customer requirements. The manufacturer will continue basing software pricing on the capacity of data under management. Hardware configurations will be priced individually, with no standardized public price list.

Senior Product Marketing Director Eric Bassier stated the firm doesn’t intend to collect hardware revenue or impose a hardware markup. Instead, components will flow through suppliers and distribution partners, while Hammerspace provides integrated deployment and support.

The strategy addresses the struggles customers often encounter with the logistics of acquiring servers, storage and other components, noted Molly Presley, senior vice president of global marketing.

“They’re looking to their vendors to simplify getting things deployed to start with,” he stated. “As long as Hammerspace doesn’t dilute their resources and continues to prioritize their investments on addressing the needs of the growing scientific and engineering communities adopting AI into their advanced technical workflows, they appear well poised for continued momentum.”.

Nossokoff stated Hammerspace’s distributed data architecture using a global namespace is well suited to emerging AI workload requirements. “Hammerspace has been building out their Data Intelligence software stack to address the requirements of the AI pipeline,” he said. The expansion follows a $100 million funding round in April 2025 that supported Hammerspace’s international expansion. The firm says its customers include Meta Platforms Inc. and the U.S. Department of Defense.
