📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crown City Solar will be North America’s first floating community solar project. Phases 1 and 2 are under construction, and the three-phase, 22.5 MW DC complex is expected to be fully operational in 2027.

CORTLANDVILLE, N.Y. — Third Pillar Power today announced it is constructing Crown City Solar, North America’s first floating community solar project, at Suit-Kote Corporation’s Polkville Crushed Stone Facility, an active sand and gravel mining operation co-located with an asphalt plant and storage terminal in Cortlandville, N.Y.

Crown City Solar 1 is the first of three 7.5 MW-dc phases and is expected to begin commercial operation in February 2027. Crown City Solar 2 and Crown City Solar 3 are scheduled to begin commercial operation in October 2027, bringing the site to 22.5 MW-dc in total and making Crown City Solar North America’s largest floating solar complex. The complex takes its name from nearby Cortland, known locally as the Crown City because it sits on an elevated plain over 1,000 feet above sea level.

“Every quarry and reservoir in this country already has a job to do. Crown City Solar indicates that those sites can take on a second one: powering their neighbors through a Central Fresh York winter, at a community scale, on a working industrial site. The question is no longer whether floating solar works here. It’s how quickly we can bring it to the next site, like Polkville, and the one after that,” mentioned Jaimeet Gulati, CEO of Third Pillar Power.

According to recent reports, third Pillar identified the approximately 120-acre flooded mine pit as an ideal host for the project in early 2024. Thanks to the collaborative efforts of Suit-Kote, the Town of Cortlandville, and Cortland County, the project team brought this first-of-its-kind project to construction less than two years after securing site control and applying for interconnection. Suit-Kote was acquired by Colas USA, the U.S. subsidiary of Colas, in October 2026.

Recent findings suggest that crown City Solar also represents a series of technical firsts. It is engineered for the conditions of a Central Latest York winter, including a ground snow load of 69 pounds per square foot, the highest of any floating solar project in the country. Additionally, the project will float its medium-voltage transformers and switchgear on custom-designed barges—another first for a U.S. floating solar project. Floating this equipment further reduces the use of agricultural land, addresses floodplain siting concerns, and improves electrical efficiency. These firsts reflect Third Pillar’s specialization in floating solar, from identifying and engineering projects on working industrial water bodies to securing the permits and interconnection needed to bring them online.

D3Energy is serving as the engineering, procurement, and construction contractor. The floating system uses Alps’ Solar PV modules, Hazelett Marine’s specialized elastic mooring systems, and Profloating’s floats.

“With more than a decade of building floating solar projects across the country, D3Energy is proud to bring that experience to a project of this magnitude. Crown City Solar demonstrates what is possible with floating solar. We’re grateful for our partnership with Third Pillar Power and the trust they’ve placed in D3Energy to help bring North America’s largest floating solar complex to life,” said Stetson Tchividjian, Managing Director of D3Energy.

Crown City Solar 1 is expected to achieve mechanical completion in December 2026.

#30075. 7 Engine Swaps Where The Exhaust Note Will Make You Do A Double Take

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1962 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

7 Engine Swaps Where The Exhaust Note Will Make You Do A Double Take

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A lot of really cool cars come straight out of the factory, but for those who want something truly unique, or just love a bizarre challenge, an obscure engine swap is often the best direction in which to head.
  • It has been revealed that the list is full of engine swaps which we love, purely because they wind up giving the base car an exhaust note that nobody would ever expect.
  • Before you race to the comments to point out all the cool swaps we have missed, it's also worth mentioning that we paid particularly close attention to projects which, from the outside at least, looked largely stock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A lot of really cool cars come straight out of the factory, but for those who want something truly unique, or just love a bizarre challenge, an obscure engine swap is often the best direction in which to head. Now, here at Jalopnik we've covered no end of awesome conversions in the past, including documenting your dream engine swaps, but this list focuses on something a little more specific.

It has been revealed that the list is full of engine swaps which we love, purely because they wind up giving the base car an exhaust note that nobody would ever expect. Included among the 7 is a VR6-swapped Porsche 911 with more than 1,000 horsepower, and a Korean city car with a GM-sourced V6 wedged under the smallest hood imaginable. And to prove our point, each feature engine swap is accompanied with a video to demonstrate just how absurd these swaps are.

Before you race to the comments to point out all the cool swaps we have missed, it's also worth mentioning that we paid particularly close attention to projects which, from the outside at least, looked largely stock. Or, if not stock, at least they weren't giving the secret away. So, no superchargers protruding through hoods here, or turbos masquerading as headlights. In no particular order, these are 7 of the most double-take-worthy engine swaps we found, kicking things off with a Ferrari-powered DeLorean that sure would have given Doc Brown a far easier time in cracking that 88 mph threshold in the "Back To The Future" films.

In a recent development, almost everything about the factory-original DeLorean is awe-inspiring. The brushed stainless steel bodywork, the rakish lines, and, of course, the silver-screen connection that immortalized the model forever as Doc Brown's time machine. However, its 130-hp 2.8-liter V6 has always been a source of disappointment in the eyes of many. Put simply, the DeLorean always deserved better.

According to recent reports, A firm by the name of FuelTech took it upon themselves to address this concern. This particular vehicle did not have an engine when they found it, but it would have been powered by a PRV (Peugeot-Renault-Volvo) engine. Instead of settling for the original engine, they put in a far more exotic 4.3-liter V8. The mill itself was sourced from a Ferrari California, and delivers 453 horsepower, alongside 358 pound-feet of torque. The soundtrack that now echoes from the DeLorean's rear-end is nothing like what bystanders might expect.

Helping to distribute that power is a six-speed Tiptronic transmission, pinched from a Porsche 911. A KW kit addressed any and all suspension-related concerns, while a larger brake kit was also understandably called upon. The DeLorean isn't a car which usually sees such in-depth modification, with most owners choosing to keep them entirely stock, or to turn them into time machine replicas. However, this particular example was purchased by FuelTech in a sorry state, with no engine and needing much work, so it's perhaps not the purist's nightmare many might first assume.

One of the wildest Cummins swaps out there is this 4BT-swapped Toyota Prius. The Toyota would have started life with a 1.5-liter inline-four hybrid system, but that — along with the entire interior and a whole heap of metalwork — has been entirely stripped out. In its place, owner Ben Schulz dropped in a turbocharged 3.9-liter inline-four diesel Cummins engine, which dynoed at 360 hhp and 550 lb-ft of torque.

Schulz states a TDI engine and front-wheel drive was at least lightly considered at one point, but instead, the Cummins and rear-wheel drive swap idea was too good to ignore. Hearing a high-capacity turbo diesel 4-cylinder thundering down the road, which is traditionally more at home in construction vehicles, but then seeing a Prius emerging through a thick cloud of black smoke must be one of the most double-take-worthy engine swaps of all time — it's a wild swap, that's for sure.

Remarkably, the car still looks fairly standard from the outside; even the standard rear wheels were widened rather than replaced, in order to retain that factory look. Future looks include refitting as much of the original interior as possible, which should further boost the sleeper appeal of this coal-rolling Toyota.

The Chevrolet Corvette hasn't always sported a V8 engine. In fact, the first Corvettes arrived with the Blue Flame inline-six engine under their hoods, but for certain, there has never been a factory four-cylinder Corvette. However, some engineers from Unruly Motorsports decided to build exactly that, swapping a C6 Corvette's 6.0-liter LS2 out for a turbocharged four-cylinder Honda K24.

According to recent reports, in its stock guise, the C6 Corvette produces a healthy 400 hp, but the minds behind this K24 build had their sights set an awful lot higher. Before dropping this particular K24 into the Corvette, it managed to make an impressive 828 horsepower on 20 pounds of boost. It boasts forged internals, a closed deck, and a 67mm turbocharger with ceramic ball bearings, and interestingly enough, it's hooked up to a built 2-speed Powerglide transmission. Once setup in the C6, Unruly Motorsports managed to see a peak of 917 hp on the dyno, alongside 563 lb-ft of torque.

This swap wasn't carried out just to annoy the purists, although no doubt it probably has upset a few of them. Instead, it was built to perform, and with it churning out quarter-mile passes in the very low 11-second range, it certainly does exactly that. All while turning more heads than most silver drop-top C6 Corvettes, thanks mostly to that most curious and un-GM-like four-pot soundtrack.

People have been swapping all sorts of engines into Miatas for a while now. We've seen 800-horsepower and 10,000 rpm K24-powered Miatas, and even motorcycle engine-swapped Miatas, and while those will both sound distinctly different from standard models, it's this Volvo-motivated Miata which has our interests piqued today.

It has been revealed that apart from a few curious graphics, this first-generation Miata looks pretty stock. It's passable for just another cheap project car, the type which are spotted fairly commonly. However, beneath the factory hood lies a B2544T engine, which belongs to the T5 family. In short, 2.4 liters, 5 cylinders, one turbocharger, a goal of between 300 and 400 horsepower, and a Miata.

Sources indicate that plans were originally made for a T6 engine to slot under the hood, but the T5 would fit into the available space easier. For our purposes, it suits too, as while a boosted inline-six does sound cool, the T5 boasts a particularly distinctive sound.

Recent findings suggest that the engine is hooked up to a manual 6-speed transmission plucked from a BMW 1 Series, which the owners notes was chosen due to its ability to handle an awful lot of torque. The real joy of a swap like this is that it demonstrates how creativity trumps funds. Mating a cheap Miata to a junkyard Volvo motor and coupling that with an old BMW transmission is just as cool as any other swap on this list.

We've looked at this 6.2-liter LS3-powered Tesla in the past, but it certainly deserves a spot on this list too. Popular automotive YouTuber Rich Rebuilds took what was a flood-damaged Tesla Model S and mated its body with the LS3 out of a Chevrolet Camaro, while at the same time making every effort to keep it looking relatively stock from the outside. A vinyl wrap was chosen for the finished product, though, in a rather unflattering brownish color, until you realize it plays on the car's "ICE-T" nickname, which cleverly combines ICE (internal combustion engine) with T, for Tesla.

That's why, when the key is turned and that thunderous V8 soundtrack booms out of the Tesla's side-exit exhaust pipe, it's absolutely one of those engine swaps that will give bystanders cause to stop what they are doing and give this former-EV a double take.

The team dropped the LS3 into the Tesla's frunk and mated it with a sequential 6-speed manual transmission, which itself was routed through a custom-made transmission tunnel. It wound up making around 440 horsepower, and bizarrely garnered the YouTuber a lot of hate online. Remember, this was a flood-damaged car; he essentially saved it from the junkyard. After the build's completion, the V8 Tesla was passed around various YouTubers before ending up back with Rich some 5 years later. The car returned to him with numerous updates, most notably a Magnuson supercharger, in addition to a heap of concerns, so it will be interesting to see how the V8-swapped Tesla's life continues from this point forward.

The Porsche 911 996 Turbo is already a powerful car, producing 415 hp and 413 lb-ft of torque as standard from its Mezger 3.6-liter flat-six engine. That engine is also really quite susceptible to tuning, with kits available from Speed Density Motorsports that can send that standard output soaring close to and even north of 1,000 horsepower.

However, Speed Density Motorsports found a way of delivering up to 1,500 horsepower from the 996 Turbo platform, but its method of securing such a figure is a little unconventional. For this, the flat-six was removed entirely, and a 3.2-liter VR6 engine – the same engine which has been doing the rounds in Volkswagen cars for over 30 years now — was dropped back into the space instead, albeit now with a wild state of tune. The engine, 3.3 liters, with billet aluminum and forged internals was installed, and a Precision 8565 ball-bearing turbocharger was fitted. Everything is upcoming and high-end; this is a 1,500-horsepower VR6 running on methanol fuel, after all.

Footage of the outfit's Stage 4-equipped shop car, with Stage 4 being detailed as a 3.2-liter VR6-swapped single turbo build capable of cracking 1,300 horsepower on E85, shows off the unusual and aggressive exhaust note thrown out the back of this once flat-six-motivated 996. This particular generation of 911 has been the subject of other curious engine swaps in the past, but the iconic warble of a VR6 has to be the best candidate yet from a soundtrack perspective.

There aren't that many reasons to celebrate the achievements of Daewoo, certainly not from an enthusiastic perspective. The Matiz was a diminutive little four-door hatchback produced by the Korean firm from the late '90s onward, until GM purchased the automaker and production carried on as the Chevrolet Matiz. Eventually, the Spark would replace the nameplate.

As standard, a 52-horsepower 0.8-liter inline-three powered the little Matiz. It was never a performer, instead prioritizing cheapness, as most Daewoo cars did. However, one man — bored of engine-swapping Vauxhalls — decided to make a humble one-owner Matiz the subject of a seriously cool engine swap. The brief was simply to place the biggest engine possible into the smallest car available.

It has been revealed that the engine in question was a naturally aspirated 3.2-liter V6 from a Vauxhall Vectra, which kicks out 208 horsepower and 221 lb-ft of torque, in addition to a sensationally unusual engine note for this dinky little city-dweller. Nothing to shout about, but considering a standard Matiz weighs only 1,711 pounds, the power-to-weight ratio is really quite impressive. It was understandably a tight fit under the Matiz' tiny hood, but with custom engine mounts and a modified intake manifold, the builder squeezed it in while still retaining the factory airbox.

According to recent reports, ample stopping power comes from a custom substantial brake kit on the front consisting of Focus RS rotors and Lancer Evolution VI calipers, which sit behind 18-inch Porsche alloys. A lightened flywheel and limited-slip differential make the most of the V6's power, and — aside from a Vauxhall gear-shifter — the interior has been kept entirely stock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Fierce Healthcare Fundraising Tracker '26: Aevius introduces with $22M for clinical insights; Abby Care secures $82M for family-led care" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

At Fierce Healthcare, we keep track of all the venture capital being funneled into the health tech and digital health industries.

Our fundraising tracker provides updated coverage of noteworthy digital health and health tech funding rounds, though we'll still profile exciting new companies and larger rounds that catch our eye in depth.

Do you have fundraising news to share? Email Heather Landi at [email protected].

Sources indicate that oct. 17—AeviusClinical intelligence AI modelsSeries: N/AAmount: $22 millionInvestors: Led by Insight Partners.

Aevius is a newly released Mass General Brigham spinout founded by veterans of AstreaZeneca-acquired Modella AI. The organization builds models that intake different forms of medical data to paint a multimodal picture of a patient's current state and trajectory. That information can then be used by healthcare, payer and life sciences organizations for potential application in care delivery, operational decision-making and clinical research.

Sources indicate that “Our mission is to make medicine computable,” Rowland Pettit, M.D., Ph.D., co-founder and CEO of Aevius, said. “As a physician-scientist, I’ve worked across many types of clinical data, and there is far more knowledge in those records than we’re able to use today. We’re bringing general medical intelligence to that data, so organizations can build on a deeper understanding for their patients.”.

Recent findings suggest that the company said it looks to use the $22 million launch money to support continued model and product development. It also plans to expand its engineering, clinical and commercial teams, as well as to focus on commercial deployment.

Oct. 15—Abby CareFamily caregiver trainingSeries: CAmount: $82 millionInvestors: Led by Transformation Capital, along with CVS Health Ventures, Frist Cressey Ventures and Pivotal, with participation from existing investors Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital and Sequoia Capital.

Abby Care is an AI-native home care startup that equips family caregivers with professional training, certification and ongoing support from dedicated RN care managers. The firm works with health aims to arrange care at home for families that need it. Abby Care's platform also gives care teams real-time visibility into care delivered in the home, helping ensure families receive the support they need while enabling health plans to verify that care is being provided. Fortune reported the series C round.

Sources indicate that the U.S. faces a major healthcare workforce shortage along with a rapidly aging population, and waitlists of vulnerable children needing care, noted Havi Nguyen, founder of Abby Care in a LinkedIn post."Family caregivers already know their loved ones best and are in the home. They’re the first to notice when something isn’t right. At Abby, we equip family caregivers with training, AI, and support from our clinicians to deliver quality care. Our platform enables real-time capture of care data in the home. Health plans and states deserve visibility and confidence that care is delivered as intended. Better care and program integrity go together," Nguyen wrote.

Abby Care functions as a Medicaid provider to pay caregivers within Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Massachusetts, Fresh Jersey, Pennsylvania and Tennessee.

So far, Abby Care has helped families deliver millions of hours of care across many states, the firm's members had 40%+ fewer reported hospitalizations in year one, she wrote.

Today, the organization serves thousands of families across eight states, with additional markets expected to launch soon, executives remarked.

The funding will enable the manufacturer to bring its model to more families, deepen its work with health plans and continue building technology and clinical infrastructure, the company stated in a blog post.

Oct. 14—AllswellBehavioral health for LGBTQ+Series: Seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Rethink Impact, Magnify Ventures, Ulu Ventures and Hopelab Ventures, Techstars and Amboy Street Ventures.

Allswell offers one-on-one virtual therapy, group programs and trauma-informed care to LGBTQ+ patients. It is in-network with commercial and Medicaid payers. The startup, released in 2025, looks to use the capital to expand beyond its DMV-area footprint, build out its clinical training program for therapists and launch psychiatric medication management next year.

"Nobody realizes how big this market is. Only 5% of Gen X identifies as LGBTQ+, compared with 25% of Gen Z. That's a massive generational and cultural shift, and we want to do for LGBTQ+ health what Midi did for menopause," Heidi Patel, managing partner at Rethink Impact, mentioned in a press release.

Industry observers note that allswell's therapeutic models were built for patients navigating depression and anxiety, identity-specific trauma, family dynamics and social transition. It is also developing its own curriculum on PTSD and trauma care.

It has been revealed that the startup, though new, is already seeing positive outcomes. The manufacturer often keeps patients for over a year, rare for behavioral health. In its most recent cohorts, 77% indicated improvements in anxiety and 71% showed improvements in depression after 60 days of treatment.

Industry observers note that "Our patients aren't used to being served with care and respect, or to having something built for them. ... This is a sleeping-giant category, and it has been underestimated at every step. Our ambition is to continue developing upcoming, thoughtful clinical programs specifically for the LGBTQ+ community, regardless of the political climate," Dawn Androphy, co-founder and CEO of Allswell, said in an announcement.

It has been revealed that oct. 14—ReadilyArtificial intelligence compliance platformSeries: AAmount: $11 millionInvestors: Define Ventures led the funding round, with participation from Y Combinator and the California Health Care Foundation Innovation Fund.

Sources indicate that readily’s platform connects regulatory requirements with policies, assigned actions and supporting evidence to reduce manual research and review processes. When the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) releases upcoming rules, CEO and co-founder Edward Tiong said, the platform can analyze them against existing policies and contracts “in hours,” identifying gaps and action items for teams.

The company’s work with healthcare organizations covers more than 25 million covered individuals across 46 states, according to its website. Tiong stated revenue has grown 10x. Read the full story here.

Sources indicate that oct. 14—Probably GeneticAI platform powering the research, diagnosis and treatment of genetic diseasesSeries: AAmount: $12 millionInvestors: Round led by Threshold, with participation from Y Combinator and other existing investors.

Sources indicate that the firm’s primary product is a physician-ordered genetic test for undiagnosed rare disease patients, who typically face a seven-year diagnostic odyssey before getting answers. There are two pathways to testing: free testing, through pharma partnerships, and insurance-billed testing. The free programs address specific conditions, with a limited number of tests available at a time.

Patients can check their eligibility by completing a health and diagnostic assessment online. Probably Genetic’s AI platform converts self-reported symptoms, medical records and biological data into phenotypic data that it hopes can be used to train AI models for precision medicine in the future. Thus far, it has collected data from 130,000 patients.

Probably Genetic said the fresh funds would be used to grow the core part of the business, for hiring and to enter the drug discovery arena. Read the full story here.

According to recent reports, oct. 14—AllaraVirtual women’s health providerSeries: UndisclosedAmount: $30 millionInvestors: Led by Index Ventures and GV (Google Ventures), alongside newly introduced investors Camino Partners, Foreground and Family Fund.

Allara, founded in 2020, has expanded to serve a broader continuum of women’s health. The organization aims to fill gaps in care for women often navigating an array of specialists. Each Allara patient is paired with a multidisciplinary team, including OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, registered dietitians and patient success leads.

Since its expansion nationwide last year, Allara has added urgent care visits for things like UTIs, bacterial vaginosis (BV) and STDs, and brought on more internal medicine providers to its interdisciplinary care team. It has also launched more supplements and medication delivery services.

It has been revealed that the newly introduced funding will accelerate enterprise partnerships, expand Allara’s clinical infrastructure and support more AI features, executives noted. Read the full story here.

Sources indicate that oct. 14—Confido HealthStartup building an agentic AI operating system Series: series A extensionAmount: $12.5 millionInvestors: Z47, formerly Matrix Partners India, led the extension round. Existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures also backed the series A extension.

Confido Health is expanding beyond AI voice agents to build out an agentic AI operating system that can execute administrative workflows across a medical practice.

The series A extension follows its $10 million series A round announced in September to continue scaling an AI platform for end-to-end healthcare operations.

According to recent reports, confido Health integrates with over 50 systems of record, including electronic health records, practice management systems, phone systems, billing systems and fax, without requiring any change to a practice's existing tech stack. Confido's AI agents can increase administrative staff's capacity to serve patients by automating routine tasks like appointment scheduling, insurance verification, billing and patient outreach, according to executives.

Confido Health executives assert that its agentic AI operations platform can actually execute administrative work across existing systems, helping practices increase capacity and control labor costs rather than simply giving staff another software tool.

Recent findings suggest that healthcare private equity veteran Justin Saks joined as an investor and board advisor. Read the full story here.

Oct. 13—SukiAmbient clinical intelligence Series: EAmount: $90 millionInvestors: Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital. All existing institutional investors also backed the round, including Venrock, Flare Capital Partners, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures and Zoom Ventures.

Suki CEO and Founder Punit Soni told Fierce Healthcare the organization is investing in three areas with the fresh capital: advancing its AI, expanding its commercial organization and scaling its partner ecosystem.

The company has raised more than $250 million to date, executives say. Patient encounters supported by its tools grew more than 190% year over year in 2026, with revenue doubling in 2025 and on track for similar growth this year.

Suki now works with over 250 healthcare organizations and more than 30 technology partners that embed its AI into their platforms, executives say. Read the full story here.

Oct. 8—OutroEvidence-informed medication tapering supportSeries: Pre-seed and seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Listen Ventures, Cake Ventures, Jason Calicanis’s LAUNCH, Actions Capital, Hannah Grey VC, SemperVirens, Brock Recovery Group, Pave Health Ventures, and more.

Outro aims to support safe deprescribing of medications, starting with antidepressants. The firm combines specially-trained clinicians with evidence-informed tapering protocols, patient monitoring, psychosocial support and technology. Its program is available in 14 states.

In a recent development, "Deprescribing guidance has existed in countries like the U.K. for years," mentioned Mark Horowitz, M.D., Ph.D., Outro's co-founder, psychiatry researcher and deprescribing expert, in an announcement. "Yet in America, where antidepressant use is widespread, tapering support is very hard to come by, so millions of patients are left without support when they are ready to come off.".

The funding will support the growth of Outro’s deprescribing clinician network, further the application of AI to deprescribing-specific workflows, expand the manufacturer’s tapering model into additional drug classes and grow existing partnerships with leading universities and advocacy groups.

Industry observers note that earlier this year, the Department of Health & Human Services unveiled a strategy to prevent the unnecessary initiation of psychiatric medications and support tapering and discontinuation for patients not experiencing clinical benefit. It recommended providers regularly review the risks and benefits of psychiatric medications and offer alternatives like therapy when clinically appropriate. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services also released guidance for providers on the importance of deprescribing.

Oct. 8—HealthleapClinical AI platform to flag undiagnosed conditionsSeries: seed/series AAmount: $38 millionInvestors: Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital and Hummingbird Ventures.

Healthleap was founded by siblings Josiah and Jemima Meyer, who teamed up after Jemima, as a clinician, started building tools to help herself and colleagues treat patients faster, according to the company.

Rolled out in 2022, Healthleap aids hospitals in identifying undiagnosed conditions across inpatient and outpatient care settings. The firm notes its platform continuously analyzes every patient’s record, including notes, labs, vitals, orders, problem lists and flags risk for conditions. Healthleap then pushes actionable risk scores into optimized electronic health record workflows to support clinicians in identifying, treating and improving their patients’ health.

Recent findings suggest that healthleap has initially focused on disease-related malnutrition, a condition that costs the U.S. healthcare system up to $58 billion annually. The company states it is the first and only validated AI malnutrition screening tool that contains EHR-integrated screening layers. Read the full story here.

It has been revealed that oct. 7—General MedicineVirtual healthcare storefrontSeries: BAmount: $120 millionInvestors: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) led the round with participation from Matrix, VXI Capital, Eli Lilly and Company, Mercy Health through Granger Management and BoxGroup.

Sources indicate that startup General Medicine, started by the founding team that built PillPack and Amazon Pharmacy, is an online marketplace where customers can search, compare and buy care, see insurance and cash prices before deciding, and get guidance from a licensed clinician. The platform connects consumers to providers to either address specific medical needs or to chat about the symptoms they're having.

The firm's platform connects healthcare recommendations to actual care, whether that means filling a prescription, ordering a lab test, scheduling a telehealth visit or booking an in-person appointment.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer's executives refer to it as a "one-stop shop" for telemedicine, prescriptions, imaging, labs and specialists. Parker and PillPack co-founder Elliot Cohen teamed up with former Amazon executive Ashwin Muralidharan to get General Medicine off the ground in the fall of 2023. Read the full story here.

Oct. 6—VitalizeAI-powered operating system for staffing and schedulingSeries: AAmount: $31 millionInvestors: Oak HC/FT, Norwest Ventures, .406 Ventures, Constellation Ventures, Y Combinator and MemorialCare Innovation Fund.

Vitalize aims to supercharge health system capacity and operations with an artificial intelligence platform that unifies staffing, scheduling, flow and capacity.

At health systems, labor and capacity management are highly manual, inefficient processes that take up hours of administrative work each day.

Labor optimization is the key constraint behind patient flow, operational efficiency and financial performance across health systems, Veeraj Shah, co-founder and CEO of startup Vitalize, said. Capacity planning is the other half of the equation. Hospital revenue depends on matching patient demand to available beds and staff.

Vitalize founders view hospital staffing and capacity management as a complex logistics problem that directly affects finances, patient outcomes and clinician experience.

Vitalize positions its software as an "air traffic control" system for healthcare operations, helping health systems automate staffing, forecast demand, manage capacity and reduce reliance on overtime and agency labor, executives mentioned. Vitalize’s AI automates the most manual scheduling tasks for clinical leaders, while forecasting demand and orchestrating staff across thousands of beds in real time. The company's platform uses machine learning, optimization models and AI agents to forecast staffing needs, fill schedule gaps, automate staffing workflows and recommend patient placement decisions, Shah noted. Read the full story here.

According to recent reports, oct. 1—Tiny HealthMicrobiome testing companySeries: BAmount: $33 millionInvestors: Capital B led the round, with participation from Spero Ventures, Black Opal Ventures, Pave Health Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Gaingels and others.

It has been revealed that tiny was launched in 2022, initially focusing on a microbiome test for babies and moms. "There was just a white space and nobody meeting the needs of those demographics,” Cheryl Sew Hoy, founder and CEO of Tiny Health, told Fierce Healthcare. Tiny expanded to a vaginal microbiome test, and today its adult tests have surpassed pediatric ones in volume.

Sept. 24—Basalt Health AI layer for post-acute care admissionsSeries: AAmount: $20 millionInvestors: NEA led the round, with participation from Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health.

Basalt Health uses AI to streamline post-acute care admissions. The company plans to use the capital to expand its platform and grow its team.

Recent findings suggest that basalt's technology automates the referral and admissions process for post-acute providers, analyzing incoming referrals from faxes, portals and EHR integrations and matching patients to appropriate facilities based on clinical and payer criteria. The company says its platform reduces administrative work and speeds placement decisions that are often delayed by manual processes.

Industry observers note that each year, roughly 14 million patients enter post-acute care—yet the placement process has failed to evolve. The archaic process typically involves case managers faxing lengthy clinical packets to 6.6 facilities per placement, then waiting for the right bed to respond. The resulting delays and mismatches contribute to an estimated $17 billion in avoidable readmission costs annually.

After nearly a decade at Accolade, where he saw administrative work increasingly pull clinicians away from patients, Ben Hackett founded Basalt in 2024 to build technology that fits existing workflows, reduces friction and gives care teams more time to focus on patients.

The startup reports strong early traction with major health systems. Basalt has been live with Lifepoint Health’s team since its seed round in 2025 and the tech giant has reduced median chart processing time from 8.5 minutes to 1.2 minutes. Basalt is also being implemented across 49 additional Lifepoint markets by the end of 2026.

“Case managers are still sending 70-page packets and waiting for responses, while patients remain stranded in hospital beds,” Hackett, founder and CEO of Basalt Health, said. “Basalt turns that uncertainty into fast, defensible decisions. This funding gives us the power to transform one of healthcare’s most stubbornly inefficient systems.”.

Basalt looks to expand beyond admissions into discharge planning and payer workflows, positioning its AI platform as infrastructure for managing patient transitions into post-acute care.

A patient may come in with complex symptoms that typically take several visits and a waiting list for a specialist to address. Then, Blair's LLM provides the family doc a recommended treatment plan. The doc reviews, adjusts and prescribes as needed.

When a patient needs prescriptions, labs or other in-person services, Blair coordinates with those providers accordingly. Blair right now offers care across menopause, urology, pelvic health, clinical nutrition and weight management.

Novellia is tackling one of pharma’s biggest R&D challenges. Researchers have long depended on real-world data to understand how treatments perform outside clinical trials. But data is still largely stitched together from third-party sources, taking data from insurance claims and hospital records. This leaves gaps in longitudinal records that limit its value in clinical settings.

Novellia works directly with patients to compile and share their records with scientists to advance medical discoveries. The organization says it puts this de-identified, anonymized data in the hands of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies and its customers include several of the top 10 pharma and early-stage diagnostics companies.

Along with the upcoming funding, the startup also rolled out its patient-facing mobile app. Through Novellia’s platform, patients with serious and complex conditions can find and unify up to 20 years of medical data from disparate hospital systems, doctors' offices and labs across the U.S. The firm then analyzes those records using proprietary natural language processing models that extract signals from unstructured clinical text, including physician notes, lab narratives and diagnostic reports, turning raw patient data into anonymized, harmonized datasets ready for research. Through Novellia’s platform, patients gain a free, unified view of their health history, while researchers unlock complete, consented, de-identified data for clinical trials and medical breakthroughs, according to the company. Gravity Rail launched out of stealth with a platform that enables healthcare organizations and care teams to build and run their own AI-powered patient engagement workflows.

Recent findings suggest that co-founded by Dan Walmsley, chief technology officer, and Scott Hoch, CEO, Gravity Rail indicates it brings a fundamentally different approach to deploying AI in healthcare that shifts control from outsourced vendors and point solutions to the teams responsible for patient engagement and care coordination. Rather than offering a single AI agent or outsourced service, Gravity Rail provides a model-agnostic operating system for AI-powered engagement, where healthcare teams can build, certify, and run workflows using their own protocols—across phone, SMS, email, web, and messaging channels—without writing code or relying on implementation vendors.

The platform is designed for any healthcare organization or companies working with them—including health aims, provider organizations, contact centers, business processing organizations, digital health companies, and clinical trial platforms—that are responsible for managing patient and member engagement at scale.

Most AI tools are still deployed as isolated solutions that sit outside operational teams, but as workflows change, those systems rapidly fall out of sync.

"Payer rules change, protocols evolve, better models emerge, and updates require coordination with an external vendor. AI transformation has to happen inside the organization. We put control in the hands of the people doing the work, turning protocols into live infrastructure they can see, test, and evolve continuously. As models commoditize, the advantage shifts to the organizations that can adapt fastest," Hoch remarked in a press release.

Industry observers note that in current deployments, Gravity Rai says it has already demonstrated measurable impact. Organizations are connecting with patients 2x to 3x more often while reducing handle times and improving patient satisfaction. Referral workflows have achieved a 30% increase in first scheduled appointment rates compared to manual outreach. Release.

April 23— Almanac HealthResearch-validated clinical AI platform for physiciansSeries: SeedAmount: $10 millionInvestors: Led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Parnters.

Almanac Health, a clinical AI platform founded by a physician, provides evidence-based clinical decision support that integrates with existing electronic health record systems. The fresh funding will advance the tech giant’s mission to bring safe, evidence-grounded AI to clinicians and health systems, executives stated.

The company aims to bring specialist-grade knowledge to clinicians at the point of care, providing evidence-based clinical decision support across medical specialties, free from pharmaceutical advertising, and governed by institutional controls. The platform is designed to work within existing EHR systems and grounded in peer-reviewed evidence. The company asserts the platform is currently undergoing rigorous clinical validation in academic medical center settings.

In a recent development, the firm was founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, M.D., whose work at Stanford University introduced retrieval-augmented generation to clinical medicine. After earning his MD, Zakka went on to conduct machine learning research at Stanford, where he developed the first retrieval-augmented generation system for clinical medicine, an approach to grounding AI in trusted medical knowledge that has since been widely adopted across clinical AI. That work, published in NEJM AI, became one of the journal’s most-cited papers and established the foundational approach used by most clinical evidence AI products today. He subsequently led health AI at Hugging Face, the largest open-source AI platform, before founding Almanac Health.

The funding will allow the firm to grow its team across clinical medicine, AI research, and health systems infrastructure, as well as advance R&D with a focus on privacy, reliability, and rigorous evaluation before deployment. Release.

It has been revealed that cala Health is a bioelectronic medicine firm developing wearable neuromodulation therapies for tremors. It developed and commercialized the Cala kIQ System, an FDA-cleared wearable device designed to help patients manage hand tremors caused by essential tremor and Parkinson's disease.

The device is worn on the wrist and measures a patient's unique tremor pattern and delivers individualized nerve stimulation to counteract tremors through noninvasive electrical stimulation. #30073. Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk

Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that your daily cup of coffee may be doing more than helping you wake up in the morning.
  • Sources indicate that researchers found that adults who consumed higher amounts of caffeinated coffee developed dementia at considerably lower rates than those who rarely or never drank it.
  • The strongest associations appeared among people who drank two to three cups of caffeinated coffee each day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that your daily cup of coffee may be doing more than helping you wake up in the morning. A long-running study of U.S. adults suggests that drinking caffeinated coffee regularly is associated with a substantially lower risk of dementia and better cognitive health as people age.

Sources indicate that researchers found that adults who consumed higher amounts of caffeinated coffee developed dementia at considerably lower rates than those who rarely or never drank it. The findings were based on follow-up periods extending as long as 43 years, offering a valuable look at how everyday drinking habits relate to brain health over time.

The strongest associations appeared among people who drank two to three cups of caffeinated coffee each day. Tea consumption was also linked to better cognitive outcomes, although the amount associated with the greatest benefit was somewhat lower.

Interestingly, decaffeinated coffee did not show the same benefits, raising questions about whether caffeine itself might help explain the connection.

Coffee Drinkers Showed Much Lower Dementia Rates.

One of the most striking findings involved the difference in dementia rates between regular coffee drinkers and people who consumed little or no coffee.

Among U.S. adults who drank higher amounts of caffeinated coffee, researchers recorded 141 dementia cases annually for every 100,000 people. In comparison, the rate was 330 cases per 100,000 people each year among those who rarely or never drank caffeinated coffee.

Dementia is a general term for conditions that progressively interfere with memory, thinking, reasoning, and the ability to perform everyday activities. Alzheimer's disease is its most common cause, although several other brain disorders can also lead to dementia.

Sources indicate that while occasional forgetfulness can be a normal part of aging, dementia involves cognitive difficulties severe enough to disrupt daily life. Identifying lifestyle habits associated with lower dementia risk is therefore an important area of research, particularly as populations grow older.

The findings suggest that regular caffeinated coffee consumption may be one such habit. However, the results show an association rather than proving that coffee directly prevents dementia. Other differences between coffee drinkers and people who avoid coffee could also contribute to the observed results.

Coffee Was Also Linked to Better Cognitive Health.

It has been revealed that the potential benefits were not limited to diagnosed dementia. Participants who drank more caffeinated coffee were also less likely to report that their memory or thinking abilities had declined.

Researchers found that 7.8% of adults who consumed higher amounts of caffeinated coffee reported subjective cognitive decline, compared with 9.5% of those who rarely or never drank it.

Recent findings suggest that subjective cognitive decline refers to changes in memory or thinking that people notice themselves, even when those difficulties have not necessarily been confirmed by formal cognitive testing. Someone experiencing it might feel that remembering information, concentrating, or finding the right words has become more difficult.

It has been revealed that such complaints do not automatically indicate dementia. Nevertheless, they can provide useful information about how people perceive changes in their cognitive abilities as they grow older.

The lower percentage among caffeinated coffee drinkers adds to the evidence linking coffee consumption with healthier cognitive aging.

How Much Coffee Offers the Greatest Benefit?

The researchers also examined whether the amount of coffee consumed was related to the strength of the observed benefits.

Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee per day was associated with the most favorable outcomes for dementia risk and cognitive functioning.

In a recent development, notably, this association remained apparent regardless of participants' genetic risk of developing dementia. In other words, the relationship between coffee consumption and brain health was observed even among people whose inherited characteristics might make them more vulnerable to the disease.

Recent findings suggest that genetic risk refers to the influence of inherited variations in DNA that can increase or decrease a person's likelihood of developing certain conditions. Although genetics can play an key role in dementia, they are only one part of a much larger picture that includes age, general health, and lifestyle.

It has been revealed that the results also suggest that drinking larger amounts of coffee is not necessarily better. Consumption beyond the range associated with the strongest benefits did not appear to provide additional protection.

Tea Drinkers May Benefit Too, but Decaf Was Different.

Coffee was not the only beverage associated with better brain health. Researchers found that drinking tea was also linked to lower dementia risk and better cognitive functioning.

According to recent reports, for tea, the strongest associations appeared among participants who consumed one to two cups per day. As with coffee, drinking more than this amount did not appear to produce further benefits.

However, the study did not distinguish between caffeinated and noncaffeinated tea. As a result, the findings cannot establish whether caffeine was responsible for the association observed among tea drinkers.

Recent findings suggest that the results for coffee offered an additional clue. While regular caffeinated coffee was associated with lower dementia risk and better cognitive outcomes, decaffeinated coffee did not demonstrate the same benefits.

Caffeine is a naturally occurring stimulant found in coffee, tea, and several other plants. It acts on the central nervous system and is best known for temporarily increasing alertness and reducing feelings of tiredness.

According to recent reports, whether caffeine also contributes to better brain health over many years is a separate question. The difference between regular and decaffeinated coffee makes this possibility worth investigating, but it does not establish caffeine as the cause of the observed benefits.

Sources indicate that taken together, the findings suggest that moderate consumption of caffeinated coffee and tea may be associated with healthier brain aging. For coffee drinkers, two to three cups daily appeared to offer the strongest association, while one to two cups of tea showed the most favorable results among tea drinkers.

Although additional research is needed to determine whether these beverages directly influence dementia risk, the long-term findings offer encouraging news for people who already enjoy coffee or tea as part of their daily routine.

UPDATED 16:22 EST / NOVEMBER 17 2026.

In a recent development, former Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang today said he’s open to returning to his old post.

Huang expressed his willingness to be reinstated in a post on X. It marks his first public statement since his ouster from Nvidia last week. He resigned following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former cloud executive suspected to be a Chinese spy.

In a recent development, huang apologized for his conduct in today’s X post. He went on to cite recent calls for him to return as a factor behind his willingness to resume his work at Nvidia.

Recent findings suggest that “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the tech giant, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

In a recent development, huang’s statement isn’t a complete surprise. On Sunday, the Financial Times reported that he had discussed a comeback with confidants. The paper stated that a member of Huang’s circle was working to assemble a group of tech executives to support the effort.

Last Thursday, an anonymous user rolled out an online petition to reinstate Huang. It drew the support of several prominent tech executives including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games Inc. CEO Tim Sweeney. The petition also garnered 180,000 other signatures, although it appears that not all of them are genuine. One entry spotted by Business Insider read “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor.”.

Sources indicate that it’s unclear whether the efforts to reinstate Huang are realistic. On Monday, CNBC reported that Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing him back. And today, on Nvidia’s earnings call, Chair Harvey Jones repeated that the board doesn’t intend to reinstate him. Earlier, sources had told Reuters that he had misled the chipmaker’s general counsel and chief marketing officer about his relationship with Alice Huang.

While some U.S. officials believe Alice Huang was part of an espionage operation, others see the evidence as inconclusive. On Thursday, sources told CNN that the intelligence collected on her doesn’t prove she’s a spy. The same day, the Justice Department stated it had not yet concluded Alice Huang is a Chinese asset.

Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider that has ordered billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. The Justice Department is investigating the company over alleged export control violations. As early as 2024, officials identified “suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential ​sensitive semiconductor diversion.”.

The Wall Street Journal today reported that Nvidia has hired a prominent executive search firm to find a upcoming CEO. According to the paper, it plans to evaluate both internal and external candidates. Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress right now leads the firm as interim CEO.

Sources indicate that kress also supervises a fresh national security and export control oversight committee that Nvidia formed today. It will be responsible for the firm’s national security policies, adherence to export control rules and global trade risk management.

According to recent reports, the committee comprises three Nvidia directors on launch. It will carry out its work in collaboration with the chipmaker’s executives and external experts in fields such as law, national security and global trade compliance. Nvidia indicates that the committee will meet at least once per quarter.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, waymo has been burning piles of money as a Google spin-off company for a decade now with no end in sight.
  • According to recent reports, "Built for women.
  • According to recent reports, A Waymo robotaxi could possibly prove safer for any rider, regardless of gender, considering how faulty human drivers can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, waymo has been burning piles of money as a Google spin-off company for a decade now with no end in sight. Technical challenges aside, what really makes or breaks a fresh technology is the behavior of the people using it. The company's latest reach-out to the average American arrived in ad-form last week, and it bets on women and their constantly compromised safety.

According to recent reports, "Built for women. Designed for peace of mind," is a one-minute video following women doing all of the things we are taught to do when simply trying to move through the world — looking over the shoulder constantly, engaging in fake, one-sided conversations over the phone, getting out keys, etc. Layered in is a voiceover montage of women's voices saying all-too-common phrases uttered when a friend leaves the pack. Things like "maybe keep your keys out before you leave the bar," and "have someone walk you out to your car." The ad ends with a woman (separately) getting into a car. She shuts the the door and gives a massive exhale. The Waymo is her safe space.

According to recent reports, A Waymo robotaxi could possibly prove safer for any rider, regardless of gender, considering how faulty human drivers can be. Meanwhile, Uber's handling of its sexual assault cases would give any reasonable woman pause. Lyft and Uber even offer women-only drivers to customers because of women's understandable hesitance to get into a car with a man they don't know. So, why not expand that logic by removing the driver entirely. Waymo further backed its advantages for women's safety in its a blog saying that the firm's data showed over half of female riders said that "Waymo improves their sense of personal safety. Having a space where riders are in control of their environment makes a real difference.".

As a woman who has noted or heard (or practiced) much of the advice in Waymo's video, I'll admit there is some comfort in not having to worry about being alone in a car with a driver. Advertising on the bet that other women will too makes me feel a cynical little queasiness in my gut, however. It's a drop in the bucket for what women have to worry about when they leave their homes. For instance, in Waymo's own video, a women walked from venue to robotaxi for some distance alone on a dark street. Should something happen in that time, a human driver might be able to spot it and intervene. A woman already has to shoulder the responsibility of her attacker's actions against her, will that scrutiny now extend to her choice in transportation?

I wanted to know more about what Waymo offers for riders in terms of safety not only in the car, but outside of it. Waymo, in response, wrote that the tech giant takes "any situation involving threats, harassment or violence toward a rider extremely seriously."  It does, however, "... recognize that personal safety encompasses more than avoiding traffic collisions. It also involves how people experience transportation, the support available to them and their ability to make informed choices throughout a trip.".

That being stated, I asked Waymo how it can help riders in a variety of safety situations whether outside and inside the vehicle, taking into consideration that it's not just women who are concerned, parents might send their kids in Waymos, among many other individuals.

For instance, if a customer were attacked outside of a vehicle, there's not a ton a Waymo car can do. The rider can reach emergency services like 9-1-1 through the app or from their phones and, in some instances, Waymo says the vehicle may remain stationary until help arrives and communicate with people outside of the vehicle via its external speakers.

In a recent development, if a vehicle were to make a stop due to a technical problem someplace, the doors remain locked and it's recommended the rider stay in the vehicle until the issue is addressed or Waymo's Roadside Assistance arrives (if the situation requires it). In some cases a Waymo driver will arrive and get behind the wheel to help the vehicle autonomously navigate to the rider's destination.

Sources indicate that in most any case, if something happens, riders are directed to call for assistance in the app, on their own by phone, or through the in-car screen. It's not a perfect system, as no one can control every element in every environment. The manufacturer earnestly takes it seriously though, and indicates it is always open to hearing more feedback.

What Waymo can't do unfortunately is fix behaviors that still remain rampant in American society in the 21st century, but hey, at least it can use the fears of those behaviors to advertise.

The Harm From Plastic Is Happening In Plain Sight

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Plastic is a major cause of the climate crisis, yet governments continue to ignore it.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) has issued a fresh briefing published to coincide with the UN Climate Change Conference, COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye.
  • Plastic already emits more than two billion tons of CO₂e a year, about twice as much as aviation, and under current policies this would more than double as the fossil fuel industry turns to plastic as its hedge against electrification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is known. Plastic is a major cause of the climate crisis, yet governments continue to ignore it.

Recent findings suggest that the Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) has issued a fresh briefing published to coincide with the UN Climate Change Conference, COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye. The briefing, “Reducing plastic production in a post-1.5°C world: A test of resolve for the international community,” calls on governments to reduce global plastic production.

Plastic already emits more than two billion tons of CO₂e a year, about twice as much as aviation, and under current policies this would more than double as the fossil fuel industry turns to plastic as its hedge against electrification.

“There’s only so much carbon the world can still emit if we want to avoid blasting past the Paris Agreement targets. Plastic’s harm to our climate is happening in plain sight, and governments are choosing to look away. Every newly introduced plastics plant locks in decades of emissions the planet simply cannot afford. As leaders gather at COP31, they must recognise plastic as a major cause of carbon pollution that is rapidly heating our world.” — Steve Trent, CEO, Environmental Justice Foundation.

In a recent development, over 90% of plastic emissions come before a plastic product is even used, during extraction, conversion and production. If current policies remain unchanged, global plastic production is projected to almost triple by 2060, and annual emissions from fossil-based plastics to more than double, to 4.3 billion tons of CO2e.

On this trajectory, plastics would emit 67 billion tons of CO2e between 2026 and 2050. That is just over half of the remaining carbon budget for a 50% chance of meeting the 1.5°C target, and 27% of the budget for a very good chance of limiting the overshoot to 1.7°C. None of this is hidden; emissions are quantified, the projections are published and the industry’s expansion aims are public, yet plastic remains on the margins of climate negotiations.

EJF is calling on governments at COP31 to recognize plastic for what it is: a major driver of climate change that must be tackled at its source, by cutting production.

The petrochemical industry’s bet on plastics.

In a recent development, as the world electrifies transport and power, the fossil fuel industry is using plastic as its hedge against electrification. With oil demand for transport and energy expected to decline, petrochemical companies are pivoting to plastics to keep oil and gas flowing. The plastics sector could account for 20% of global oil consumption by 2050, up from around 12% today. The top fifteen petrochemical companies received an estimated US$590.8 billion in financing between 2019 and 2025, and the sector was propped up by state subsidies estimated at over $80 billion in 2024 alone, almost half of which came from Saudi Arabia.

A test of resolve for the plastics treaty.

Sources indicate that A total of 145 countries from every continent have expressed support for provisions to reduce plastic production during the global plastics treaty negotiations. Rwanda and Peru have proposed a global target to cut plastic production by 40% by 2040 against a 2025 baseline. Modelling cited in the briefing reveals that a 40% cut in high-ambition countries, joined by China and emerging producers, could reduce global emissions from plastics by as much as 21% compared with business as usual.

But negotiations have reached a deadlock, driven by a small group of oil- and plastic-producing states, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iran and China, with the United States recently aligning with their position. At least 234 fossil fuel and chemical industry lobbyists attended the latest round of talks in Geneva — more than the combined delegations of the EU and its 27 Member States.

At COP31, EJF is urging governments to:.

Final Thoughts about Plastic and our Leaders.

In a recent development, the truth about plastics is perverse. Plastics are widely used around the world due to ease of manufacturing, low cost, stable chemical properties, and good water resistance. They have infiltrated every part of the environment and human life cycle. More than 16,000 chemicals are used in manufacturing plastics, and at least 4,200 of these have been identified as hazardous to human health and the environment. Thousands more chemicals used in plastic production have never been tested. Many of these chemicals migrate out of plastic packaging into our foods, drinks, household products, and bodies.

Sources indicate that researchers have come up with many possible solutions to plastic pollution, as well as ways to mitigate microplastics in the environment. But will governments have the wherewithal to stand up to the powerful fossil fuel lobby that is behind plastic propaganda?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that with its WS6 RPO-optioned ram-air induction, today's Nice Price or No Dice Trans-Am has over 300 horsepower to play with.
  • Europa, the celestial body, is the smallest and least massive of Jupiter's Galilean moons.
  • Small, light, and smooth also describes the 1973 Lotus Europa John Player Special we looked at on Tuesday, proving Colin Chapman's marketing savvy was on point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that with its WS6 RPO-optioned ram-air induction, today's Nice Price or No Dice Trans-Am has over 300 horsepower to play with. Let's see if the seller's set price means they're playing with us.

Europa, the celestial body, is the smallest and least massive of Jupiter's Galilean moons. Notably, it also has the closest orbit to its host planet, and tidal forces from the gas giant have molded the moon's surface into an almost smooth landscape, devoid of the craters and topographical deviations common on other otherworldly bodies.

Small, light, and smooth also describes the 1973 Lotus Europa John Player Special we looked at on Tuesday, proving Colin Chapman's marketing savvy was on point. Our car was number 90 out of 100 Lotus built in the iconic black-and-gold livery of the tech giant's Formula One race team's sponsor, John Player & Sons, celebrating the team's 1972 World Championship win.

At $27,000, few of you wanted our Europa in your orbit, with many of the comments focusing negatively on the car's odd, semi-El Camino looks. In the end, voters overlooked that personal taste, paving the way for the Europa's narrow 54% 'Nice Price' win.

Unlike Lotus, which expanded its racing efforts into many series, including Formula 1, Indy cars, and the GT class, Pontiac largely limited its factory-supported on-track heroics to the drag strip, the NASCAR circuit, and the namesake series of today's 1997 Pontiac Trans-Am.

Sources indicate that boutique cars are all the rage today, with companies like Mini and Porsche allowing buyers to choose from a plethora of add-on options to personalize their cars to the nth degree. That wasn't always the case, though; back in the day, an automaker's option sheet let a buyer craft a car to fit their needs, but within limits. At General Motors, that option list has long been denoted by three letters: RPO. They stand for "Regular Production Option," and have given rise to many package codes denoting now-venerated performance options like the WS6 group on this Trans-Am.

First introduced in 1978, the WS6 Special Performance Package was originally positioned as a handling upgrade. The package included snowflake alloy wheels fitted with fatter-than-stock tires and a rear anti-roll bar. Later editions added four-wheel disc brakes. For our car, WS6 still means bigger wheels and tires and more aggressive suspension tuning, but it notably adds a ram-air induction intake fed by two functional nostrils fronting the car's blistered hood.

That ram-air induction feeds an LT1 V8, kindly provided by the capable engine builders over at Chevrolet. This was the last year for the LT1, as Pontiac introduced the LS1 the following year. That engine had previously been exclusive to the Corvette. With the big gulp air intake, the 350 CID LT1 still puts out a very healthy 305 hp and 335 pound-feet of torque, significant increases over the standard engine's 285 hp and 325 lb-ft.

Recent findings suggest that here, that mill is mated to a 4L60E four-speed automatic, something the seller touts in the ad, claiming this to be one of only 347 auto-equipped WS6 cars produced this year. The ad also boasts that "Everything works like it came off the showroom floor.".

It's not all stock, though. The ad claims a replacement quad-tip exhaust with Flowmaster mufflers, fresh poly suspension bushings, and KYB shocks as notable updates. There are 79,778 miles on the clock, a modest number, but still called out in the ad, with the seller explaining, "While it has changed hands among enthusiasts, the low 79k mileage and remarkable preservation proves it has spent its life as a garage-kept weekend toy rather than a daily driver.".

Recent findings suggest that back in 1997, a corral of 300 horses was a lot. Today, even a four-cylinder Mustang offers more than that and will easily outdo this Trans-Am in any dimension of performance. That doesn't mean this cool red-over-white convertible isn't worth a look. First off, when did you last see a classic Trans-Am like this? I bet it was at a Cars & Coffee or other enthusiast enclave. That makes it interesting simply because of its uniqueness. Then there are the pop-up headlamps. We love those guys! This is also, as the ad touts, an incredibly well-maintained example of the breed, needing nothing but the next owner to agree not to mess it up.

In a recent development, yes, the interior is gawd-awful, with miserable hard plastic surfaces, wide gaps between panels, and buttons that look like they came straight from the bargain bin at Temu, but that's just how Pontiac (and pretty much all of GM) rolled in this era. At least the seats look comfortable as all get out, and the car has all the niceties one could want, including manual climate, cruise, power windows, locks and top, and a CD stereo. As an added incentive, the title is as clean as the car.

Industry observers note that okay, so if anyone is in the market for a last-of-the-Mohicans Trans-Am, this is a strong candidate. Yes, later cars with the LS do perform better and have more aggressive styling, if that's your thing. On the other hand, they also tend to command substantially higher prices. This car's $13,000 asking price might make up for that performance gap.

We'll now need to debate that question, as that's what we do here. With that in mind, what's your take on this Trans-Am and that $13,000 asking price? Does the WS6 package sway your opinion of the car's value? Or is that immaterial, and is spending more on a later, more capable car really the way to go?

#30065. Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins
