Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1486 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A major clinical trial has raised new questions about how doctors decide who should take statins to prevent heart attacks and strokes.
  • The findings, presented during a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026, also revealed a striking difference in how consistently patients took their medication.
  • It has been revealed that although the results suggest that heart scans could help doctors make more targeted treatment decisions, the trial did not establish that the scan approach was as effective as conventional risk assessment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A major clinical trial has raised new questions about how doctors decide who should take statins to prevent heart attacks and strokes. Researchers found that using heart scans to guide treatment decisions produced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events as traditional risk assessments, even though the scans led to far fewer recommendations to begin taking statins.

The findings, presented during a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026, also revealed a striking difference in how consistently patients took their medication. Those advised to use statins based on calcium buildup in their coronary arteries were substantially more likely to follow their treatment recommendations.

It has been revealed that although the results suggest that heart scans could help doctors make more targeted treatment decisions, the trial did not establish that the scan approach was as effective as conventional risk assessment. Researchers say additional studies are needed to determine whether it offers a better strategy for preventing cardiovascular disease.

Why Predicting Heart Disease Risk Remains a Challenge.

In a recent development, cardiovascular disease remains the world's leading cause of illness and death. Much of this burden comes from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), which develops when fatty deposits known as plaque accumulate inside arteries, restricting blood flow and increasing the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Coronary artery disease and ischemic stroke are two major forms of this condition.

Several common factors increase the likelihood of developing ASCVD, including smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure, and elevated cholesterol. Doctors use these factors to estimate a person's cardiovascular risk and determine whether preventive medications are appropriate.

It has been revealed that statins are among the most widely used treatments for lowering that risk. These medications reduce cholesterol levels, particularly low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, often called LDL or bad cholesterol. They also help lower the likelihood of serious cardiovascular complications.

However, identifying which patients stand to benefit from statins remains a significant challenge. Some people who eventually experience a heart attack do not appear to be at particularly high risk under conventional screening methods.

"For far too many patients, the first symptom of ASCVD is a heart attack," said Doctor Joseph B Muhlestein from the Intermountain Medical Center, Murray, USA, the Principal Investigator of the CorCal Outcomes trial. "Statins have been shown to be highly effective in the prevention of ASCVD; however, there is a major gap in risk assessment, statin initiation, and statin persistence.".

Sources indicate that according to Muhlestein, many people who suffer their first heart attack, particularly younger adults, would not previously have been classified as having enough cardiovascular risk to justify statin treatment. This limitation has prompted researchers to investigate whether directly examining the arteries might provide more useful information.

Can Heart Calcium Scans Improve Statin Decisions?

The CorCal Outcomes trial investigated two different approaches for determining which patients should be advised to begin statin therapy before experiencing a cardiovascular event.

The first relied on the pooled cohort equations (PCE), a commonly used risk assessment tool that estimates cardiovascular risk using traditional factors such as age, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, and smoking status.

The second approach measured coronary artery calcium (CAC), which provides a more direct indication of plaque buildup in the arteries supplying the heart.

This measurement uses a computed tomography (CT) scan to detect calcium deposits in the coronary arteries. Calcium can accumulate within atherosclerotic plaque, making it a useful marker of underlying coronary artery disease, even in people who have not developed symptoms.

Unlike traditional risk calculators, which estimate the likelihood of future cardiovascular problems based on personal characteristics and health measurements, calcium scans provide evidence of disease already present in the coronary arteries.

Researchers wanted to determine whether using this information to guide statin recommendations could improve cardiovascular outcomes.

Nearly 5,800 Patients Put Both Methods to the Test.

The trial enrolled 5,772 patients from the Canyons and Desert regions of Intermountain Health Care in the United States. Participants had no known history of ASCVD or diabetes and had not previously received statin therapy.

Their average age was 64, and women accounted for 51% of the study population.

Sources indicate that eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to one of two groups. One group received statin treatment guidance based on traditional cardiovascular risk scores, while the other received recommendations based on coronary calcium scan results.

Both patients and their physicians were informed of the treatment recommendations generated by the study protocol. However, the final decision about whether to start taking statins remained with the patients and their doctors.

The researchers then tracked major cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and arterial revascularization).

This combined outcome included death from any cause, heart attacks, strokes, and procedures to restore blood flow through narrowed or blocked arteries.

Heart Scans Led to Far Fewer Statin Recommendations.

After an average follow-up of 4.2 years, researchers found that major cardiovascular events occurred at exactly the same observed rate in both groups.

In a recent development, A total of 2.7% of patients in each group experienced one of the events included in the study's primary outcome. The estimated relative risk over time was also nearly identical (hazard ratio 0.99; 95% confidence interval 0.71 to 1.38; p=0.045 for noninferiority).

However, this similarity did not establish that the two strategies were equally effective. The study failed to meet its predetermined statistical requirement for demonstrating that the calcium scan approach was not meaningfully worse than conventional risk assessment.

A notable difference emerged in how frequently patients were advised to begin taking statins.

Participants evaluated using traditional risk scores received recommendations to start statin therapy more than three times as often as those whose decisions were guided by coronary calcium measurements.

Despite this substantial difference in treatment recommendations, both groups experienced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events during the follow-up period.

A Surprising Difference in Statin Adherence.

Perhaps the most intriguing finding involved whether patients actually followed their prescribed treatment.

Among those advised to take statins, patients whose recommendations were based on calcium scans were much more likely to adhere to their medication regimen than those assessed using traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

It has been revealed that the difference was substantial (62% vs. 23%).

In other words, patients recommended statins based on visible evidence of calcium buildup in their arteries were approximately 2.7 times as likely to follow their medication regimen.

One possible explanation is that seeing evidence of disease in their own arteries makes patients more motivated to take preventive medication. However, the trial did not establish why adherence differed so dramatically between the groups.

The findings raise the possibility that coronary calcium scans could influence not only which patients receive statin recommendations, but also whether those patients consistently take the medications.

What the Findings Mean for Heart Disease Prevention.

Despite these potentially important differences, the researchers emphasized that the study could not establish whether calcium scan-guided treatment provides cardiovascular protection comparable to traditional risk assessment.

One notable limitation was that fewer participants experienced major cardiovascular events than the investigators had anticipated. With fewer events to analyze, the trial had less statistical power to determine whether a meaningful difference existed between the two approaches.

"The power of the study to detect a difference was reduced by the lower-than-expected event rates and we did not demonstrate noninferiority between the groups," said Doctor Muhlestein, who concluded: "The study did provide important hypothesis-generating insights into the efficiency of statin initiation and adherence when decisions are based on CAC scoring. Taken together, our data could be used to proposal an additional well-powered randomized trial comparing CAC with current risk factor-based algorithms.".

The findings may help researchers design future trials capable of determining whether coronary calcium scans can improve the efficiency of statin prescribing without compromising cardiovascular protection.

Current European recommendations already recognize a potential role for these measurements. The 2025 Focused Update of the 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidemias recommends considering increased coronary calcium scores, when available, as an additional factor in cardiovascular risk assessment.

This guidance applies particularly to people at moderate cardiovascular risk or those whose estimated risk falls near the threshold at which preventive medication would normally be recommended.

For these individuals, evidence of calcium buildup may help doctors make more informed decisions when the need for statin therapy is uncertain.

According to recent reports, the CorCal Outcomes findings add to the discussion by suggesting that heart scans may also influence how faithfully patients follow treatment. Whether that advantage translates into better long-term cardiovascular outcomes remains an notable question for future research.

Welcome to this week's Chutes & Ladders, our roundup of hirings, firings and retirings throughout the industry. Please submit the good news—or the bad—from your shop, and we will feature it here each week.

Industry observers note that >SimpliFed, a virtual breast- and baby-feeding support platform, has welcomed Gemma Wenstrom as the tech giant's new chief operations officer. She will help create the systems, accountability and operational foundation required to support sustainable growth and strong outcomes.

Wenstrom hails from Kaia Health, where she was also COO, driving commercial delivery, upcoming business development and product strategy.

Recent findings suggest that “SimpliFed has built an incredibly strong foundation centered around improving access, continuity, and support for families during pregnancy and postpartum,” remarked Wenstrom. “I look forward to helping scale the operational infrastructure, systems, and team needed to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care while supporting the company’s continued expansion and impact.”.

In a recent development, earlier this year, SimpliFed also added Melissa Walsh, M.D., as medical director. Walsh is a board-certified OBGYN with nearly two decades of experience spanning clinical care, academic medicine, digital health innovation and maternal health equity. She was previously national medical director of OBGYN at Pomelo Care. At SimpliFed, she will lead clinical strategy and care model development.

Industry observers note that >Mayo Clinic has revealed Matthew R. Callstrom, M.D., Ph.D., as its next president and CEO, taking over for Gianrico Farrugia, M.D., who in May announced looks to step down at the end of the year.

Callstrom, a radiologist, has been with Mayo Clinic since 2002 who is at the moment medical director for Mayo Clinic Strategy and its AI Program. He's also a member of its board of governors and board of trustees. He's credited for his role in the major nonprofit system's organizational strategy and integration of AI into care.

According to recent reports, farrugia, who has headed Mayo since 2019, aims to stay on through Dec. 31 to ensure a smooth handoff.

>Carl S. Armato, president and CEO of Winston-Salem, North Carolina-based Novant Health, will retire at the end of this year after 15 years leading the system.

Armato joined the nonprofit in 1998 as vice president of finance and operations in its Charlotte and Winston-Salem physician divisions, and held increasing regional and organization-wide leadership roles over subsequent years.

He's credited with boosting access points and unifying Novant's "collection of strong regional organizations into a unified, innovative health system." He also headed substantial growth, with the organization today counting 45,000 employees, 22 hospitals and about 900 total locations.

With his retirement, current Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer John Gizdic will become president and interim CEO on Jan. 1, 2027. His resume includes over 30 years of healthcare leadership, including more than 20 with Novant.

> UnitedHealthcare has named Suha Assi as CEO of individual Medicare Advantage, per a LinkedIn post.

Assi previously spent nearly a decade as executive director for Medicare and Retirement in Tennessee, and she previously held roles based in the state for Cigna. She wrote in the post that the "relationships with our teams, providers and communities have shaped how I think about this business and, most importantly, the people we serve.".

"As I step into this national role, I’m excited about what’s ahead for Medicare Advantage," she wrote. "I look forward to working alongside teams and provider partners across the country to modernize how we work together, strengthen relationships, and find newly introduced ways to deliver for our members.".

> Daryl Tol, president and CEO of General Catalyst's Health Assurance Transformation Organization (HATCo) is stepping down from the role, the venture capital firm's CEO Hemant Taneja shared Tuesday.

Tol had been with the firm for about four and a half years in the wake of his time as president and CEO of AdventHealth's Central Florida Division. During that time, he headed HATCo's partner and advisory network—helping grow it to nearly 40 providers, payers and other portfolio companies—and took the organization's top spot partway through 2025. Of note, he helped HATCo close its acquisition of regional health system Summa Health and served as its interim CEO for much of the past year until the appointment of Jennifer Eslinger last month.

Tol is being succeeded by Reva Nohria, a founding member of the HATCo team who has been with General Catalyst since 2018. Taneja, in his announcement, remarked her work at both organizations has encompassed investment, organization creation and strategic partnership, and that she will continue as an investor at the venture capital firm alongside her new appointment.

Tol will support a smooth leadership transition and remain in an advisory role, a representative of General Catalyst told Fierce Healthcare.

> Jennifer Shuford, M.D., is leaving her post as deputy director and chief medical officer of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Nov. 12, just four months after joining, according to a Washington Post report that was confirmed by the agency on Tuesday.

The agency told press in a statement that Shuford was departing "to spend more time with family." Her appointment was confirmed by President Donald Trump in April, and she joined in June.

Shuford is an infectious disease specialist who came to the federal stage from a role as commissioner of the Texas Department of State Health Services and before that, served as the state's chief epidemiologist. Notably, she was credited with heading Texas' response to a measles outbreak last year. Her departure comes as the CDC clashes with state health departments and other public health leaders over its response to a growing national measles outbreak.

Satish Pillai, M.D., is slated to fill the role in the interim as the agency seeks a replacement, the CDC said.

> Johns Hopkins Health System CEO Kevin Sowers is set to retire at the end of 2027.

Sowers has served as president and CEO of the Johns Hopkins system since 2018. He also previously spent more than 32 years as a leader within the Duke University Health System, including eight as CEO of Duke University Hospital.

The early announcement of his retirement plans gives Johns Hopkins significant time to conduct a search for a successor, with Theodore DeWeese, dean of the medical faculty and CEO of Johns Hopkins Medicine, leading the charge. Sowers will become a strategic adviser to Johns Hopkins to support the transition, the health system stated.

Recent findings suggest that "When I joined Johns Hopkins Medicine in 2018, I made a commitment to the organization and to myself to give 10 years of everything I had to this extraordinary place—to the talented, dedicated people who work here, and the people and communities we serve. And I intend to keep that commitment," Sowers noted in a video message.

According to recent reports, > Calley Means, a prominent senior advisor to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. closely aligned with the Make America Healthy Again Movement, resigned from his role on Thursday.

The resignation was reported by the Wall Street Journal and confirmed by Means on social media.

Media reports from the past several months described Means' frustrations seeing MAHA policy priorities delayed or blunted by others in the administration, with the journal citing sources describing him as "disillusioned." Still, his time advising the secretary notched several wins for the movement, including overhauled dietary guidelines, steps toward greater food ingredient transparency and loosened restrictions on psychedelics as potential medical treatments.

Means wrote in his confirmation post that he still holds "tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy" in their battles against "the entrenched, dark forces in D.C. that profit from Americans getting sick.".

"More policy and cultural change has happened around these goals in the past two years than any time in history—and I know this movement is just getting started," he wrote.

> Premier Health, a five-hospital nonprofit academic system in Southwest Ohio, has appointed Rosanna Morris as its upcoming president and CEO, effective in the first quarter of 2027.

Morris is right now executive vice president and chief clinical operating officer at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, and was previously president of Beaumont Hospital-Royal Oak. She is a registered nurse by training and has more than 27 years of health leadership.

She takes over for the retiring Michael Riordan, who has led Premier Health for about half a decade. During that period, he's credited, by the system's board, with stabilizing the system's finances.

> Centivo has added two leaders to its C-suite, the health blueprint announced.

Sources indicate that lisa Bielamowicz, M.D., will join the company as chief health officer, while James Parr will step into the role of chief commercial officer. Both are veteran healthcare leaders, Centivo said.

Bielamowicz has a long career as a physician and health system consultant, and will take on the chief health officer title after advising Centivo's board of directors.

Industry observers note that parr has previously served as a senior adviser to employers at Lockton as well as senior vice president and head of sales at Collective Health. Parr has also held leadership roles at Cigna, per the announcement.

Industry observers note that "There are few leaders in healthcare who have the health benefits strategy knowledge and have built the strong relationships that Lisa and James bring to Centivo," said Ashok Subramanian, co-founder and CEO of Centivo, in the announcement. "These new leaders put Centivo in a strong position as we launch in new markets and help more employers across the country tackle rising healthcare costs and restore affordability by rethinking their healthcare benefits strategy.".

> Inspira Health CEO Amy Mansue will be retiring at the end of the year, and will be succeeded by current President and Chief Operating Officer Warren Moore, the four-hospital South Jersey system declared this week.

Mansue will have been at the helm for six years, and is credited by the organization for expanding local care access and championing a culture of wellness among its 7,800-person workforce.

Moore has led Inspira's operations since 2021 and was promoted to president at the top of this year. He has 35 years of industry experience and will most immediately prioritize the opening of a upcoming hospital tower and building upon the system's recent Epic launch.

It has been revealed that “Leading Inspira has been one of the great privileges of my career,” Mansue said in the announcement. “I’m proud of what our team has accomplished and grateful for the trust of our communities. After working alongside Warren for many years, I know his ability to bring people together, navigate complex challenges and understand what our patients and neighbors count on us to deliver. I have every confidence in his leadership of Inspira’s next chapter.”.

> Joint Commission has named Ken Grubbs as its chief operating officer, effective Jan. 1.

According to recent reports, grubbs is the first nurse to serve as COO of Joint Commission Enterprise in organization’s history, according to the Oct. 13 announcement. He currently serves as the organization's chief nursing executive and executive vice president of Accreditation and Certification Operations.

He will succeed James Merlino, M.D., who will take over as the organization's president and CEO this coming January.

It has been revealed that > Beth Israel Lahey Health's national leadership search has yielded Peter Shorett as its next president and CEO. His appointment takes effect this coming January.

Industry observers note that shorett is at the moment the system's senior executive vice president and chief operating officer, and played a role bringing together its Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for an upcoming strategic collaboration for cancer care. Prior to joining in 2019, he was a senior partner at Chartis.

Industry observers note that he'll be taking over for Kevin Tabb, M.D., who in March gave notice to the system's board that he plans to step down after this year. He'd the role at Beth Israel Deaconess since 2011 and guided the organization through its 2019 merger with Lahey Health.

> WellSpan's Board of Directors has named Laureen Driscoll as the Pennsylvania-based system's new president and CEO.

Sources indicate that the executive and registered nurse's appointment will go into effect Jan. 4, 2027. She takes over for Roxanna Gapstur, Ph.D., who announced looks to retire this past spring.

Driscoll is joining the 12-hospital, $4.7 billion nonprofit from Providence, where she presently serves as chief executive for its south division and oversees 17 hospitals with $10.3 billion of net operating revenue. Prior to that she held roles at MultiCare Health System, Swedish Health System, Le Bonheur Children's Medical Center and Maine Medical Center.

Industry observers note that “She has led complex health systems through transformation while strengthening quality, culture, access and performance," Board Chair Joe Crosswhite remarked in the announcement. "Just as key, she leads with purpose and understands that listening to team members, clinicians and communities is essential. The Board is confident Laureen is the right leader for WellSpan’s next chapter.”.

> UnitedHealthcare has elevated Bobby Hunter to the role of president at the insurer.

Hunter wrote in a LinkedIn post that in the upcoming position he will be tasked with leading the charge on the manufacturer's modernization efforts, including investments in technology and other initiatives to simplify the healthcare experience for its members.

Hunter most recently served as CEO of Government Programs at UnitedHealthcare, and has held multiple leadership roles at the insurer dating back to 2011.

"The future we're working toward is one where aims and providers work together more seamlessly, information flows instantly, trust is earned through transparency and accountability, and care teams are able to spend more time focused on patients," he wrote in the post. "To get there, we must continue to deliver on the commitments we make to the people, providers, customers, and communities who count on us every day.".

> Jonathan B. Perlin, M.D., Ph.D., will retire from his roles as president and CEO of accrediting organization Joint Commission on Dec. 31. Current Chief Operating Officer James I. Merlino, M.D., is slated to succeed him.

Sources indicate that perlin boasted three decades of healthcare executive leadership across his career, which included five at the top of Joint Commission. During that period he oversaw a substantial reduction on Joint Commission standards deemed to be burdensome or obsolete, and programs to support healthcare safety complications in low- and middle-income countries. Titles preceding his time at the organization included president of clinical operations and chief medical officer for HCA Healthcare, and the U.S. Department of Veteran's Affairs' under secretary for health.

Perlin will remain a strategic advisor to the group following his retirement, holding the title of president emeritus.

Merlino's career included leadership roles at Cleveland Clinic such as chief clinical transformation officer and chief experience officer, as well as at healthcare performance improvement company Press Ganey.

Recent findings suggest that > Robert C. Garrett, CEO of Hackensack Meridian Health, will retire next year after decades with the organization, including its formative 2016 merger.

Garrett is set to step down on June 30, upon which time he'll hold the role of CEO emeritus for a year to help ease the transition. The 18-hospital, nearly $10 billion nonprofit noted it plans to announce his successor before the year's end.

Garrett began his career in the early 1980s at Hackensack University Medical Center, and in 2009 was named president and CEO of Hackensack University Health Network. When the organization merged with Meridian Health in 2016 to form Latest Jersey's largest health system, he served as co-CEO for two years before taking on the solo mantle.

Alongside the organization's growth to more than 500 patient care locations, Garrett's tenure also marked the opening of the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine, New Jersey's first new medical school in decades.

"Bob has been the driving force behind HMH's unprecedented growth and transformation, its superior quality, innovation and commitment to building an exceptional workforce," Board Chair Keith Banks said in a statement. "At the heart of Bob's legacy is his unwavering belief that we must deliver the most innovative and compassionate care to all patients. HMH is solidly positioned for continued growth, and we are profoundly grateful to Bob and extend our warmest wishes to him for this well-deserved next chapter.".

> The Pharmaceutical Care Management Association, the leading lobbying group for the pharmacy benefit management industry, has named CVS Health executive Ed DeVaney as its board chair.

According to recent reports, deVaney currently serves as president of CVS Caremark, one of the PBM industry's "Significant Three" firms. He succeeds Adam Kautzner, president of Express Scripts and Evernorth Health Services, representing one of the other "Big Three" companies.

“The role PBMs play in lowering costs and improving access to prescription drugs for Americans is critically important,” DeVaney mentioned in the announcement. “As Board Chair, I’m committed to ensuring PCMA shares our story with policymakers, consumers and employers so they have a full understanding of the work we do to fulfill our commitment to lower drug costs.”.

> UnitedHealth Group has elevated Dan Kueter to serve as the firm's chief commercial officer, per a LinkedIn post.

According to recent reports, kueter previously served as the CEO of UnitedHealthcare's commercial business for four years. UHC is the health insurance arm of UnitedHealth Group.

In the new role, Kueter will be tasked with working across both UnitedHealthcare and Optum to support coordination in product development and innovation, he wrote in the post. He remarked he will also collaborate closely with other senior leaders at the UnitedHealth Group level.

"I'm looking forward to working across the tech giant with colleagues at Optum and UnitedHealthcare to help drive our next chapter of growth and innovation, focused on helping make healthcare work better for everyone," Kueter wrote.

According to recent reports, in a separate post, Brandon Cuevas revealed that he will succeed Kueter as CEO of UHC's commercial unit. Cuevas most recently served as executive vice president for the national health strategy at Kaiser Permanente, and he previously held multiple leadership roles during a 14-year stint at UnitedHealthcare.

Cuevas remarked in the post that he "couldn’t be more excited to rejoin a team that is so capable and committed to making positive change in healthcare.".

> Optum has named Ujjwal Ratan as the new chief AI officer for its Optum Insight unit, per a LinkedIn post.

In the role, he will be tasked with leading the development of the critical infrastructure that Optum Insight will build its agentic AI toolset on. Ratan has previously held leadership roles at Amazon Web Services and at Oracle, according to his profile.

In a recent development, "Agentic AI only works if the agents have real, connected data to reason over — and few organizations sit across as much of the healthcare journey as Optum does: providers, payers, pharmacy, life sciences and government programs, under one roof," Ratan wrote. "That's exactly the foundation this next wave of AI needs, and exactly why I think Optum is positioned to set the standard for agentic AI across healthcare, not just inside it.".

In a recent development, > Association of American Medical Colleges President and CEO David J. Skorton, M.D., will retire from his post on June 30, 2027, the group confirmed this week. A search for his replacement is at the moment under way.

In a recent development, skorton stepped into the role in July 2019 and was kept on by the board in a unanimous 2023 vote. He's credited with guiding the association through the pandemic and overseeing a comprehensive strategic planning process that brought a new vision and mission. Prior to joining he served as secretary of the Smithsonian Institution and was president of Cornell University and the University of Iowa.

“He will be leaving the AAMC an even stronger association than when he arrived," Board Chair Michael Waldrum, M.D., noted in a statement. "Identifying a visionary leader to guide the association and the academic medicine community into the future will be our next challenge.”.

> Cotiviti, a healthcare infrastructure and data analytics platform, has appointed Erin Schmuker as its chief operating officer.

It has been revealed that she enters the role with over 20 years of healthcare leadership, coming directly from a job as president of integrated pharmacies at OptumRx. The new position tasks Schumuker with scaling Cotiviti's operating model, bolstering execution and accountability, simplifying operations and bolstering its growth.

Recent findings suggest that “Our opportunity is to connect data and intelligence to the workflows where decisions are actually made and turn that intelligence into action at scale," President and CEO Ric Sinclair mentioned of the appointment. "Erin is a proven operator who understands how to do that. She knows healthcare, she knows our clients and she knows how to bring people, technology and operations together to deliver results. She will help us move faster, operate better and scale Cotiviti for what healthcare needs next.”.

> Kaiser Permanente recently confirmed that Shaun Smith will be joining as executive vice president and chief people officer, effective Oct. 12.

Smith, who will be reporting directly to the CEO as well as to the president of integrated care and coverage, comes from a chief people and culture officer roles at NewYork-Presbyterian.

> The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association (BCBSA) has named Dan Serrano senior vice president and chief financial officer to oversee the organization’s enterprise financial strategy.

Serrano joins BCBSA after holding leadership roles across the health insurance, provider and value-based care sectors. His experience includes serving as chief financial officer for Aetna's Mid-Atlantic Region and holding senior finance positions at ChenMed, Healthfirst, as well as several other home-based and primary care organizations. He also served as vice president of value and risk-based contracting at Mount Sinai Health System.

“Dan's extensive experience across the healthcare ecosystem, combined with a strong track record of aligning financial performance to operational outcomes, makes him a tremendous addition to our leadership team,” said BCBSA president and CEO Kim Keck in a statement.

>Keck Medicine of USC announced that CEO Rodney Hanners will be stepping down on Sept. 24, alongside a handful of other leadership changes at the system and its affiliated Keck School of Medicine of USC.

Hanners was in the role for six years, a period in which he extended the Los Angeles-based organization's reach into Pasadena and the San Gabriel Valley.

Taking over for him will be Steven Shapiro, M.D., currently senior vice president for health affairs, who joined in 2021 from a run as president of the University of Pittsburg Medical Center.

The university noted that it will be trimming the role's responsibilities, reverting supervision of some USC health science schools to the provost "to allow Steve to focus more intensely on elevating our academic medical enterprise.".

Industry observers note that beneath him, the university has also named Chief Clinical Officer David Peng, M.D., as deputy executive vice president for health affairs and Keck Medical Center of USC CEO Marty Sargeant as chief operating officer of the broader system. Both Peng and Sargeant will remain in their prior roles alongside the new responsibilities.

Recent findings suggest that USC's announcement also included word that Keck School of Medicine of USC Dean Carolyn Meltzer is stepping down for a newly introduced role as president of the Radiological Society of North America. Vassilios Papadopoulos, dean of the university's pharmaceutical school, will be filling her role on an interim basis.

>Health tech manufacturer Health Catalyst appointed Simeon Kohl as Chief Executive Officer and President and a member of the company’s Board of Directors, effective September 14.

Kohl most recently served as CEO of Performant Healthcare, a public healthcare company he led through significant strategic and operational transformation, culminating in its sale to Machinify for approximately $670 million. He brings more than 20 years in healthcare, spanning operations, growth and public company leadership. The company’s current CEO and President, Ben Albert, will become Chief Business Officer and will step down from the Board of Directors effective September 13.

During his tenure, Albert led Health Catalyst's strategic priorities and operating initiatives and aligned the leadership team now running the business. He sharpened the company’s focus on its highest-conviction technologies, positioning Health Catalyst as an AI-forward healthcare intelligence company, executives mentioned. To support that focus, he led the divestiture of Vitalware, which enabled the company to retire its approximately $160 million credit facility and strengthen its balance sheet.

> The American Medical Association tapped Jennifer Goldsack as senior vice president and inaugural leader of the AMA Center for Digital Health and AI. Goldsack joins the AMA from the Digital Medicine Society (DiMe), a global non-profit organization dedicated to advancing digital medicine to optimize health, where she was both founder and CEO.

A leading voice on the responsible adoption of digital health and AI in healthcare, Goldsack has a record of bringing together evidence, clinical practice, technology and policy to help ensure digital innovations are safe, effective, equitable and capable of delivering meaningful value for patients and physicians, according to the AMA.

"We are at a defining moment for medicine. Digital health and augmented intelligence are rapidly and fundamentally changing how and where care is delivered. For these tools to reach their full potential and be effective for patients, physicians must lead the way in developing and implementing them. Jennifer is the right leader for this moment because she knows how to bring physicians and innovators together and translate that collaboration into real-world impact on patient care," AMA CEO John Whyte, M.D., said.

Sources indicate that “Reimagining how we care for people in the digital era has been the focus of my career, and we are at an extraordinary moment of opportunity,” Goldsack remarked in a statement. “We have powerful upcoming tools at our disposal and a responsibility to make sure we harness them to improve people’s lives. I’m thrilled to join the AMA and work alongside physicians and partners across healthcare. We’re going to set a high bar for what better healthcare looks like in the digital and AI era. And together, we will make it happen.”.

Since its launch last year, the AMA Center for Digital Health and AI has produced key research, including: a survey of AI usage among physicians, showing growing confidence in the technology’s clinical advantages; and an international survey on wearables.

>Teladoc Health appointed Michael Grasher as its newly introduced chief financial officer.

Industry observers note that grasher has more than three decades of experience across the insurance and financial services industries, most recently serving as CFO of property-casualty insurance tech giant IFG Companies, according to an Aug. 31 press release.

"Teladoc Health has built a strong foundation with unmatched scale, deep clinical expertise and a global footprint," said Grasher. "I'm excited to work with Chuck [Divita] and the leadership team to build on that foundation and deliver lasting value for the members, clients and shareholders we serve.".

>Johns Hopkins Health Initiative has named Daniel Chojnowski as its interim CEO.

Industry observers note that chojnowski has served as the insurer's chief financial officer for the past seven years, according to a post from JHHP on LinkedIn. Former JHHP CEO James Holland departed the organization in mid-August to become president of Medicaid for Humana.

JHHP said in the LinkedIn posted that Chojnowski will "provide stability and trusted guidance" while it conducts a search for a permanent CEO.

"Dan believes in leading with courage and compassion," per the post. "He embodies the modern CFO, which has evolved from the number-crunching budget guard to a strategic partner, helping to steer organizational decisions.".

>Wilmington, Delaware-based ChristianaCare welcomed Jenn Schwartz as its upcoming president and CEO on Sept. 1.

The newly introduced top exec came to came to ChristianaCare in 2018 to initially serve as chief legal officer, having previously spent over a decade at Lourdes Health System where she was vice president of legal affairs and general counsel as well as its executive director. She'd already been named as executive vice president and chief strategy officer earlier this year.

Schwartz is taking over for Janice Nevin, M.D., who revealed earlier this year she'd be retiring after about 23 years at the nonprofit system. She'd held the top roles for a dozen years.

ChristianaCare is a nonprofit teaching health system with three hospitals hosting 1,430 beds as well as a network of primary care and outpatient services.

In a recent development, janice Nevin, M.D., will end her 12-year run as president and CEO of ChristianaCare on Sept. 1, the system's board revealed.

According to recent reports, she retires after 23 years at the organization, initially joining as its chair of family and community medicine. The physician executive is credited by the board with expanding the system's physical footprint, shepherding "significant investment in historically under-resourced areas" and strengthening its academic partnerships.

Taking up the mantle will be Jenn Schwartz, who was named executive vice president and chief strategy officer at the top of 2026. She came to ChristianaCare in 2018 to initially serve as chief legal officer. Prior to that she spent over a decade at Lourdes Health System, where she was vice president of legal affairs & general counsel as well as its executive director.

According to recent reports, >Insurer Centene has named Bradley Bolivar as its fresh chief information officer, with the new role taking effect on Aug. 31.

According to recent reports, bolivar succeeds Brian LeClare, who is set to retire in October. He previously served as CIO at Fannie Mae, where he led strategy around technological development, infrastructure, cybersecurity and more. Bolivar brings more than three decades of technology leadership experience to the role at Centene, according to an announcement from the company.

"We are entering a latest era where data, technology and AI are not just business enablers, but strategic capabilities that shape how we operate, innovate and create value," CEO Sarah London said in the announcement. "Brad's proven ability to solve complex technology challenges will position Centene to deliver simpler, better health experiences and improved outcomes for the nation's most underserved populations.".

>Elevance Health has named Patrick Fox, M.D., as president of Carelon Behavioral Health.

Sources indicate that fox's background includes more than three decades of experience in clinical psychiatry, behavioral health, public health and health strategy leadership, the tech giant said in an announcement. He most recently served as president Elevance-affiliated plan Wellpoint Latest Jersey.

Fox also previously helmed the company's Colorado Medicaid blueprint, per the announcement. Fox's upcoming title is effective immediately.

Recent findings suggest that "Patrick brings a rare combination of experience as a practicing psychiatrist, behavioral health leader and health plan executive,” remarked Kristy Duffey, president of Carelon Health, in the announcement. “He understands the challenges facing behavioral healthcare from the clinical, operational and system perspectives.".

"That breadth of experience will be invaluable as we work to improve access, strengthen connections across the healthcare system and deliver better outcomes for the people we serve," said Duffey.

Patrick Gillespie, regional vice president for state affairs at Elevance Health, has been named as Fox's successor as Wellpoint New Jersey president, the firm said.

>Providence St. Joseph Health has named a fresh chief financial officer.

It has been revealed that kevin Smith will take the CFO seat on Oct. 26, according to an announcement from the health system. As CFO, he'll oversee Providence's "inancial strategy, planning, capital allocation and operational performance," the system noted.

Smith will join Providence from SSM Health, where he right now serves as CFO. He's also held leadership roles in finance at Luminis Health, Lehigh Valley Health Network, Universal Health Services and the University of Pennsylvania Health System.

It has been revealed that “Kevin is a highly respected healthcare finance leader with a strong track record of improving performance, guiding complex organizations and positioning health systems for long-term success,” said Erik Wexler, CEO of Providence, in the announcement. “His experience, judgment and commitment to Mission-driven stewardship will be invaluable as we continue strengthening Providence for the future.”.

>Accolade executive Shantanu Nundy will join Humana as its upcoming chief medical officer.

It has been revealed that nundy, M.D., currently serves as executive vice president of care delivery and chief health officer at Accolade, a healthcare navigation and care delivery organization. He'll step into the role at Humana on Aug. 31, according to an announcement from the company.

Recent findings suggest that nundy also held leadership roles at Evolent Health, and has provided council to a number of organizations on digital health and AI, including the Food and Drug Administration and World Bank. He continues to practice medicine, including primary care a community health center and hospital-based medicine through a local health system.

Nundy will report to Humana CEO Jim Rechtin as part of the enterprise leadership team.

Recent findings suggest that "Clinical excellence is at the heart of Humana’s vision to be a leading consumer healthcare firm, and I am thrilled to welcome Dr. Nundy as our newly introduced chief medical officer," Rechtin remarked in the announcement. "I am confident Shantanu’s experience at the intersection of clinical outcomes, technology and the consumer experience will advance our efforts to simplify the path to care and help the people we serve achieve their best health.".

Industry observers note that >St. Jude Children's Research Hospital has named Charles W.M. Roberts, M.D., Ph.D., as its next president and CEO, effective Jan. 1, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that he right now serves as director of the St. Jude Comprehensive Cancer Center, having joined the organization in 2015 to fill the post. The pediatric hematologist/oncologist has headed the center's five research programs, pushed the center to its best scores in National Cancer Institute rankings and has his own body of medical research that has paved the way to FDA-approved and investigational cancer therapies.

His appointment follows the February announcement from St. Jude that its current leader, James R. Downing, M.D., planned to step down. The organization said it conducted "an extensive international search" before selecting a successor from within.

>CVS Health has announced changes to its board of directors, including the addition of JPMorgan Chase executive Teresa Heitsenrether.

According to recent reports, heitsenrether brings nearly forty years of experience in financial leadership to the board, and currently serves as the chief data and analytics officer at JPMorgan. She will join CVS' board on Nov. 18.

“Teresa’s extensive experience leading complex global businesses and driving technology-enabled transformation will be invaluable as CVS Health continues to innovate on its path to become a consumer focused, health technology company,” CVS CEO David Joyner remarked in the announcement.

In a recent development, in addition, Larry Robbins has departed CVS' board as of Aug. 13. Robbins has served on the board since 2024, with roles on its Audit and Public Policy and External Affairs Committees.

Robbins is the CEO of Glenview Capital Management.

>Drew Asher, chief financial officer at Centene, will step down from the position in December, the manufacturer revealed on Monday.

Recent findings suggest that asher intends to retire from Centene at the end of 2027, per the announcement. He will take the year between stepping down as CFO and retirement to support the transition and ongoing strategic priorities.

It has been revealed that chris Neczypor has been tapped as Asher's successor and will join the company in September, according to the release. Neczypor is a veteran executive who most recently served as CFO at Lincoln Financial, which provides life insurance, annuities and retirement solutions.

According to recent reports, he had multiple leadership roles at Lincoln after joining the company in 2018, Centene said. Neczypor spent more than a decade in financial services prior to Lincoln, including a stint as an equity research analyst at Goldman Sachs.

Recent findings suggest that "Chris brings a proven track record of strengthening financial performance, optimizing operations and creating long-term shareholder value," Centene CEO Sarah London mentioned in the announcement. "Just as importantly, he is a collaborative, values-driven leader who understands how to build strong teams and drive meaningful impact.".

"Our organization will benefit from his expertise, energy and perspective as we deliver on Centene's next phase of transformation and growth," London remarked.

Asher has served as CFO at Centene since 2021.

>Humana has named a latest executive to lead its growing Medicaid business.

The insurer said Monday that James Holland will join the company as senior vice president and president of Medicaid effective Aug. 17. In the role, he will oversee plans that cover 1.6 million people across 11 states, according to an announcement.

Recent findings suggest that holland most recently helmed Johns Hopkins Health Plans, overseeing Medicaid, Medicare and other government plans. He has also held leadership roles at Elevance Health, Amerigroup and WellCare Health Plans.

Holland will report to Aaron Martin, president of insurance at Humana.

It has been revealed that “Medicaid is an important part of how we deliver on Humana’s purpose, helping some of the most vulnerable populations access the care and support they need to achieve their best health,” Martin mentioned in the announcement. “J.P. brings deep expertise leading government-sponsored healthcare looks and maintaining strong relationships with state and provider partners.".

"His experiences and insights will be invaluable as we continue to grow our Medicaid business and better serve our Medicaid members," Martin said.

>Amid the health system's financial strengthening project, Tufts Medicine CEO and CFO have transitioned away from the company.

Sources indicate that the current CEO, Mike Dandorph, will step down on September 30, which is also the conclusion of the 2026 fiscal year. He will continue to work towards a transition that ensures Tufts Medicine continues its upward trajectory.

Phil Okala, the COO of Tufts Medicine, will serve as Acting President and CEO. Phil has held multiple leadership roles at Tufts Medicine, and other health systems, including Penn Medicine. With the Board’s full support, he hopes to “focus on guiding Tufts Medicine to greater clinical, operational and financial success.”.

Andrew DeVoe, the current Executive Vice President and CFO, has also decided to depart Tufts Medicine, after playing an notable role in improving the organization's performance. Soon, Tufts Medicine expects to begin a nationwide search for his replacement. As for right now, Greg Kruse, Tufts’ Vice President of Strategic Operations and Analytics Intelligence, will assume responsibility for future budget planning.

Industry observers note that dandorph stated “Serving as President and CEO of Tufts Medicine and working closely with such extraordinary people has been a distinct privilege these past six and a half years. I am proud of what we have accomplished together and am grateful to the amazing physicians, nurses, researchers, learners, staff and leaders whose commitment to our mission has inspired me every day. I believe this transition is in the best interest and right time for Tufts Medicine. In the coming months, I will work closely with Phil Okala to ensure a thoughtful and orderly transition that best positions the organization for its next chapter and future success.”.

Recent findings suggest that >Summa Health revealed on August 3 that Jennifer Eslinger will join as the health system's new President and CEO beginning on September 21. She will succeed Daryl Tol, the current Acting CEO, who has led the organization following its acquisition by Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo).

Eslinger brings more than two decades of leadership experience; most recently serving as President and COO of Rochester Regional Health. At Rochester Regional Health, she led the $4.2 billion health system through significant transformation and strategic growth.

According to recent reports, "Jennifer is an accomplished healthcare leader with deep experience driving operational and clinical excellence, embracing innovation and creating a culture of curiosity and continuous improvement,” said Kate Walsh, Chair of Summa Health’s Board of Directors. “She has both the judgment and values to build on Summa Health's strong foundation while accelerating our impact in the communities we serve and helping shape the future of healthcare.”.

>Jaewon Ryu, the chief executive officer of Risant Health at Kaiser Permanente, has decided to step down from the role to focus on his family. Dale Maxwell, former president and CEO of Presbyterian Healthcare Services, will serve as interim CEO during the national search by the board.

It has been revealed that "Jaewon has been instrumental in turning the vision for Risant Health into reality," said Greg Adams, chair and chief executive officer of Kaiser Permanente and chair of the board of Risant Health. "He built an exceptional leadership team, established the organization's operating model, and positioned Risant Health to help more communities benefit from value-based care.”.

It has been revealed that ryu served as Risant Health’s inaugural CEO, establishing its operating model and recruiting the initial leadership team. Key moments in his tenure include the addition of both Geisinger and Cone Health as well as meaningful clinical and operational improvements.

The interim CEO, Dale Maxwell, brings over 24 years of executive leadership experience at Presbyterian Healthcare Services, New Mexico's largest nonprofit integrated health system.

Recent findings suggest that "This leadership transition reflects thoughtful planning, not a change in strategy," Adams noted. "Kaiser Permanente and Risant Health will continue to advance their mission to help leading community-based health systems deliver high-quality, value-based care. We are confident in the organization's leadership, its momentum, and its future.".

>Paul Smith and Frederick Crawford were elected as upcoming members of the Humana board, effective immediately.

Smith presently serves as the chief commercial officer at Anthropic, PBC, leading commercial strategy and go-to-market operations. Prior to joining Anthropic, he was chief commercial officer and president of global customer and field operations at ServiceNow and held senior leadership roles at Salesforce and Microsoft.

Crawford also brings significant experience to the Humana board, having spent more than 30 years in the insurance and banking industries. Before his retirement in 2024, Crawford was president and chief operating officer at Aflac. He also sits on the Board of Webster Financial Corporation as a member of both the Audit and Risk committees.

It has been revealed that “We are pleased to welcome Paul and Fred to the Humana Board. Paul has deep experience guiding the world’s largest enterprises in responsibly adopting technology and AI at scale along with a strong track record in product development and client service, while Fred brings broad industry experience and financial expertise focused on disciplined capital allocation and risk management,” said Humana Chairman of the Board Kurt J. Hilzinger.

>Centene confirmed that Kenneth A. Burdick has retired from the company's board of directors, effective July 28, and that Paul J. Diaz has been appointed to the board, effective immediately.

In a recent development, burdick joined the Centene board of directors in January 2022, offering insight that drew upon his long-standing leadership in healthcare. He served as executive vice president of products and markets at Centene and before that was the chief executive officer of WellCare Health Aims.

Industry observers note that diaz is currently a managing partner at Cressey & Organization, a private investment firm focused on cultivating high-quality healthcare firms. Before joining Cressey, he was president and CEO of Myriad Genetics Inc., as well as CEO of Kindred Healthcare. He has also served on the board of healthcare organizations, such as DaVita and PharMerica.

Industry observers note that "Ken has been a valued member of our Board. His deep industry expertise, strategic perspective, and commitment to improving healthcare have made a meaningful impact on Centene. On behalf of the Board, we thank him for his service and wish him all the best in retirement," noted Frederick H. Eppinger, Chair of Centene's Board of Directors. "We are also pleased to welcome Paul Diaz to the Board. His extensive healthcare leadership experience, public tech giant governance expertise and record of guiding organizations through growth and transformation will bring valuable perspective as Centene continues to advance its strategy and serve its members.".

In a recent development, >Siemens Healthineers announced on July 30 that João Seabra will succeed John Kowal as president and head of the Americas for Siemens Healthineers, effective Oct. 1, 2026. He is presently the head of Siemens Healthineers Enterprise Services.

Recent findings suggest that seabra joined Healthineers in 2001, and from 2015 to 2018, he led the Western Europe and West Africa regions. In his most recent role as head of enterprise services, he quadrupled its revenue over the last eight years.

Recent findings suggest that “We would like to thank John for his many years of successful service and outstanding commitment to Siemens Healthineers, first within our Varian business and later as President and Head of our Americas business. We are very pleased to appoint João Seabra as our newly introduced President and Head of the Americas. Under his leadership and thanks to his innovative thinking, Siemens Healthineers paved the way in our industry by creating Value Partnerships of increasing scope and impact with key customers,” said Darleen Caron, Member of the Managing Board at Siemens Healthineers with responsibility for the Americas and Chief Human Resources Officer.

>PayZen, an AI-driven patient affordability platform, has declared that Jingwei Wu will serve as senior vice president of engineering.

Recent findings suggest that prior to joining PayZen, Wu led the engineering team behind the LinkedIn Jobs Marketplace, expanding it to reach millions more job searchers. He’s also been part of engineering leadership teams at both Twitter and Tinder.

In his latest role at PayZen, Wu will lead the firm’s engineering organization, overseeing platform architecture, AI infrastructure and product engineering.

“Healthcare affordability is one of the biggest challenges facing patients and providers today, and PayZen is proving that AI can fundamentally improve how people access and pay for care,” Wu stated.

>Sarah Bast was appointed as the chief marketing officer of OptimizeRx, a healthcare technology solutions provider.

She brings over two decades of experience from companies including Publicis Health Media, Lilly, Bayer, Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca. In these roles, she developed significant expertise in point of care media strategy, which she will bring to her role at OptimizeRX.

As CMO, Bast will lead Optimize Rx’s marketing strategy and continue strengthening the firm's relationships with healthcare marketing agencies.

"Sarah's decision to join OptimizeRx speaks to both the strength of the business we've built and the tremendous opportunity ahead," said Steve Silvestro, Chief Executive Officer, OptimizeRx. "She has spent her career helping life sciences brands solve complex marketing challenges and understands firsthand how healthcare marketers can reach providers more effectively. As OptimizeRx enters its next phase of growth, her strategic vision and deep understanding of the market will help us strengthen our customer relationships and accelerate the development of solutions that improve healthcare engagement.".

According to recent reports, >Matt Swafford has been named executive vice president and chief financial officer of Peace Health, succeeding Ric Magnuson, the current interim CFO. He will join the firm on September 21 from St. Charles Health System, where he currently serves as CFO and senior VP of strategy and finance.

Swafford brings over 35 years of experience in nonprofit health system finance, helping health systems navigate change and invest in patients.

It has been revealed that sarah Ness, PeaceHealth president and chief executive officer, mentioned, “We are creating a stronger PeaceHealth, one that is easier for patients to navigate, better connected for caregivers and positioned to meet the needs of our communities well into the future. Matt has shared with me that he sees every financial decision through that human lens, which makes him a strong fit for our Mission and our commitment to put people first.”.

Industry observers note that >Hannah Alphs Jackson, M.D. will join Availity, the nation’s largest real-time health information network, as the tech giant's first chief medical officer.

Availity remarked in a statement that it created the CMO role “to ensure clinical expertise is injected throughout the organization's strategy, innovation, and customer solutions.” This is significant as the healthcare industry and Availity continues to become dependent on automation and AI, executives said.

Before joining Availity, Alphs Jackson held roles in physician and payer leadership, where she integrated value-based care models with clinical operations. In her new role as CMO, she will guide the responsible usage of emerging technologies, as part of Availity’s clinical strategy.

It has been revealed that “Dr. Jackson brings a rare combination of clinical expertise, provider perspective, payer experience and strategic vision,” mentioned Russ Thomas, CEO of Availity, in a statement. “As healthcare continues to evolve, it's critical that we have strong clinical leadership guiding how we integrate automation and AI capabilities to support the entire healthcare system – and ultimately improve the entire experience.”.

>Clinical AI assistant startup Nabla revealed the appointment of Brian Manning as its new CEO to lead the tech giant's next phase of growth.

Manning joins Nabla from Bamboo Health, where he served as president and chief revenue officer and helped scale the organization to more than $140 million in revenue. He also assisted in the growth and development of PatientPing and Zocdoc.

As Nabla continues to expand, supporting more than 190 healthcare organizations and 100,000 clinicians, Manning will spearhead the manufacturer’s scaling efforts. His more than 20 years of experience accelerating growth will ensure that Nabla continues to be adopted across the healthcare industry, executives stated in a press release.

According to recent reports, "Healthcare organizations are looking for partners that can deliver real value today while helping them prepare for the future of AI. Nabla has built an exceptional foundation and has earned the trust of clinicians and healthcare organizations. The opportunity now is to accelerate that momentum, expand our reach, and further establish Nabla as the clinical AI partner of choice for healthcare organizations across the world,” noted Manning.

>Aptarro, a manufacturer that provides healthcare revenue cycle management software solutions, hired Paul Wiley as chief growth officer.

Recent findings suggest that wiley’s appointment comes at a significant time for Aptarro as the company continue to scale its engine for denial prevention and reimbursement intelligence. Wiley has more than two decades of executive leadership experience spanning healthcare technology, enterprise software, AI and travel technology, according to the company, and he has been tapped to steer the company through its current commercial growth.

Most recently, he served as chief commercial officer at Avodah, and prior to that, he founded Opargo, an AI-powered healthcare scheduling manufacturer. His experience will ensure that Aptarro continues to effectively address the persistent and costly problem of denials, executives mentioned.

"As reimbursement continues to grow more dynamic, healthcare organizations need technology that evolves alongside it. We're building the leadership team to support that mission," mentioned Jeff Diamond, Aptarro CEO. "Paul's experience will be instrumental as we continue expanding our platform and defining the future of reimbursement intelligence.".

>The Pharmaceutical Care Management Association (PCMA) added two senior public affairs leaders to its team. Mackay Jimeson will join PCMA as Vice President of Coalitions, and Christine Rex will join as Senior Director of State Communications.

It has been revealed that jimeson joins PCMA from Patients Rising, where he was served as Executive Director, expanding the organization’s national influence and strengthening its role in health care policy. In his fresh role at PCMA, he will lead PCMA’s coalition strategy and third-party partnership engagement efforts.

Rex will oversee state campaigns and coalition communications, while working closely with PCMA's member companies.

“Bringing this level of talent reflects PCMA’s commitment to strategically meeting the needs of this moment,” said David Marin, President and CEO of PCMA. “The pharmacy benefit manager industry has been transformed and is more responsive than ever, and we are entering a latest era of advocacy at PCMA. MacKay will use his unique experience advocating for patients to strengthen our coalition partnerships and build broader alliances for the industry and the 289 million patients we serve. Christine is a battle-tested communicator who expertly navigates state legislative debates. Our team is deeper and more dynamic having them at PCMA.”.

>Vanderbilt Health has chosen David C. Miller as the successor to Jeff Balser as President and CEO and Dean of Vanderbilt University School of Medicine.

Recent findings suggest that miller is presently serving as Chief Executive Officer of Michigan Medicine and Executive Vice President for Medical Affairs for the University of Michigan and will assume the role at Vanderbilt on January 1, 2027. Earlie this year, Balser announced looks to retire on December 31, after serving Vanderbilt in leadership roles for nearly two decades.

Miller’s experience at the similarly sized Michigan Health uniquely prepares him to become Vanderbilt Health’s newly introduced leader, the health system mentioned. Miller’s selection as the new senior leader for Vanderbilt Health and Vanderbilt University School of Medicine finalizes an extensive national search by the VH Board of Directors to identify Balser’s successor.

As Chief Executive Officer, Miller will be responsible for shaping the future strategic direction of Vanderbilt Health and maintaining the scholarly activities shared by the Medical Center and University.

“From an incredibly strong field of applicants, Dr. Miller’s personal warmth, prior leadership experiences, and commitment to organizational culture stood out. David has presented an exciting vision for advancing the Medical Center’s missions and is the ideal candidate to succeed Dr. Balser. We look forward to welcoming David, his wife, Inge, and family to the Nashville community,” noted Edie Carell Johnson, Chair of the VH Board of Directors.

>Aledade appointed Darren Thayne as chief technology officer and hired Josh C. Mandel, M.D. as chief scientist. Thayne and Mandel will bring deep expertise in enterprise scale and open data standards to the manufacturer, Aledade remarked.

Leveraging their combined experience, Aledade will further integrate advanced AI into its platform.

In a recent development, thayne joins Aledade from Domo, where he spent 15 years leading its technology team, as founding technology leader, chief technology officer and executive vice president of product. He was responsible for breakthrough technology and deployment of AI-based tools that were central to customer experience.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Mandel, who is both a physician and software engineer, joins Aledade from Microsoft research, where he helped build open standards such as FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources). His work will focus on external interoperability and data exchange efforts, as well as AI strategy.

“AI raises the stakes on that alignment. Deployed inside fee-for-service, it accelerates billing. Deployed inside our value-based care model, it accelerates health. Daren and Josh have built infrastructure and open standards at national scale, and they're joining us to make sure that the value created by AI in healthcare flows to patients and practices,” said Farzad Mostashari, M.D., co-founder and CEO of Aledade.

>Rad AI declared that Leonard Law will join the tech giant as Chief Product Officer. Law's hiring comes at a pivotal moment for the radiology reporting market, as health systems and radiology practices shift from legacy reporting software to AI-native radiology workflow platforms, the company remarked.

It has been revealed that law joins Rad AI from Primer, an enterprise AI platform, where he served as chief product officer. Previously, he was head of product at Coinbase and he also spent nearly a decade at Google Cloud and YouTube.

According to recent reports, his appointment builds on other recent executive additions and rolls out, including Rad AI's next-generation speech recognition technology and appointment of David Leonard as COO. Law will work closely with Jeff Chang, M.D., co-founder and president of Rad AI, to build on the company’s radiologist-led product foundation and help scale the next generation of AI-native workflow solutions.

>Laura Kaiser, the president and CEO of SSM Health, has been elected by the American Hospital Association (AHA) Board of Trustees as its chair-elect designate. She will serve as chair-elect in 2027, eventually becoming chair of AHA and the top elected official of the national organization that represents America’s hospitals.

Industry observers note that since 2017, Kaiser has been a crucial part of SSM Health, which serves serves millions of patients across Missouri, Illinois, Wisconsin and Oklahoma. As part of her work with SSM Health, she transformed the health system's telehealth capabilities and announced a partnership with Siemens Healthineers to expand access to care and train healthcare workers.

According to recent reports, she also serves on several other boards, including Greater St. Louis Inc., Merit Medical and Navitus Health Solutions.

“I look forward to the opportunity to serve, continuing to advocate for America's hospitals and health systems to advance solutions that work for everyone. The AHA's vision of a society of healthy communities, where every person has the potential to live a healthy life, is one I have pursued throughout my career,” Kaiser said in the announcement.

>Ted Holden was named as the Vice President of Client Success for Collective Health, an independent third-party administrator that combines administration, cost management and care.

It has been revealed that prior to this appointment, he served as Head of Strategic Partnerships and Network Strategy at Noom and Chief Growth Officer at Catapult Health. During his early career, he spent over 20 years at BlueCross BlueShield of Texas.

Holden will lead a team delivering a stellar experience to Collective Health’s self-funded employer clients, drawing on his relationships across the healthcare industry and his robust experience, the manufacturer said.

“I’ve spent my career on the carrier side, the digital health side, and everywhere in between, and what Collective Health has built is genuinely different,” Holden stated in a statement. “One unified foundation that brings together administration, cost management, and care navigation, with incentives aligned with employers. I’m excited to help our clients understand what’s possible and make sure they’re getting every ounce of value from it.”.

Industry observers note that >Brian S. Kim, M.D. has been named the first vice president and chief biotechnology officer at Northwell Health, as well as head of intellectual asset management at the Feinstein Institutes. He will also join the department of dermatology as a professor at Northwell Health.

According to recent reports, the Feinstein Institutes is home to Northwell Health’s research center, and it serves as the largest health care provider and private employer in Latest York State. Kim joins Feinstein from the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, bringing his expertise in dermatology, medical research and biotechnology.

His work has led to significant clinical advances, including the design of pivotal clinical trials that resulted in two first-in-class U.S. Food and Drug Administration-approved treatments for atopic dermatitis and prurigo nodularis. He has founded three biotech companies, including Alys Pharmaceuticals, and authored over 190 peer-reviewed publications.

Kim will continue to advance Feinstein Institute’s groundbreaking research on electric stimulation to treat disease, including work on nerve stimulation implants that could potentially treat Crohn’s disease and other inflammatory conditions.

“Dr. Kim’s appointment reflects our commitment to transforming bold research into better outcomes for our patients,” said John D’Angelo, M.D., Northwell’s president and CEO. “With his leadership, we can better translate breakthrough science and pioneer the future of medicine while staying grounded in our mission to produce knowledge to cure disease.”.

Industry observers note that >Anita Girard, R.N., of the American Nurses Association\California, was elected by representatives of the American Nurses Association (ANA) as the new president representing the interests of more than 5 million nurses. Her two-year term of service will begin on January 1, 2027.

According to recent reports, girard, a Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP), will lead ANA’s implementation of the organization's 2026-2030 strategic plan, and its Board of Directors. She presently serves as vice president of the American Nurses Association and most recently served as the president of the American Nurses Association\California. Prior to leading these associations, she was chief nursing officer and VP of nursing at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, California.

Sources indicate that “I am deeply honored to be elected to serve as the next president of the American Nurses Association and to help lead this organization into its next chapter,” Girard mentioned in a statement. “For more than 30 years, I have served this profession across clinical, operational, executive, and association leadership roles, and that experience has reinforced one enduring belief: nurses must be supported, respected, and empowered in every setting where they are educated and practice.”.

>The University of Oklahoma’s academic health system (OU Health) has named Jonathan W. Curtright as the new president and CEO, effective July 1, 2026. Richard P. Lofgren, M.D., OU Health’s inaugural president and CEO, revealed his retirement earlier this year and Curtright will be his replacement.

Curtright has been chief operating officer of OU Health since August 22, and under his leadership, the system saw an annual revenue increase from $1.9 billion to a projected $3.7 billion in fiscal year 2026. Admissions also increased 22.3% percent and outpatient clinic visits statewide reached more than 1 million, reflecting higher patient volumes and service intensity as opposed to acquisitions.

He was also responsible for program expansions, including investments in pediatric health, cancer centers and neonatal intensive care.

According to recent reports, OU Health board of directors Chair G. Rainey Williams Jr. said, “Jonathan has been instrumental in helping advance OU Health’s mission and strategic vision during a period of extraordinary growth. He understands the unique responsibilities of an academic health system and has demonstrated the leadership, operational expertise and long-term vision needed to guide OU Health into its next chapter. The board is confident in his ability to build upon the strong foundation established under Dr. Lofgren’s leadership.”.

>Christopher O’Connor, the CEO of Yale Upcoming Haven Health System (YNHHS), will be leaving after 14 years with the organization.

He will serve as a special advisor to the chair of the Board of Trustees during the transition, and the board will also be conducting a CEO search over the next months. Pamela Sutton-Wallace, the current president of YNHHS, will serve as acting CEO, effective immediately.

Recent findings suggest that O’Connor joined YNHHS after leading the acquisition of the Hospital of Saint Raphael, and during his time with Yale, he oversaw multiple hospital integrations and strategic collaboration with Yale Medicine. YNHHS has been well positioned by O’Connor to open the Adams Neurosciences Center in 2027, which is the largest strategic project in the history of the academic health system, according to the release.

Sources indicate that “We are extremely grateful to Chris for his commitment to the System and many years of service,” said Mary Farrell, chair of the YNHHS Board of Trustees. “He has worked tirelessly to serve our patients and communities during the pandemic with exemplary care and results, and leaves YNHHS in a strong and successful position as we continue to offer the very best care to every one of our patients.”.

Sources indicate that >The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) revealed that their president, David J. Cole, will retire in June 2027 after 13 years. He initially joined MUSC in 1994, and Cole will remain a professor and surgical oncologist with the system.

An extensive nationwide search for Cole’s successor will be led by former board chairman and sitting trustee James Lemon, D.M.D, and conclude next spring.

According to recent reports, during his tenure, he secured support for the construction and opening of Shawn Jenkins Children’s Hospital and Pearl Tourville Women’s Pavilion, as well as the Jean and Hugh K.
